project.name: AniSequel
project.description: Android app (Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, Material 3 Expressive) that traverses the AniList relation graph to recommend sequels, films, OVAs and spin-offs from a user's completed anime and manga, with one-tap Planning, a self-contained signed-APK updater and no Play Services.

nodes.name: DashboardViewModel.kt
nodes.summary: State holder for the dashboard: loads the viewer and their anime list, caches the relation walk behind a filter key, and applies the filter/sort pipeline off the main thread. It exists as one class because the memo fields (discoveredCandidates, discoveryKey, the detail cache, the watched-count memo, the debounce generation guard) only stay coherent while they share the ViewModel's private state.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses StateFlow for UI state and a buffered MutableSharedFlow for one-shot snackbar events; the recompute pipeline hops to Dispatchers.Default and guards publication with a generation counter.

nodes.name: DashboardViewModel
nodes.summary: The dashboard's state holder, constructed with optional preference stores so demo and public-profile dashboards can be built without persistence. Its three optional constructor parameters are the reason one class serves a signed-in dashboard, a demo dashboard and a name-scanned profile without three variants.

nodes.name: loadData
nodes.summary: Cancels any in-flight load and starts a new one, painting the disk snapshot first so a cold start shows a list instead of a spinner. Two overlapping loads used to both write _uiState and the slower one won, so cancelling the previous job is load-bearing rather than tidy.

nodes.name: onForegrounded
nodes.summary: Restarts the freshness watch on resume, joining an in-flight load rather than skipping it. Android resumes a process instead of restarting it and delivers one resume per launch, so the earlier skip meant a dashboard left open never noticed its list had aged.

nodes.name: recompute
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the visible list from the cached collection: discovers candidates once, partitions hidden from visible, applies filters and sorts on Dispatchers.Default, then publishes a Success state only if its generation token is still the newest. The generation check is what stops an older run that finished last from overwriting a newer sort.

nodes.name: requestRecompute
nodes.summary: The single entry point every filter control uses to ask for a recompute, cancelling the previous job first. Rapid taps used to launch independent runs that each wrote state in completion order, so the header could claim a sort the list was not using.

nodes.name: toggleHideSequel
nodes.summary: Hides or restores one recommendation and persists the decision, updating the in-memory set first because the preference collector is skipped entirely when no store exists (demo mode). Offers an Undo snackbar, since hiding is easy to trigger by accident and otherwise only reversible by clearing app data.

nodes.name: addToPlanning
nodes.summary: Optimistically marks a card as pending, writes to the viewer's AniList Planning list, and clears the flag again on failure so the detail sheet's spinner cannot hang. The success path re-checks the loaded list rather than trusting the local set, because AniList is authoritative for what is already planned.

nodes.name: Factory
nodes.summary: ViewModelProvider factory for the manual construction in AppNavigation. It replaces the earlier `remember { DashboardViewModel(...) }`, which tied the view model to the composition so a rotation threw it away and re-fetched the whole list.

nodes.name: InfoPage.kt
nodes.summary: The title page's scrolling Info tab: hero, synopsis, numbers, cast, crew and related titles on one page instead of the three tabs it replaced, which split the answer to "what is this show" across two screens. This file owns the page's behaviour and scroll-driven motion; the ordered section list lives elsewhere.
nodes.languageNotes: Scroll-driven values are produced with derivedStateOf and read inside graphicsLayer lambdas so a scroll does not recompose the page body.

nodes.name: AnimeInfoPage
nodes.summary: Composes the whole Info page: a LazyColumn of sections under a collapsing hero, plus the floating bar that appears once the hero is out of the way. Its list state is hoisted by the sheet because the capsule's other destination disposes this page, and a remembered state would send the reader back to the top of the page.

nodes.name: rememberThemeSongs
nodes.summary: Fetches the title's openings and endings through produceState, keyed on the media id and its artwork so walking to a related title cancels the previous fetch instead of letting it land on the new page. AnimeThemes has no per-sequence thumbnail, so the title's own banner (falling back to its cover) is used as the row's key visual.

nodes.name: rememberInfoCollapse
nodes.summary: Derives the hero's 0..1 collapse from the list's scroll offset. Keying the remember on the list state is the fix for a shipped bug: the sheet gives each title its own list state, so an unkeyed derivedStateOf kept measuring against the title the reader had just left and opened the new one with its hero already collapsed and the docked bar stacked over it.

nodes.name: rememberShowFloatingBar
nodes.summary: Turns the collapse fraction into a Boolean so the docked bar recomposes once when it crosses its threshold instead of on every frame before it. Keyed on the collapse because a new collapse must own its own threshold.

nodes.name: rememberReadProgress
nodes.summary: Share of the page the reader has passed, measured in items scrolled rather than pixels because page items differ in height by an order of magnitude. Read only inside the bar's graphicsLayer, so it animates without recomposing.

nodes.name: ApiFailureBody.kt
nodes.summary: The shared "AniList is not answering" screen: heartbreak artwork, friendly copy, a live reachability strip and the two honest exits, retry or step away. It was extracted because the dashboard and a profile page each had their own copy of the same column and said the same thing two slightly different ways.
nodes.languageNotes: The quip pool is seeded from remember(kind, message) so a line is stable while one failure is on screen but changes on retry, and rememberSaveable keeps the grass interlude across rotation.

nodes.name: ApiFailureBody
nodes.summary: Renders the failure scene, choosing broken-heart versus warning artwork by whether the failure was a dead session or an unreachable API. The artwork heals itself when a live status probe turns green while the screen is still up, so the screen stops contradicting its own status strip without pretending the load succeeded.

nodes.name: GrassInterlude
nodes.summary: The "Go touch grass" off-ramp: a calmer note with a way back, not a link out and not a close. It keeps the status strip, because leaving the screen does not make AniList wake up and hiding the check would be the one dishonest thing on the page.

nodes.name: FailureMessage
nodes.summary: The headline, explanation and joke, including the swap to the healed copy when a live check turned green during the outage. Split out because the screen's body reads better as artwork, words, strip, choices.

nodes.name: FindMissedSequelsUseCase.kt
nodes.summary: Pure domain logic that walks the AniList relation graph of a user's list and reports franchise entries they have not started. Discovery and filtering are deliberately separate functions because discovery walks every entry and edge while filtering only touches candidates, and merging them made every keystroke re-walk a whole account.
nodes.languageNotes: No Android imports; the year used by the "this year" filters is a parameter so tests do not inherit the machine's clock.

nodes.name: FindMissedSequelsUseCase
nodes.summary: The relation-graph recommender: given a media list collection and filter criteria, it produces the missed-sequel candidates, filters and sorts them, and can split the result into visible and hidden halves. It holds no state, which is what lets the ViewModel memoize its output on a collection-identity plus criteria key.

nodes.name: discover
nodes.summary: Classifies every list entry by status, then walks the relation edges of each usable parent and emits one MissedSequel per unseen relation kind match. Dedups on the fly so a sequel reachable from two parents is one gap, and can optionally build hidden entries too, because the stored hidden set is only bare ids and cannot render a title or poster.

nodes.name: applyFilters
nodes.summary: Searches, filters and sorts the candidate list, cheap enough to re-run on every keystroke. The status and format comparisons deliberately go through the model's predicates and raw AniList keys: comparing a readable label against an enum key once filtered the list to zero.

nodes.name: splitHidden
nodes.summary: Partitions a full candidate list into still-offered and hidden halves, sorting the hidden half by title because it is a settings-style list of decisions rather than a ranked feed. Partitioning instead of dropping hidden entries during discovery is what makes hide and unhide instant.

nodes.name: HiddenSplit
nodes.summary: The two halves produced by splitHidden, named so callers cannot confuse the visible feed with the hidden review list.

nodes.name: DetailActionRow.kt
nodes.summary: The action row under the title page hero: an AniList link plus whichever quick-add control is honest for that title. A title already on one of the viewer's lists gets a badge rather than an add button, because AniList mutations overwrite the entry and offering "Add to Planning" on a completed show would silently lose the watched status.
nodes.languageNotes: Kept inside the page's own scroll rather than pinned, because the sheet's bottom edge already belongs to the capsule that switches between page and editor.

nodes.name: DetailActionRow
nodes.summary: Chooses between the dashboard's own recommendation write, a store-backed quick add for any other title, and an inline "Sign in to add" line. It holds the quick add back until the detail query answers, since the detail is what reveals whether the viewer already tracks the show.

nodes.name: SequelQuickAdd
nodes.summary: The dashboard recommendation's write path, kept separate so its mutation still recomputes the card behind the sheet. Falls back to a sign-in affordance instead of hiding the control when the session cannot write.

nodes.name: MediaQuickAdd
nodes.summary: Quick-add for any title opened outside the dashboard (library, studio page, favourites, activity feed) through the screen's PlanningAddStore, so such a title can be planned without leaving the sheet.

nodes.name: SequelCardDetails.kt
nodes.summary: The text half of a missed-sequel card: titles in all three spellings, status and info chips, a live airing countdown, the viewer's progress meter and a genre line. Every optional field is gated because a relation node often arrives with no studio, score or airing data.

nodes.name: SequelCardDetails
nodes.summary: Draws the card's titles and chips as a FlowRow so four to six chips wrap instead of truncating, plus the countdown and progress rows that only appear when the data supports them.

nodes.name: ArrivingSection.kt
nodes.summary: The "Currently arriving" section: the viewer's own airing and announced entries, deliberately separate from the missed-sequel list and deliberately ignoring every filter, because filtering it would answer "what am I missing?" with things the viewer is not missing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses AnimatedVisibility with FastSpatialSize/FastEffects tokens and animateItem for the horizontal row; the compact variant skips artwork so it loads and recomposes nothing on a schedule.

nodes.name: ArrivingSection
nodes.summary: Renders a collapsible header with a count badge and either a LazyRow of full cards or the artwork-free compact list. It returns early when empty so the section hides itself rather than showing an empty shelf.

nodes.name: AniTopAppBar.kt
nodes.summary: The app's single top bar: avatar, wordmark and viewer handle, with filter, refresh and settings actions. It exists so the dashboard's three controls share one scroll behaviour, one haptic vocabulary and one loading indicator instead of three ad-hoc variants.
nodes.languageNotes: Each action owns a MutableInteractionSource shared with bouncyPress, so a press is cancelled when the gesture becomes a drag instead of the icon squashing through a fling.

nodes.name: AniTopAppBar
nodes.summary: Draws the bar and wires the three actions, showing a badged filter count only when filters are actually narrowing the list and swapping the refresh glyph for an indeterminate indicator while a refresh runs.

nodes.name: QuickFilterBar.kt
nodes.summary: The one-tap status filters above the list. It replaced a horizontally scrolling chip row whose off-screen format filters were unreachable, and now restates the active filter underneath plus an explicit clear control.
nodes.languageNotes: The segmented index follows FilterCriteria rather than stored state, and is -1 for statuses the bar does not offer so the bar cannot highlight "All" while the sheet is filtering by hiatus.

nodes.name: QuickFilterBar
nodes.summary: Composes the four-segment status control and the narrowing row with its clear button. The narrowing test comes from the shared FilterCriteria.isNarrowing predicate, because a local copy missed hidden and relation filters and left no way to explain a shorter list.

nodes.name: SequelCard.kt
nodes.summary: One recommendation row on the dashboard: relation banner, poster, details column, quick plan/watch control and a "Not interested" hide action. The card shares a single interaction source with its press animation because there is one of these per list row and a per-row pointer loop sprung every card a fling passed over.

nodes.name: SequelCard
nodes.summary: Assembles the card and forwards open, plan, watch and hide gestures to the screen. Passing its own interaction source to the Card onClick overload keeps ripple and press scale on the same signal and avoids a second pointer-input node per row.

nodes.name: DashboardUiState.kt
nodes.summary: The dashboard's public contract: the Loading/Success/Error state the screen switches over and the one-shot snackbar event it collects. Split out of the ViewModel so a reader can see what the UI requires without scrolling through the state-mutation half.
nodes.languageNotes: Sealed hierarchies with no behaviour and no dependencies, which is what makes them safe to move out of the state holder.

nodes.name: DashboardUiState
nodes.summary: The three dashboard states. Success carries both the missed list and the arriving list because they answer different questions and only one of them is filtered, plus an isCached flag so the screen can say when it is drawing a saved copy.

nodes.name: Success
nodes.summary: The loaded dashboard: viewer, filtered recommendations, unfiltered arriving rows, both counts, and the flags that tell the screen whether it is refreshing, showing a device snapshot, in demo mode, or able to write to AniList.

nodes.name: DashboardEvent
nodes.summary: One-shot user-facing events, kept apart from the state because a snackbar that has already been missed cannot be un-missed by a re-collection, which is exactly what happens across a configuration change or while a detail sheet covers the screen.

nodes.name: ShowSnackbar
nodes.summary: A snackbar with an optional action label, which is how hiding a recommendation carries its own Undo instead of only telling the reader where the list lives.

nodes.name: ThemeSongsRepository.kt
nodes.summary: Caches a title's openings and endings for the session so revisiting a card costs no second request to the free, rate-limited AnimeThemes service. Successful answers live for a day and empty answers for ten minutes, because a day-long memory of a dropped request would hide the section until the app restarted.
nodes.languageNotes: A synchronized access-order LinkedHashMap gives LRU eviction; the clock is injected so TTL behaviour is testable.

nodes.name: ThemeSongsRepository
nodes.summary: The session cache in front of AnimeThemesApi: 64 entries evicted LRU, a day for a hit and ten minutes for a miss. It is the only network budget in the app that is not AniList's, which is why the cache exists at all.

nodes.name: themes
nodes.summary: Returns a title's themes from cache when fresh, otherwise fetches and stores them. Hit and miss answers expire on different clocks so a transient failure cannot suppress the section for a whole session.

nodes.name: AniThemes
nodes.summary: Process-wide holder for the single ThemeSongsRepository instance. Two instances would double both the requests and the memory for the same cards.

nodes.name: EmptyStateView.kt
nodes.summary: The dashboard's nothing-to-show state, which distinguishes "your filters matched nothing" from "you are caught up". Only the first variant offers a reset button, because telling a caught-up reader to reset filters would be advice that changes nothing.

nodes.name: EmptyStateView
nodes.summary: Draws an Expressive polygon orb, a headline and a body, switching icon, colours and copy between the searching and caught-up cases.

nodes.name: ArrivingEntry.kt
nodes.summary: One of the viewer's own entries that is airing or announced, with its airing countdown and a fuzzy start date. It is its own shape rather than a MissedSequel because a recommendation needs a parent and a relation type that mean nothing for a row already on the user's list.
nodes.languageNotes: siteUrl is built from the media id instead of requested, because the list query cannot afford one more field per entry on its hottest request.

nodes.name: ArrivingEntry
nodes.summary: Carries both the show's status and the viewer's own list status, kept separate so the title page opened from this row knows the entry is already tracked and does not offer to "add" a show that is being watched.

nodes.name: nextAiringCountdown
nodes.summary: Formats the time until the next episode through the shared AiringCountdown helper, with the current time injectable so the countdown can be tested without waiting.

nodes.name: ThemeSong.kt
nodes.summary: A single opening or ending as the title page draws it. It exists because AniList's GraphQL API has no theme-song fields at all, making this the one piece of the title page served by a second service, and the video URL is handed to the system rather than played in-process.

nodes.name: ThemeSong
nodes.summary: Label, type, title, video URL and artwork for one theme. The type is kept apart from the label because the slug is free text while the header needs to count openings and endings separately.

nodes.name: themeSongsSummary
nodes.summary: Builds the section header's second line, "2 openings · 2 endings", pluralising each count and omitting a category the service has nothing for.

nodes.name: SequelPlanningButton.kt
nodes.summary: Thin dashboard-facing wrapper over HoldAndSwipePlanningButton, so a card can offer tap-to-plan, hold-for-progress and swipe-to-watching without knowing the gesture implementation.

nodes.name: SequelPlanningButton
nodes.summary: Delegates to the shared hold-and-swipe control, forwarding the hold duration and swipe toggle so a host can disable the gesture where it would conflict with the surrounding scroll.

nodes.name: DashboardScreen.kt
nodes.summary: The dashboard destination: collects the ViewModel's state, resolves one detail subject from whichever list row, arriving row or relation card was tapped, and owns the filter sheet, the detail sheet and the person-profile sheet. Re-checks list freshness on ON_RESUME because Android resumes the process rather than restarting it, which used to answer from the same cached list for up to an hour after the app was closed and reopened.
nodes.languageNotes: Six collected StateFlows and one memoised subject resolution keyed on the state instance and the open ids; the quick-add settings flow is collected unconditionally because the earlier `prefs?.flow?.collectAsState() ?: remember{...}` form changed composable calls between recompositions.

nodes.name: DashboardScreen
nodes.summary: Draws Loading, Error or Success and routes every tap into one of three sheets. A nullable repository is accepted on purpose: the demo route has no AniList connection, so cast and crew rows render as captions rather than as buttons that could only report a failure.

nodes.name: DashboardRecovery
nodes.summary: Turns a connection-trouble error followed by a success into one shot of the recovery overlay. Kept at screen level because the error view is replaced by the success content, so an animation owned by the error view would be disposed before the glue could finish.

nodes.name: HoldAndSwipePlanningButton.kt
nodes.summary: The quick-add control: tap writes Planning, hold fills toward Watching, an optional drag right confirms Watching immediately. Two entry points (a MissedSequel from the dashboard, a bare media id from any title page) funnel into one implementation so the two hosts cannot drift into different gestures.
nodes.languageNotes: Two Animatable values drive the hold fill and the drag offset; `holdJob` and the 'a hold already committed' flag live inside the pointer-input coroutine rather than in composition because nothing in the layout reads them.

nodes.name: HoldAndSwipePlanningButton
nodes.summary: Adapter that unpacks the dashboard's MissedSequel flags into the id-addressed control, keeping one gesture definition for both call sites.

nodes.name: QuickAddPlanningButton
nodes.summary: The real control, addressed by media id plus flags so a Library row, an activity entry or a studio credit can use it without inventing a parent. Checks Watching before Planning so a title that has been moved on shows its current state, and rounds its own outline into a capsule as the hold fills so the hold does not look identical to a tap.

nodes.name: quickAddGestures
nodes.summary: The pointer-input half of the control: tap-versus-hold by elapsed fill, plus the horizontal drag. Its `holdCommitted` flag is load-bearing — the hold handler snaps the fill back to zero on completion, so without it the release after a finished hold reads as a quick tap and the same title is written to Planning right after Watching.

nodes.name: FilterSortSheet.kt
nodes.summary: The Filter & Sort bottom sheet: sort chips, airing status, media format, the boolean narrowing axes, the franchise-gap relation chips, and the hidden-anime list last because it is the one section that is not a filter. Switch callbacks receive the value the switch is about to hold rather than a bare toggle, so the announced state and the applied state cannot disagree.
nodes.languageNotes: One vertically scrolling Column inside ModalBottomSheet; the current year is read once via remember because the filter itself re-reads it when it runs.

nodes.name: FilterSortSheet
nodes.summary: Renders the sheet from a FilterCriteria snapshot and raises every change upward; it owns no filter state itself, which is what lets the top bar badge, the quick filter row and the empty state share one definition of 'narrowing'.

nodes.name: HiddenSequelsSection.kt
nodes.summary: The collapsible list of anime the user asked to stop being reminded about, with per-row Restore and a Show-all control. It exists because hiding used to be a one-way door: the gesture persisted an id and pointed the user at a Filters > Hidden screen that was never built, leaving clearing app data as the only way back.
nodes.languageNotes: `spring<IntSize>` is spelled out because passing a Dp threshold would pin the spec to FiniteAnimationSpec<Dp>; rows draw colour blocks instead of poster images to avoid decoding thumbnails inside a scrolling sheet.

nodes.name: HiddenSequelsSection
nodes.summary: Collapsed by default and guarded on the list being non-empty, so restoring the last row from inside the expanded body cannot leave an open, empty section behind.

nodes.name: HiddenSequelRow
nodes.summary: One hidden entry with its parent relation and the single control that brings it back; whole-row click restores. Deliberately has no exit animation of its own, since restoring disposes the row and an AnimatedVisibility here would only ever add an enter for something already on screen.

nodes.name: InfoPageItems.kt
nodes.summary: Declares what the Info page lists and in which order, as a LazyListScope extension. Split out of AnimeInfoPage after that function's four-hundred-line body failed CodeFactor's Complex Method check; the split follows the reason to change — the page owns how it behaves, this file owns what is drawn and where.
nodes.languageNotes: Sections take a `visible` argument instead of an `if` at the call site: a LazyColumn item that draws nothing still pays the list's spacedBy gap, and gating by argument keeps the ordering function branch-free.

nodes.name: infoPageItems
nodes.summary: Emits the fifteen numbered sections in reading order, from the parent card through actions, progress, streaming, synopsis, specs, categories, themes, meta rows, rankings, cast, relations, staff and extras.

nodes.name: InfoSections
nodes.summary: The per-title answer to 'which sections draw', precomputed so the gates can answer before the list is built. Fields are booleans rather than the lists they were derived from because that is all this page does with them, except streaming links, which the card is handed directly.

nodes.name: infoSectionsFor
nodes.summary: Pure builder for InfoSections, so the page can remember the whole decision set in one call instead of re-walking genres, tags, links and credits on every recomposition while the sheet opens.

nodes.name: cardItem
nodes.summary: Adds one card section with the page inset and its place in the entrance stagger, and skips the item entirely when invisible rather than drawing an empty slot. The modifier is handed to the content rather than taken by it, because a section that added its own inset would double it.

nodes.name: rowItem
nodes.summary: The edge-to-edge counterpart of cardItem for artwork rows (cast, relations, staff, theme songs): it joins the stagger but applies no page inset, because those rows draw their own heading and LazyRow padding.

nodes.name: MissedSequel.kt
nodes.summary: The model for one franchise entry the viewer's list is missing: the sequel node, the parent it hangs off, the parent's cover and completion year, and the per-card add flags. Its derived strings are memoised with `by lazy` because SequelCard reads them once per visible row on every scroll frame and keystroke while the filter chips animate.
nodes.languageNotes: `by lazy` (SYNCHRONIZED by default) is safe here because every memoised getter reads only `val` fields, and the sync lock is what keeps it correct when a detail load patches a card from a background dispatcher mid-draw.

nodes.name: RelationKind
nodes.summary: The four AniList relation kinds that mean 'a franchise entry this person's list is missing'. Unknown API values fall back to SEQUEL so a new relation name from AniList degrades to the historical behaviour rather than dropping the row.

nodes.name: MissedSequel
nodes.summary: One recommendation as the UI consumes it, including a pre-lowercased search blob whose fields are joined with newlines so a query cannot match across a field boundary no single field contains. `withDetail` folds a lazily fetched node back in, which is how a card gains synopsis, banner and studio after the detail query lands.

nodes.name: InfoThemeSongsSection.kt
nodes.summary: The Openings & Endings row on the title page, the one section fed by a second service. Cards open the .webm externally rather than embedding a player, and the art is the page's own banner because AnimeThemes carries no thumbnails — six cards showing the same cover would read as a gallery rather than a row of this title.
nodes.languageNotes: LazyRow keys include the index because the service can answer two themes with the same label, and a repeated key makes Compose throw while a sheet is opening.

nodes.name: InfoThemeSongsSection
nodes.summary: Draws the heading plus a horizontally scrolling row and nothing else: the absence of themes is decided above it, because a section that rendered its own spinner would need a list slot before it knows it has anything to show.

nodes.name: ThemeSongCard
nodes.summary: One 172x96 card: scrimmed key visual, OP/ED badge, play button and song title, where the play button is the card's only spoken label and only exists when there is a URL to open.

nodes.name: AnimeThemesApi.kt
nodes.summary: Read-only client for AnimeThemes.moe, the only source of OP/ED data AniList's GraphQL schema does not have at all. Builds its own OkHttpClient with no interceptors so the AniList token never leaves for a third party, and returns an empty list on every failure so a second service going away costs one section instead of the title page.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately uses the deprecated-but-live JSON endpoint (one GET, tiny response) instead of AnimeThemes' GraphQL API, which would mean a second client, schema and model set for one row; cancellation is rethrown, everything else collapses to an empty list.

nodes.name: AnimeThemesApi
nodes.summary: Resolves one AniList id to its theme set using the documented `filter[has]=resources` + AniList pair, because `filter[id]` is AnimeThemes' own primary key and would answer nothing. Short timeouts and Dispatchers.IO keep the page from ever waiting on it.

nodes.name: toThemeSongs
nodes.summary: Pure mapping from the service's DTOs to ThemeSong, kept separate from the request so the edge cases can be pinned by a JVM test without a network: slug preferred over sequence (sequence is nullable in practice), unplayable themes still listed, one card per label, openings before endings.

nodes.name: ApiRecoveryOverlay.kt
nodes.summary: The 'Ani-chan is back' celebration shown once a connection failure has been retried successfully. It sits above the screen rather than inside the error view because the error view is exactly what gets replaced, so an animation owned by it would be gone before the glue reached the seam.
nodes.languageNotes: An empty detectTapGestures consumes pointers over a live screen so a tap cannot open a sheet for a card the reader cannot see yet; dismissal is the button or a 2.4s timer.

nodes.name: ApiRecoveryOverlay
nodes.summary: Fires one haptic on appearance, then dismisses itself after a beat long enough to read the line and short enough not to hold a reader hostage to a joke.

nodes.name: DashboardStateViews.kt
nodes.summary: Loading, error and demo-banner bodies for the dashboard, kept apart from the success composition so the screen itself stays about layout.
nodes.languageNotes: The skeleton list takes one shimmer phase from the caller instead of one rememberInfiniteTransition per card, which phase-locks five sweeps into a single travelling highlight.

nodes.name: DashboardLoadingView
nodes.summary: A status surface plus five shimmer cards sharing one animation driver, so the placeholder reads as one list loading rather than five independent sweeps.

nodes.name: DashboardErrorView
nodes.summary: Delegates to ApiFailureBody so the dashboard's failure copy, the connection-status strip and the retry/sign-in actions match every other screen's.

nodes.name: DashboardDemoBanner
nodes.summary: The notice that the list on screen is sample data and signing in will scan the viewer's own list, so a demo session is never mistaken for an empty account.

nodes.name: AnimeRankingsSection.kt
nodes.summary: All-time AniList ranking badges for the Info page, with a single top-rank pill as the fallback when the detailed list is empty. Kept because an all-time ranking is a fact about a title that nothing else on the page can state.
nodes.languageNotes: Ranks of ten or better take the trophy pill and the tertiary container; the rest use a sparkle and the high surface so the section does not shout every ranking equally.

nodes.name: AnimeRankingsSection
nodes.summary: Draws up to four ranking pills, falling back to the best formatted ranking label, and returns early when the title has neither.

nodes.name: RankingPillBadge
nodes.summary: One '#3 Highest Rated' pill whose colour and icon are chosen from the rank, so the top tier is distinguishable without reading the number.

nodes.name: StatsBanner.kt
nodes.summary: The two-card summary at the top of the dashboard: how many entries the viewer has completed and how many franchise gaps were found, with counters that animate to their value.
nodes.languageNotes: The missed-count card switches its icon tint and container when the count is zero, so 'nothing found' does not look like an active result.

nodes.name: StatsBanner
nodes.summary: Lays out the two equal-weight stat cards side by side from the counts the dashboard already holds.

nodes.name: StatCard
nodes.summary: One outlined card with a tinted icon tile, the animated count and a single-line caption that ellipsises rather than wrapping.

nodes.name: FindArrivingEntriesUseCase.kt
nodes.summary: Single pass over the viewer's own list for entries that are airing now or announced — the 'what is coming' question, as opposed to FindMissedSequelsUseCase's relation walk for what is missing. Completed and dropped shows are excluded because those are not arriving for the viewer, while paused stays in because they mean to come back.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Kotlin with no Android imports, so the filtering and ordering can be unit-tested without a client; it never touches relations, which is why it is cheap next to the discovery walk.

nodes.name: FindArrivingEntriesUseCase
nodes.summary: Builds one ArrivingEntry per show, de-duplicated by media id and sorted airing-first then soonest-first.

nodes.name: soonestFirst
nodes.summary: Orders within a half by next episode for airing entries and by start date for upcoming ones, pushing unknown dates last because 'date unknown' is the least useful row to put first.

nodes.name: SequelRelationBanner.kt
nodes.summary: The '<relation> to <parent title>' strip on a recommendation card, with the parent's cover thumbnail and a different tint and icon for an earlier franchise entry, so a missing first season never reads as a sequel.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the parent cover already carried on the model rather than fetching it, which is why MissedSequel keeps coverUrl and coverColor.

nodes.name: SequelRelationBanner
nodes.summary: Renders the relation label and parent in one line, with the thumbnail only when a parent cover URL exists.

nodes.name: AnimeDetailSubject.kt
nodes.summary: One type for whatever the detail sheet is showing: a franchise recommendation with a parent, or a plain list, activity, arriving or relation entry with none. Replaces two nullable parameters every consumer had to unwrap, and deliberately refuses to fabricate a MissedSequel with a meaningless parent.
nodes.languageNotes: Both variants expose the same MediaNode; only the parent narrative and the add-to-list action are sequel-specific and both are gated on `sequel` being non-null.

nodes.name: AnimeDetailSubject
nodes.summary: Sealed interface with Sequel and Media variants, so the sheet, its Info page and its action row take one parameter and cannot disagree about whether there is a parent.

nodes.name: toDetailMedia
nodes.summary: Builds the first-frame node for an arriving row so the sheet can draw before the detail query lands. Pins `type = ANIME` because an untyped detail fetch resolves the id against both namespaces and would answer with the manga sharing that number.

nodes.name: HiddenSequelsPreferences.kt
nodes.summary: Persists the media ids the user chose to stop being reminded about. Deliberately outside FilterCriteria's session lifecycle: hiding is a standing decision someone would be annoyed to repeat on next launch, unlike the other filters the app is free to forget.
nodes.languageNotes: Stored as one comma-separated string because DataStore has no set type and the set is unbounded; parsing drops blanks, stray separators and non-numeric junk instead of throwing on a value the app cannot control.

nodes.name: HiddenSequelsPreferences
nodes.summary: Exposes the hidden ids as a Flow, toggles one id, and clears the set for the Show-all affordance; every write round-trips through the same parser as reads, so a malformed value self-heals.

nodes.name: GetViewerProfileUseCase.kt
nodes.summary: Thin pass-through to AniListRepository.getViewer(), kept so presentation depends on a use case rather than on the repository type.
nodes.languageNotes: Returns the repository's Result as-is; there is no error mapping here because the failure kinds are classified in the data layer.

nodes.name: GetViewerProfileUseCase
nodes.summary: Holds the repository reference and exposes one call, so the signed-in viewer can be read without a screen touching the data layer.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Returns the viewer profile or the repository's failure, with the network error kinds already classified.

nodes.name: SaveToPlanningUseCase.kt
nodes.summary: The single write path a quick-add tap goes through, so the dashboard card, the arriving rows and the detail sheet all land on the same AniList mutation and the same error handling.
nodes.languageNotes: One parameter, one delegation; the point is the seam, not the logic.

nodes.name: SaveToPlanningUseCase
nodes.summary: Wraps the repository's add-to-Planning mutation so no composable or ViewModel has to know how a list entry is written.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Adds one media id to Planning and returns the created list entry, or the repository's failure.

nodes.name: AniListRepositoryImpl.kt
nodes.summary: The one implementation of AniListRepository: composes GraphQL documents, coalesces identical reads, caches list, detail, cover and profile answers in memory and on disk, and classifies every failure into an AniListErrorKind. Deliberately over the 700-line ceiling because the caches, the coalescer and the rate-limit errors are a single mechanism whose invariants would have to be passed around if it were split.
nodes.languageNotes: Kotlin with ConcurrentHashMap caches stamped from one injectable clock, a volatile listEpoch that rejects writes from fetches which began before a mutation, and an injected TTL supplier so the staleness windows are testable at their edges without sleeping.

nodes.name: AniListRepositoryImpl
nodes.summary: Answers every read and write the app makes to AniList and owns the cache policy above them: which answers are worth keeping, for how long, and what a mutation invalidates. All I/O funnels through one execute() so a HTTP, GraphQL or Moshi failure becomes a typed failure instead of wording the UI has to guess at.
nodes.languageNotes: Every read is keyed on a namespace (MediaCoverKey, PersonKind + id, user: / userName:), because AniList ids are unique per namespace and a bare-id cache served an anime to a manga caller.

nodes.name: mediaCoverBatches
nodes.summary: Splits cover keys into documents of at most ten aliases. The cap exists because AniList refuses an over-complex document with HTTP 400 for the whole thing, and a refused cover batch is invisible: every poster it carried stays on its placeholder with nothing on screen to explain it.

nodes.name: toSaveVariables
nodes.summary: Encodes which SaveMediaListEntry arguments may be absent. Sending progressVolumes as null makes AniList answer HTTP 400 and store nothing (verified against the live API), so it is omitted instead while progress and score default to 0 and the dates keep their null-means-clear meaning.

nodes.name: toVariables
nodes.summary: Turns a partial FuzzyDate into the FuzzyDateInput map AniList expects, keeping per-field nulls because a year with no month or day is a real date to the API and is how the editor clears a date.

nodes.name: DemoProfileProvider.kt
nodes.summary: The demo profile screen's fixture: bio, statistics, five favourites lists, an activity feed, followers and following. Kept apart from DemoDataProvider because that file exists to make relation edges while this one populates a person's page, and its aggregate numbers deliberately do not match the five-entry demo list.
nodes.languageNotes: Object of builder helpers. Distributions are built in the statistics.anime shape because the deprecated stats.favoured* fields answer HTTP 500 for the whole profile document.

nodes.name: DemoProfileProvider
nodes.summary: Holds the demo person's whole page in the exact response shapes the real queries parse, so the stats, favourites and social tabs can be exercised without a session and a shape change in the API breaks the demo too.

nodes.name: getDemoUserOverview
nodes.summary: Builds the demo UserOverview: Markdown bio, anime and manga statistics, the deprecated aggregate block and five favourites lists whose status counts add up to the 261 in statistics.anime.count so the Stats cards cannot disagree with each other.

nodes.name: getDemoActivity
nodes.summary: A recent activity feed with relative timestamps, including the fixture's only manga row so the chapter wording and type chip are exercised offline, and two rows on one media so the feed is keyed on the activity id rather than the media id.

nodes.name: getDemoFollowers
nodes.summary: Returns real AniList accounts as followers, so tapping a face in the demo opens a profile that actually exists instead of making the Social tab look broken.

nodes.name: UserOverview.kt
nodes.summary: Moshi models for the profile payload: the person, their deprecated aggregate statistics, five favourites lists, per-day activity history, and the activity feed modelled only as its ListActivity union member. Split from ViewerProfile so the payload every launch needs does not carry the favourites tree.
nodes.languageNotes: @JsonClass(generateAdapter = true) data classes. Every connection node is nullable because AniList omits branches a user never filled, and the favoured format/year/genre/tag fields are absent on purpose: asking for any one of them makes the entire profile document answer HTTP 500.

nodes.name: UserOverview
nodes.summary: The profile query's payload: the bio as raw Markdown for the in-app renderer, avatar, banner, statistics, favourites and the deprecated stats block. The bio is not stripped to plain text because AboutCard renders the parsed nodes, and the API's ParsedMarkdown is a GFM AST rather than anything drawable.

nodes.name: AniListUserStats
nodes.summary: User.stats, kept despite deprecation because activityHistory and the status and score distributions have no replacement in the schema. The four favoured* lists were deleted from it because any one of them makes AniList answer HTTP 500 for the whole profile document, so a future edit cannot ask for them by accident.

nodes.name: ListActivity
nodes.summary: One row of the activity feed. The feed is a GraphQL union Moshi cannot discriminate, so only this member is modelled and isUnrecognised lets the repository drop other members instead of drawing a blank card; isLiked stays nullable because null means unknown (no token), never not liked.
nodes.languageNotes: status arrives lowercase here, unlike every other status in the API, so the display helpers compare case-insensitively.

nodes.name: Favourites
nodes.summary: The five lists a person has pinned by hand. Each branch is separately nullable because AniList omits or nulls any of them a user never added to, and a missing branch means the same thing to the UI as an empty one: no section to draw.

nodes.name: PersonName
nodes.summary: One name object serving both CharacterName and StaffName, which AniList declares separately with identical fields. displayName falls back full to native to the first alternative and finally to Unknown so a cast row can never render blank.

nodes.name: FollowUser
nodes.summary: Somebody in a followers or following grid, keeping both the id (so their profile query can be keyed on it) and the name (because it is what the grid prints and what the next screen's cache key uses).

nodes.name: BuildListInsightsUseCase.kt
nodes.summary: Reshapes AniList's aggregate statistics into the rows the Stats tab draws, keeping the ordering and share arithmetic out of the UI so it can be tested without an emulator: status in a fixed order with watching first, scores ascending by score, formats and genres by count.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Kotlin with no Android imports. Shares are always relative to the largest row of the same chart, which is what lets a status chart and a years chart sit under each other without one being a flat line.

nodes.name: BuildListInsightsUseCase
nodes.summary: One invoke turns the raw distributions into the screen model. A status this app has never seen is labelled by breaking its enum name apart rather than dropped, because the label is the only place a person would learn the status exists and an underscore would be the database leaking through.

nodes.name: ListInsights
nodes.summary: Everything on the Stats tab that one profile round trip answers for. Countries and release years arrive already tallied by the list-entry insights use case and are not re-sorted here, because sorting by label put a nineteen-hundreds year after an apostrophe-prefixed one.

nodes.name: BucketTally
nodes.summary: One row of a horizontal bar chart: label, count and share of the chart's own maximum. The share is computed in the use case so every chart on the screen scales the same way rather than each composable inventing its own denominator.

nodes.name: StatusDistribution
nodes.summary: The status chips plus the segmented strip they describe. Segments are a separate shape from BucketTally because widths have to sum to one whole, and isEmpty keeps the card from drawing an empty strip.

nodes.name: PersonProfileStore.kt
nodes.summary: Holds whichever character or staff sheet is open and runs its fetch, with a pending (kind, id) guard so a late answer for a dismissed person cannot paint over the one now open. Remembers fetched profiles so tapping back to a face costs no request and never flashes a spinner over a page already read.
nodes.languageNotes: A plain class rather than a ViewModel because the state is Closed whenever nobody is looking at it; it cancels its scope on dispose only when it created that scope, so a test-supplied TestScope is left alive.

nodes.name: PersonProfileStore
nodes.summary: Opens, guards, remembers and retries character and staff profiles for the sheet. The id travels on the Failed state so retry() has something to re-run, because a retry button that cannot name its own subject is a control that does nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: The map is keyed on PersonKind as well as id: Character(1) and Staff(1) are different people, the same namespace collision the repository's caches document.

nodes.name: toMediaNode
nodes.summary: Maps a profile row's appearance to the MediaNode the detail sheet opens on, so a tap routes to the sheet instead of re-fetching a title the reader is already looking at. type travels with the id because an id alone resolves against whichever namespace AniList prefers.

nodes.name: ActivityLikersSheet.kt
nodes.summary: The read-only sheet listing who liked an activity. Visibility is derived from the ViewModel's nullable likers state so a loading or empty sheet is never up with nothing under it, skeleton rows stand in for the faces that are coming, and a failed load offers the retry that would succeed.
nodes.languageNotes: Material3 ModalBottomSheet over a single LazyColumn keyed per row; shimmer comes from the shared rememberShimmerPhase and the rows reuse the comments sheet's spacing so the two engagement sheets read as one family.

nodes.name: ActivityLikersSheet
nodes.summary: Draws the likers sheet and picks one body per state: skeleton rows while loading, an error sentence with a retry, an explicit empty line, or the list. Liking itself is a tap on the card, so nothing here writes.

nodes.name: LikersHeader
nodes.summary: The count line above the rows. While the list is still coming it reads Likes rather than Liked by 0, because a zero would be a claim about the activity the app has not been told yet.

nodes.name: LikerRow
nodes.summary: One liker: a 34dp avatar circle plus their name, the same shape a comment author gets so the same person reads the same in either sheet.

nodes.name: AniListApiService.kt
nodes.summary: The Retrofit contract for AniList's single GraphQL endpoint: one POST to root per document, told apart only by the query body. Kept as thin documented declarations so the per-operation reasoning stays beside the signature, such as why followers and following are two methods or why covers must go through Page.
nodes.languageNotes: Every method is a suspend @POST(/), with identical JSON headers, taking a GraphQLRequest and returning GraphQLResponse<T>; the documents themselves live in GraphQLQueries.

nodes.name: AniListApiService
nodes.summary: One method per GraphQL operation the app performs, including the deliberately narrow ping used as the reachability probe. The interface exists so the repository composes variables while the query strings stay in one place, and so a test can answer any single operation without a socket.

nodes.name: RequestCoalescer.kt
nodes.summary: Collapses identical in-flight requests into one network call, which is the only de-duplication AniList permits: it rejects GET and sends no-cache headers with no ETag, so an OkHttp disk cache would store nothing and re-download every time. It also refuses to hand a leader's cancellation to its waiters, which used to kill the load that replaced it and leave the screen on a silent spinner.
nodes.languageNotes: A mutex-guarded map of CompletableDeferred keyed by the caller. Slot claiming is one critical section, and the leader's removal runs under NonCancellable so a cancelled leader cannot strand a completed deferred that would then be served forever.

nodes.name: RequestCoalescer
nodes.summary: Generic over the key type so the repository can key on operation plus sorted variables. A real failure such as a 429 is shared verbatim with every waiter, because retrying it once per waiter would turn one rate-limit answer into N requests; only cancellation is refused and retried.

nodes.name: MediaDetailHost.kt
nodes.summary: One app-wide owner of the detail store, created at the navigation root so the Library, the Profile and the studio page share a single cache. Four separate owners used to mean the same title opened from two tabs was two requests, two loading flags and two different pages.
nodes.languageNotes: rememberMediaDetailHost builds a SupervisorJob scope and disposes on the scope rather than the host, so rebuilding the host for a new repository cannot leave the previous scope's requests running.

nodes.name: MediaDetailHost
nodes.summary: Exposes only the three things a screen needs from MediaDetailStore: the fetched nodes, the ids still on the wire, and the load callback the detail sheet calls. It is an addition, not a different rule, which is why the dashboard keeps its own store for the extra write it makes into the recommendation cards.

nodes.name: rememberMediaDetailHost
nodes.summary: Remembers the host for the life of the composition and cancels the scope it made when that composition goes. It has to be called once at the navigation root: calling it per route brings back exactly the split cache the host exists to fix.

nodes.name: EntryEditor.kt
nodes.summary: The read-write contract the detail sheet's Edit tab is handed: load, save and delete as one bundle, so no screen can be built with one of the three controls dead. Null wherever the sheet is read-only removes the tab instead of drawing an editor that silently does nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: All three methods suspend and return Result, so the tab can run them in its own scope and keep a saving flag to itself rather than threading it through the dashboard state.

nodes.name: EntryEditor
nodes.summary: The three answers to one question: what is on my list for this show, and change it. load returns an empty entry carrying the media id rather than a failure, because not being on the list yet is the ordinary state for an arriving show the form has to create.

nodes.name: GraphQLQueries.kt
nodes.summary: Every GraphQL document the app sends to graphql.anilist.co, kept in one file so the cost of a field in one document can be read against the others. Deliberately over the 700-line ceiling: asking studios(isMain: true) inside relations turns a 476-entry list into an HTTP 500, and that is a fact about the boundary between documents rather than about any single query.
nodes.languageNotes: Raw GraphQL in Kotlin string templates with `${'$'}` escapes for variable sigils; detail documents are assembled with buildString so a concatenation seam cannot swallow a newline.

nodes.name: GraphQLQueries
nodes.summary: Object holding the query and mutation documents as constants, with builder functions only where the document varies by input (media type, cover batch size). Field lists are shared constants so the list query and the detail query cannot drift apart field by field.
nodes.languageNotes: Private const field-list constants (RELATED_NODE_FIELDS, MEDIA_DETAIL_FIELDS, STUDIO_MEDIA_FIELDS, PROFILE_MEDIA_FIELDS) interpolated into the documents.

nodes.name: mediaListQuery
nodes.summary: One builder for both the anime and manga list documents, differing only in the MediaType variable, because a second copy of this long field list would be a second place to forget to widen. Also the app's heaviest request: it asks for relations once per page of the user's whole list, so every added field is multiplied by the page size.
nodes.languageNotes: Takes the query name as a parameter and passes MediaType as a GraphQL variable so AniList validates it instead of it being pasted into query text.

nodes.name: getMediaCoversQuery
nodes.summary: Builds a batch of aliased Page.media lookups so a bio's dozen preview cards cost one request instead of a dozen of AniList's 30-a-minute budget. Each alias resolves Page.media rather than the nullable Media root field because a single stale id in the batch makes Media(...) answer HTTP 404 and blanks every poster, while a connection filters to an empty list.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds the variable declaration string with an explicit `\$` sigil; omitting it produced `id0: Int`, which AniList rejected with a 400 for the whole batch.

nodes.name: mediaCoverAlias
nodes.summary: Returns the alias for the nth requested id so batched cover results can be read back. Indexed by position rather than media id because one batch can carry the same numeric id in both the anime and manga namespaces, and a per-id alias would collide and silently drop one poster.

nodes.name: getMediaDetailQuery
nodes.summary: Builds the single-title detail document, typed or untyped depending on whether the caller knows the media namespace. AniList media ids are not unique across anime and manga, so a bare id resolves to whichever namespace the server prefers - opening a manga from the Library used to render the anime sharing its id, and the failure looked like missing content rather than wrong content.
nodes.languageNotes: Declares `type: MediaType` nullable rather than `MediaType!` so a summary node with no type can still open the sheet instead of invalidating the document.

nodes.name: getStudioQuery
nodes.summary: One studio plus one page of its filmography, sorted START_DATE_DESC for the screen's year shelves. It is Studio.media rather than Page.media because Page has no studioId argument at all, and perPage is capped at 25 because that is this connection's documented maximum - both mistakes answer HTTP 400 rather than an empty page.

nodes.name: getCharacterProfileQuery
nodes.summary: One character and the titles they appear in, asked as edges so characterRole and voiceActors travel with each poster. Both media namespaces are requested: filtering to ANIME quietly dropped the source manga of the very title whose cast row opened the sheet, while the staff page listed manga credits the character page hid.
nodes.languageNotes: voiceActors is selected twice under Japanese and English aliases because the field answers null without a language argument.

nodes.name: getStaffProfileQuery
nodes.summary: One staff member with both staffMedia and characterMedia, so a creator page can show what they produced and who they voiced. Deliberately the same shape as the character query because both render through one composable, and twenty-five edges are asked for since a staff connection has one edge per credit rather than per title.
nodes.languageNotes: dateOfBirth and dateOfDeath are both requested because either is null for a living person and the card hides whichever is absent.

nodes.name: ProfileSocialTab.kt
nodes.summary: The Social tab: a fixed three-column face grid (or a full-width name list) of the followers and following of whichever profile is open. Search narrows the grid; the A-Z switch is the only thing that reorders it, because AniList's own order is roughly most-recently-followed and throwing that away by default answers a question nobody asked.
nodes.languageNotes: Both view modes live in one LazyVerticalGrid keyed by list plus mode, so switching mode keeps the scroll position and does not rebuild the header rows.

nodes.name: ProfileSocialTab
nodes.summary: Composable that triggers the first load when the tab is opened (otherwise it sits in Idle forever), then draws selector chips, a search field, the A-Z chip and the people grid. Search and sort are rememberSaveable so a rotation does not hand back AniList order with the grid silently reshuffled.
nodes.languageNotes: Takes an externally hoisted LazyGridState so the scroll position outlives a tab switch; sorts with Locale.ROOT because a Turkish locale would otherwise sort every name containing an i to the end.

nodes.name: SocialViewToggle
nodes.summary: Grid/list switch whose glyph shows the mode currently on screen rather than the one the tap will switch to, because a control sitting under the grid reads as a claim about that grid. Sized at 48dp rather than the chip row's 44 because it has no label and its hit area is the only sign it is a control.

nodes.name: FollowerCard
nodes.summary: One face in the grid: a square avatar with a hairline border and a single ellipsised name. The border exists because two hundred avatars on the app's surface colour bled into a single mosaic with no edges; the square crop matches AniList's own 220x220 avatar so nothing is resampled.

nodes.name: FollowerRow
nodes.summary: One person as a full-width row with a 52dp portrait and an unconstrained, two-line name - the mode that answers 'who is this handle'. The portrait cannot go much below 48dp or it stops reading as a face next to a line of text.

nodes.name: UserActivityViewModel.kt
nodes.summary: State holder for the Activity tab of a profile: paginated list history, optimistic likes, the likers sheet and the delegation to CommentThreadStore. Fetches only when the tab is selected, because a profile someone glanced at must not spend AniList's request budget on a scrollback.
nodes.languageNotes: Exposes ActivityState and LikersState as StateFlows; a mutation-version flow from the repository refetches the viewer's own feed after a list write.

nodes.name: UserActivityViewModel
nodes.summary: Owns the feed's page cursor, the started flag and the pending-like set, and is the single holder the profile screen talks to even though the comment thread lives in a separate store. Its init records the repository's mutation version without reacting to it, because the first emission is the count of writes that happened before this feed existed.
nodes.languageNotes: Distinguishes userId (whose feed) from viewerId (whose comments may be managed); the feed is refetched only when those two match.

nodes.name: ActivityState
nodes.summary: Sealed feed state carrying pendingLikes so a card can disable its own heart on the frame the tap lands, and loadMoreError because a failed extra page used to leave no trace: the pagination effect never re-fired and the feed ended for the session with hasMore still true.

nodes.name: LikersState
nodes.summary: The likers sheet's state, carrying the activity id it belongs to so a slow response for a sheet the reader already closed and replaced is discarded instead of painted over the new one. Nullable in the ViewModel, so the sheet's visibility derives from the state and it is never up over nothing.

nodes.name: toggleLike
nodes.summary: Optimistically flips one activity's heart and count, then settles both from the server's answer because the optimistic count was a guess. Refuses while a request for the same activity is in flight and when isLiked is null (no session), so a double tap cannot toggle twice.

nodes.name: Factory
nodes.summary: ViewModelProvider.Factory that injects the repository, the feed's user id, the viewer id and the demo flag, so the profile route can build a feed for whoever it opened rather than for the signed-in account.

nodes.name: LibraryScreen.kt
nodes.summary: The reader's own library as a main-bar page rather than a profile tab, because a library belongs to one account and the bar is where the reader's own things live. Draws ProfileLibraryTab unchanged, adds a title-count subtitle, and opens the same SequelDetailSheet the dashboard opens so a title is the same page everywhere.
nodes.languageNotes: Applies start and end Scaffold insets explicitly: padding only the top dropped the resolved horizontal insets and ran the bar and every poster under a landscape display cutout.

nodes.name: LibraryScreen
nodes.summary: Composable page that collects the overview, the manga half of the library and the shared detail store at page level (a fetch already started must not be dropped by a grid scrolled away from), then hosts the detail sheet and the person sheet as siblings of the content because a ModalBottomSheet is its own window. Favourite ids come from the overview so pinning and favouriting can never disagree.
nodes.languageNotes: AnimatedContent on the subtitle with ExpressiveMotion.FastEffects so the count lands a beat after the name instead of hard-swapping a line in the top bar.

nodes.name: MediaDetailStore.kt
nodes.summary: The detail sheet's on-demand media detail, shared by one instance across the Library, the profile and the studio page so the same title is the same page everywhere. A failed load is swallowed on purpose: the sheet already has the summary query's data, and interrupting the reader over a synopsis that did not arrive is worse.
nodes.languageNotes: Two access-ordered LinkedHashMaps bounded at 250 entries - one keyed by MediaCoverKey for fetches, one keyed by id for what the screens read - because publishing used to grow without a bound.

nodes.name: MediaDetailStore
nodes.summary: Holds the namespaced fetch cache, the published snapshot the screens read, and the in-flight set, and owns the rule that a re-opened entry is republished without another request. The fetch cache is keyed by media type as well as id, so a manga is never served out of the anime that shares its id.
nodes.languageNotes: details is a snapshot of the access-ordered map because MutableStateFlow compares by equality and an in-place mutation would emit nothing to collectors.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Fetches one title's heavy fields unless it is cached or already in flight, then publishes it and hands it to the host's fold callback. Wraps the repository in repositoryResult because a throwing repository used to escape the launch and close the app while the sheet was opening.
nodes.languageNotes: The in-flight guard was once a Set<Int>, so opening anime/1 while manga/1 was loading was dropped as already loading; the spinner is only cleared when no namespace for that id is still fetching.

nodes.name: cached
nodes.summary: Returns a title's already-fetched detail without starting a request, namespaced by type because the fold a card performs on it is invisible - the card would just keep rendering another title's synopsis.

nodes.name: clear
nodes.summary: Drops both caches, the in-flight set and the spinner when the collection they were built against changes. In-flight work is cleared rather than left to drain, since a launch for a collection that no longer exists has nothing to fold its answer into.

nodes.name: AniListException.kt
nodes.summary: Classifies every AniList failure at the boundary so screens can branch on a kind instead of searching exception text for words like 'invalid'. AniList answers a rejected token with the same HTTP 400 it uses for a malformed query, so the parsed error body has to decide, and signing a working user out over a typo is the failure this avoids.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads at most 64 KB of an error body through okio Buffer.read so a proxy's HTML error page cannot exhaust the heap during a failed request.

nodes.name: AniListErrorKind
nodes.summary: The branchable set of failures: dead session, rate limited, offline, server, not found, invalid request, malformed response and unknown. MALFORMED_RESPONSE is its own kind because retrying re-sends the same request and gets the same unparseable body - what helps is a build whose models match the API.

nodes.name: AniListException
nodes.summary: A failure carrying its kind plus the Retry-After wait when the kind is RATE_LIMITED, so the notice can print a real number instead of a message the UI has to parse.

nodes.name: aniListHttpError
nodes.summary: Maps an HTTP status plus the first parsed GraphQL error into a classified failure, kept separate from the Retrofit plumbing so the mapping can be tested without a network response. 401/403/429/5xx are decided first, and only then may the body overturn 400 or 404, which AniList overloads.
nodes.languageNotes: Drops a negative Retry-After (free text from the server) because the old mapping printed 'Try again in -1s.'; zero is kept as a real 'retry now'.

nodes.name: toAniListException
nodes.summary: Extension that classifies one GraphQL error entry by its message, used only where the HTTP status is ambiguous. Status 400 is deliberately not trusted on its own because AniList uses it for both a rejected token and a malformed query, and only the wording separates them.

nodes.name: readCapped
nodes.summary: Reads at most 64 KB of an error body, because ResponseBody.string() would read an arbitrarily large HTML error page into memory before the classifier could reject it. Returns null on any failure: an unreadable body is not a reason to replace the failure the caller already has.

nodes.name: BuildActivityCalendarUseCase.kt
nodes.summary: Turns AniList's per-day activity history into a GitHub-shaped heatmap of 26 Sunday-first weeks. Uses activityHistory rather than completions because bumping progress on a show in flight is activity that leaves no completedAt anywhere, and buckets in UTC so the same account draws the same grid on two phones.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Kotlin with java.time; Sunday-first indexing via dayOfWeek.value % 7 must stay consistent with the M/W/F gutter labels.

nodes.name: BuildActivityCalendarUseCase
nodes.summary: Folds history into one entry per calendar day, adds duplicates rather than overwriting them, and totals only the cells it actually draws so a future-dated entry cannot make the header claim activity above an empty grid.

nodes.name: ActivityCalendar
nodes.summary: The finished grid: columns of seven days, month labels placed only where the month changes, three weekday gutter labels, a total and a week count, plus isEmpty so the UI does not have to re-derive 'nothing happened'.
nodes.languageNotes: Only Monday, Wednesday and Friday are labelled because seven letters in a 13dp column overlap, and unlabelled rows read as gaps in the data.

nodes.name: ActivityDay
nodes.summary: One cell, holding a 0f..1f intensity instead of AniList's 1-to-7 level so the colour ramp never has to know how many steps that scale has, plus inRange so the tail of the last column past today is not painted.

nodes.name: UserSocialViewModel.kt
nodes.summary: State holder for the Social tab. Fetches followers and following in one coroutine as two deferred requests, because Page accepts one data field but the user is one tap from switching, and prefetching on that tap turns a spinner into an instant switch.
nodes.languageNotes: Both requests are launched with async and awaited together; the first failure wins and is classified with AniListErrorKind.INVALID_SESSION.

nodes.name: UserSocialViewModel
nodes.summary: Holds one state flow for both social lists. updateUserId deliberately does not treat Idle as 'go and get it': Idle is the initial state, so doing that spent two requests on every scanned profile the reader had merely glanced at.
nodes.languageNotes: updateUserId's `when` over Error/Loading has no else on purpose - widening the guard must stop compiling rather than fetch the wrong list.

nodes.name: SocialList
nodes.summary: Which side of the social graph is showing; carried through the state so a retry or an id update re-fetches the list the reader is looking at rather than the default one.

nodes.name: SocialState
nodes.summary: Sealed tab state. Success carries both lists and the selected side with a peopleFor helper, so switching tabs is a copy rather than a request; Error keeps the list it failed for so the retry row can name it.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Fetches the picked list and its counterpart once each, reusing a loaded Success for a plain tab switch. Fetched on demand rather than in init because this is the one tab that fans out into two requests.

nodes.name: Factory
nodes.summary: ViewModelProvider.Factory injecting the repository, the profile's user id and the demo flag, so the Social tab is always built for the profile the route opened.

nodes.name: AniSequelWidgetData.kt
nodes.summary: Where the home-screen widgets read their numbers, titles and artwork. Reads a SharedPreferences snapshot the app writes on each load, because widgets are updated outside the process lifecycle, and falls back to demo fixtures only until a session has synced - a signed-in user with nothing missed used to see '3' and 'Demon Slayer'.
nodes.languageNotes: KEY_USERNAME being present is the marker that demo fallbacks must stop applying; it is never cleared, or every accessor would flip back to fixtures.

nodes.name: AniSequelWidgetData
nodes.summary: Singleton holding the widget cache keys and the read accessors, each of which prefers a present preference key over the fixture - even when that key holds an empty string - so a real session never sees somebody else's poster.

nodes.name: storedString
nodes.summary: The rule every string accessor shares: a present key wins, and once a username exists an absent value is genuinely absent rather than an invitation to draw demo data. Factored out so the seven accessors cannot each get that rule slightly differently.

nodes.name: updateData
nodes.summary: Persists the latest dashboard and profile snapshot for the widgets. A null argument means clear rather than leave-as-is: writing only non-null values left a stale 'Top: ...' title under the widget's 'all caught up' caption after the missed list emptied.

nodes.name: RepositoryEntryEditor.kt
nodes.summary: The EntryEditor implementation for hosts that are not the dashboard - the Library, the studio page and the profile - so the same title no longer opens a sheet with one fewer tab depending on which list the reader came from. There is one class rather than three because the entry on that tab is always the viewer's own.
nodes.languageNotes: No post-save refresh here on purpose: the repository drops its list cache on every write, so the next pull-to-refresh re-reads the server instead of a copy this class would have to update.

nodes.name: RepositoryEntryEditor
nodes.summary: Delegates load, save and delete straight to the repository, passing a nullable viewer id so an omitted id resolves to the authenticated viewer. Null is a valid request, not a signed-out one, and a null id with no session fails in the repository so the tab surfaces it instead of drawing a form that cannot save.

nodes.name: SaveToWatchingUseCase.kt
nodes.summary: One-tap 'start watching': a thin domain entry point that puts a media id on the user's Currently Watching list through the repository, keeping the sheet's action out of the data layer's naming.

nodes.name: SaveToWatchingUseCase
nodes.summary: Adds an anime entry directly to Currently Watching, returning the created entry; exists so callers depend on the intent rather than on the repository method that implements it.

nodes.name: ProfileLibraryTab.kt
nodes.summary: The reader's own anime and manga library as a poster grid with type, status, search and sort controls. Its filtering, ordering and progress-badge rules are pure top-level functions rather than composable state so each can be pinned by a unit test, because every one of them replaces a specific shipped failure: a Recent sort that returned the input unchanged, a Score sort that reversed null scores to the top, and a Manga filter that still showed anime because it compared status but never the media type.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure helpers (toggleSort, selectSort, sortLibrary, filterLibrary, libraryCounts, libraryProgressLabel) sit above the composables deliberately; the remembered view is resolved one level up so re-entering the page never re-asks DataStore, and the grid uses animateItem with the shared spring tokens so a filter reads as a rearrangement rather than a redraw.

nodes.name: UserProfileScreen.kt
nodes.summary: The profile page shell: top bar, four-tab capsule (Home, Activity, Stats, Social), per-profile saved tab, and the comment, likers and person-profile sheets drawn as siblings of the tab content. Those sheets are hoisted out of the tabs because AnimatedContent disposes the outgoing tab and a ModalBottomSheet drawn inside one is torn down with it, losing an open thread mid-draft.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a private staticCompositionLocalOf to carry the main-bar flag down to profileListPadding without threading a parameter through every tab signature, and hoists the LazyListState of all four tabs above AnimatedContent so scroll position survives a tab switch.

nodes.name: UserOverviewViewModel.kt
nodes.summary: State holder for the profile's Home and Stats tabs and for the Library page. It issues two requests on purpose: the single overview query paints the bio and favourites immediately, while the whole media list (one request per 500 entries and the most expensive query in the app) is merged in afterwards so the page is never held hostage by the tallies. It also owns the on-demand manga list, the bio cover batch, and the cold-start paint from the last saved snapshot.
nodes.languageNotes: MutableStateFlow backed by asStateFlow, a cancellable loadJob plus separate coverJob and mangaJob, and internal helpers flattenLibrary and distinctById that exist because AniList returns duplicate list entries and duplicate favourites, which crash a keyed LazyRow.

nodes.name: AniListRepository.kt
nodes.summary: The repository contract every screen reads through, declared as an interface with defaulted members so the demo and test doubles only implement what they can honestly serve. Anything an implementation cannot answer throws rather than returning an empty list, because an empty activity feed and a failed one look identical on screen and only one of them is a claim about the person.
nodes.languageNotes: Defaults live on the interface (Kotlin requires them there) with unsupported() throwing; listMutationVersion is a shared IdleListMutations StateFlow so a collector is not handed a new object on every recomposition of a title sheet, and STUDIO_PAGE_SIZE is named once because 25 is AniList's documented maximum rather than a preference.

nodes.name: ProfileActivityTab.kt
nodes.summary: The profile's Activity tab: the 26-week contribution calendar followed by a paginated feed of tinted activity cards. It fetches its first page only when the tab is composed rather than when the profile opens, so opening a profile to look at favourites costs one request. The comment sheet is intentionally not drawn here; UserProfileScreen owns both sheets so they outlive a tab switch.
nodes.languageNotes: Paging is triggered by a derivedStateOf over LazyListState layoutInfo six rows from the end, and the scroll state is a required parameter because a state created inside this composable dies with the AnimatedContent transition.

nodes.name: ProfileDestination.kt
nodes.summary: The navigation route for a profile: three route shapes, the route constants the widget and dashboard navigate to, and the wiring that builds three ViewModels keyed per profile plus the entry editor the detail sheet needs. Identity is passed in rather than looked up so the first frame is a header instead of a spinner, and so the list fetch reuses the dashboard's user:<id> cache instead of re-downloading the most expensive query in the app.
nodes.languageNotes: Routes are matched exactly, so OWN_DEFAULT is profile?tab= with an empty optional argument: navigating to bare "profile" matched nothing and made the dashboard avatar tap silently dead.

nodes.name: BuildListEntryInsightsUseCase.kt
nodes.summary: Tallies the three Stats-tab distributions AniList publishes no aggregate for - country of origin, release year, the year a title was finished, and episode-count bands - from the media list the app already downloaded for the sequel walk. It is a use case rather than a groupBy in the ViewModel because the bucket boundaries are decisions that have to be written down and pinned by a test.
nodes.languageNotes: No Android imports; groups year charts on the real Int year rather than the two-digit label, because 1999 and 2019 both render as '19 and sorting on a reconstructed century placed 1995 after 2019.

nodes.name: PlanningAddStore.kt
nodes.summary: One-tap Add to Planning / Add to Watching for any title the detail sheet is showing, keyed by media id so walking a franchise keeps each title's own state. It exists because the dashboard's add lived on a MissedSequel and a snackbar host, neither of which exist on the Library, a studio page or somebody's activity feed - which is why those hosts used to draw no add button at all.
nodes.languageNotes: Error is part of QuickAddStatus rather than a snackbar event, because only the dashboard owns a SnackbarHostState; a busy guard collapses a double tap into one request, and the remembered host owns its own scope so a write outlives the sheet that started it.

nodes.name: PersonProfileHost.kt
nodes.summary: The bundle three screens need to offer character and staff profile sheets: the store, its state, two nullable callbacks for the detail sheet, and the sheet itself drawn as a sibling of that sheet. Without it the same forty lines are written three times and drift, typically by one screen gaining a retry button the others never get.
nodes.languageNotes: Callbacks are nullable rather than defaulted to a no-op: a demo host with no repository must draw cast rows as captions, and an empty lambda cannot be told apart from a real handler, which is how a tappable control that does nothing appears.

nodes.name: ProfileAvatarButton.kt
