nodes.summary: The avatar as the way into the reader's own AniList profile, shared by the dashboard top bar and the Library page so the two entries cannot drift. It is not an IconButton because both tap and hold must open it, and because the hold gesture installs a pointer handler rather than a clickable, so Role.Button and a content description have to be set by hand.
nodes.languageNotes: The 36dp image and the 6dp padding are one element so the touch target clears 48dp; while enabled is false the modifier chain omits the gesture and declares disabled(), because a tap during a cold start would otherwise open the demo profile.

nodes.name: LibrarySort
nodes.summary: The orderings the library grid can use, each carrying its chip label and whether a direction is meaningful. LIST_ORDER is documented as the order AniList returned - it used to be called Recent, which was a lie because MediaListCollection returns status groups with no timestamp; UPDATED_AT is the real recency sort the fake one was pretending to be.

nodes.name: LibraryFilter
nodes.summary: The list buckets the library can be narrowed to, each with a reading label and an anime label so a manga row never says Watching. Dropped and Rewatching are included even though they are less prominent, because AniList records both and a filter row that omitted them would make those entries reachable only under All.

nodes.name: ProfileLibraryTab
nodes.summary: Draws the three-column poster grid with its type, filter, search and sort controls, and refuses to draw anything until DataStore has answered the remembered view. Rendering an ALL grid during that window flashed every anime entry before a remembered Manga view landed, and made never-chosen look identical to not-answered.

nodes.name: sortLibrary
nodes.summary: Applies the chosen ordering while keeping entries that have no value for it at the bottom in both directions. The obvious compareBy-on-null flag is wrong because reversing the comparator reverses the flag too, so a descending Score sort opened on the unrated titles - indistinguishable from a list of favourites.

nodes.name: filterLibrary
nodes.summary: Narrows entries by media type, status bucket and search text in one predicate. Favourites is a membership test against the profile's own id set rather than a status match, because AniList models a favourite as its own connection - which is also what stops a removed favourite still appearing under Favourites.

nodes.name: toggleSort
nodes.summary: Re-tapping the active sort flips its direction, and a sort with no direction hands over to A-Z instead of visibly ignoring the tap. Entering Score and Recently updated opens descending, because the first thing a descending list shows would otherwise be the entry the reader liked least or has not touched in years.

nodes.name: selectSort
nodes.summary: The direction a sort opens in when its chip is newly selected, deliberately separate from toggleSort. Both used to be one function called with the current sort for every chip, so pressing Score while List order was active selected A-Z - the chip pressed and the sort applied were different controls.

nodes.name: libraryProgressLabel
nodes.summary: Formats the poster's progress badge as Ep or Ch, falling back to the total for a completed entry whose progress AniList left null, and switching to a percentage for a rewatch. Without those two branches the badge vanished exactly when a show was finished, and said 24/24 for somebody on episode 3 of a rewatch.

nodes.name: libraryCounts
nodes.summary: Counts entries per filter chip over the unfiltered scope, so narrowing the list never makes Completed (0) appear for a bucket that is merely excluded. A count that shrank would read as a statement about the account rather than about the current filter.

nodes.name: UserProfileScreen
nodes.summary: Assembles the profile page: observes the overview, activity, comments, likers, social and detail-host flows, draws the top bar with the tier-list trophy gated on isOwnProfile, and hosts the tabs plus every sheet as a sibling of the tab content. The sheet placement is the point - a ModalBottomSheet drawn inside a tab is disposed with it.

nodes.name: profileListPadding
nodes.summary: The padding every tab's scrollable content uses: the scaffold's top plus the app's main-bar clearance, but only on the profile the bar actually floats over, plus the device's real navigation-bar inset read at draw time. A hardcoded bottom inset either wastes space or leaves the last row under the bar, and produces the bounce-back snap when the list reaches its end.

nodes.name: ProfileTabsContent
nodes.summary: Draws the tab capsule, the expandable refresh bar and the AnimatedContent switch over the four tabs. It hoists all four scroll states and the Stats section choice above the animation because the outgoing tab is disposed when its transition finishes, which used to drop the reader at the top of a long feed on every return.

nodes.name: UserOverviewViewModel
nodes.summary: Loads one profile as two concurrent requests - overview published first, the chunked anime list merged in when it lands - and builds the single Success state that Home, Stats and the Library page all read. It threads the user id through rather than looking it up, because the repository keys lists under user:<id> for a signed-in viewer and re-downloading by name would repeat the most expensive query in the app.
nodes.languageNotes: load() paints the last saved snapshot before the first request unless forceRefresh is set, cancels the list fetch when the overview fails, and keeps a live page rather than a failure page when a refresh fails - except on INVALID_SESSION, which a saved copy may not hide.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: The two-request pipeline: cancel the previous job, paint the disk snapshot, run the overview and the list as siblings, publish the overview alone so the bio renders while the tallies are still counting, then merge the list - or the saved one, carrying the failure message - into the final state.

nodes.name: loadMediaCovers
nodes.summary: Fetches cover art for every AniList link in the bio as one batched request, called as soon as the overview is published rather than after the list download. It clears the map before the early returns, because a refresh after the links were removed used to leave the old covers published and an in-flight request could still overwrite them.

nodes.name: loadMangaLibrary
nodes.summary: Fetches the manga half of the Library page exactly once, guarded rather than idempotent because the trigger is a filter chip a tapper will hit repeatedly and each tap would otherwise spend one of AniList's 30-a-minute requests. A failure leaves the list null so the chip stays a retry rather than becoming an empty answer.

nodes.name: flattenLibrary
nodes.summary: Flattens the per-status list groups into one sequence de-duplicated by media id. AniList can return the same title in more than one status group and a custom list can overlap the standard ones, and the Library grid is keyed on the media id - a repeated key throws IllegalArgumentException while it lays out, so this is a crash guard rather than tidying.

nodes.name: distinctById
nodes.summary: Drops repeated entries from an AniList favourites connection, first occurrence winning. A captured response really did return six favourited anime as six copies of the same media, and the favourites rows are LazyRows keyed on the media id - so one person's favourites would crash the screen on a device. Internal so the test can exercise the real function.

nodes.name: Factory
nodes.summary: The ViewModelProvider.Factory that lets ProfileDestination build one overview ViewModel per profile identity, so two profiles opened in sequence do not share the first one's bio and favourites.

nodes.name: AniListRepository
nodes.summary: The single read/write contract for AniList: viewer and profile lookups, lists (anime, manga, by id or by name), on-demand detail, studio, character and staff pages, list-entry writes, the activity feed with its comments and likes, and the TTL-free lastKnown* snapshots used for first paint and for failure fallbacks. forceRefresh exists on the list and overview reads because pull-to-refresh through a cache is a gesture that silently does nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: Every member a double cannot serve defaults to unsupported(), which throws; the sole exception is getActivityLikes, whose answer is still useful without a session so it degrades to an empty list.

nodes.name: unsupported
nodes.summary: The default body for a read an implementation does not serve. It throws rather than returning an empty list because an empty activity feed and a failed one look identical on screen, so a silent default would turn does-not-answer into this-person-has-done-nothing - the one claim the profile must never make about somebody.

nodes.name: ProfileActivityTab
nodes.summary: The Activity tab: loads the first page on first composition, pages six rows from the end, and draws the calendar, the feed of activity cards, the skeleton, the empty orb and a retry row. Deliberately draws no comment or likers sheet - those live in UserProfileScreen so they are not disposed with this tab.

nodes.name: ActivityPagingRetry
nodes.summary: A tappable retry row for a page that failed, drawn before the hasMore check because hasMore is still true after a failure and a plain spinner would sit under a feed that has silently stopped growing. The only previous way to retry was scrolling seven rows away and back, which nobody would guess.

nodes.name: ProfileRoutes
nodes.summary: The three profile routes plus the widget's tab request. BY_ID is separate from BY_USERNAME because the activity feed and both social lists are addressable only by id, so a profile opened from the Social grid would otherwise pay a name lookup on the screen where the user is tapping fastest; the tab is an optional query argument rather than a second destination so navigate(OWN) cannot drift.

nodes.name: ProfileDestination
nodes.summary: Builds the three per-profile ViewModels under one identity key, derives the entry editor from viewerId, and forwards navigation intents as callbacks so UserProfileScreen never holds a NavController. Follower taps use navigateSingle because a grid of faces is where a thumb lands twice and stacked duplicate profiles made Back look broken.

nodes.name: BuildListEntryInsightsUseCase
nodes.summary: Turns one media list collection into the country, release-year, watch-year and episode-band tallies the Stats tab charts. Only entries with a status are counted, matching AniList's own aggregates, and the episode bands are fixed and ordered so the chart reads as a scale rather than a second copy of the Format chart.
nodes.languageNotes: Share is normalised against the largest bucket rather than the total, and a pre-2000 year keeps its full form because '19 is otherwise both 1999 and 2019.

nodes.name: ListEntryInsights
nodes.summary: The use case's result: four tallied distributions plus the count of entries with no episode figure at all, which land in no band and are reported separately rather than being dropped or counted as zero.

nodes.name: episodeBuckets
nodes.summary: Bands episodes per show so a movie, a two-cour, a standard season and a long runner land in four different rows, with 29+ kept rather than dropped because a 40-episode show is somebody's most-watched title. An entry with no episode count is counted separately instead of being forced into the first band.

nodes.name: PlanningAddStore
nodes.summary: Owns the per-media quick-add state and performs the write: the in-flight flags, the confirmation and the error, keyed by media id. A second tap while the first is on the wire is dropped, because AniList would accept both writes and spend two requests reaching the same state.

nodes.name: QuickAddStatus
nodes.summary: One title's add-control state, carrying the error as a field rather than as a snackbar event so a failed write on the Library or a studio page - which have no SnackbarHostState - still says so under the button that caused it.

nodes.name: PlanningAddHost
nodes.summary: The slice of the store a screen needs - the status flow and the two add callbacks - so the components package can draw the action row without knowing how a write is routed. Mirrors MediaDetailHost, one owner per screen.

nodes.name: rememberPlanningAddHost
nodes.summary: Remembering a host with its own SupervisorJob scope so a write outlives the sheet that started it, cancelled on dispose so a request for a screen the reader has left does not continue. canWrite is a remember key because a session change must not leave a signed-out host serving added flags to the account that signs in behind it.

nodes.name: PersonProfileHost
nodes.summary: Carries the character and staff callbacks for the detail sheet and draws the person-profile sheet as a sibling of that sheet, because a ModalBottomSheet is its own window and one drawn from inside another covers it. Callbacks are null when the host has no repository so cast rows render as captions rather than as controls that could only fail.

nodes.name: Sheet
nodes.summary: Draws the person-profile sheet when one is open, comparing against Closed rather than null-checking because the state is non-nullable and Closed already means nobody is looking. A tap on the titles row closes this sheet first and only then hands the appearance to the host, so the new page is not covered by a window belonging to the old one.

nodes.name: rememberPersonProfileHost
nodes.summary: Remembers a person-profile store for the composition and disposes it when the host leaves. A null repository is the documented way to say this host cannot open profiles at all, which the host turns into null callbacks rather than into a handler that always fails.

nodes.name: ProfileAvatarButton
nodes.summary: The avatar control that opens the reader's own profile from both the dashboard top bar and the Library page. It answers to tap and to hold, draws its own press spring so it does not read as a different kind of control from the IconButtons beside it, and sets Role.Button plus a content description by hand because the hold gesture is a pointer handler rather than a clickable.

nodes.name: AppNavigation.kt
nodes.summary: The app's single navigation graph and its composition root: it builds every application-scoped DataStore reader, the AniList repository and the detail-sheet host once, then routes login, demo, dashboard, profile, library, studio, tier list and settings. Most of its comments record failures it fixes - picking a start destination before the stored session is read showed a login screen on every cold start, and constructing DashboardViewModel while unauthenticated issued a viewer query with no Authorization header that then stuck as "Session expired".
nodes.languageNotes: A single @Composable holding the NavHost; preferences objects are `remember(context)`-scoped so one DataStore reader exists per process, and route transitions reuse ExpressiveMotion tokens instead of local springs.

nodes.name: AppRoutes
nodes.summary: String constants for the top-level destinations, plus the builder for the parameterised dashboard_user route. Keeping them in one object is what stops the login, demo and scanned-profile entry points from each spelling a route differently.

nodes.name: AppNavigation
nodes.summary: Draws the NavHost, the floating main bar and the joke toast host, and reacts to auth-state changes by navigating between login and dashboard. It holds the splash while the stored session is still unknown rather than guessing a destination, and defers the widget's profile-activity request until an identity exists.

nodes.name: WidgetSync
nodes.summary: Pushes the live dashboard counts into the home-screen widgets. Hoisted into its own composable because inlining it put a read of `uiState` in the app root, so every character typed into the dashboard search box recomposed the NavHost, the bar and the toast; it is keyed on the rendered values rather than the state object for the same reason.

nodes.name: InfoSettingsTab.kt
nodes.summary: The Settings > Info tab: profile card or demo notice, list snapshot, the AniList connection probe, build/version facts, the update card, "What's new" from the bundled changelog and the sign-in/sign-out action. The privacy copy lives here because saying which two hosts the app contacts is the only privacy policy a no-telemetry app can actually show.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads the newest changelog block rather than looking up BuildConfig.VERSION_NAME, because the release workflow advances the patch number after the notes are written.

nodes.name: InfoSettingsTab
nodes.summary: Lays out the Info tab as a stack of cards and decides, from whether a viewer exists, between the signed-in profile card and the read-only demo explanation. Every optional input has a safe default so previews and demo builds render without a repository or a session.

nodes.name: ConnectionSection
nodes.summary: The "AniList connection" card and the dialog it opens. Extracted so one probe instance is shared by the row and the dialog - two probes would let a Check tap disagree with the row that opened it - and so the tab itself stays a layout.

nodes.name: ChangelogSectionCard
nodes.summary: Renders the "What's new" card from the newest changelog block. The empty case is handled as normal rather than as an error, because a build between releases can carry notes for a version it has not shipped and the card still has to say something.

nodes.name: AuthViewModel.kt
nodes.summary: Owns the AniList session: restores a stored token, handles the OAuth redirect and pasted tokens, verifies a new token against AniList before believing it, and signs out. Its states encode the distinction between "not known yet" and "signed out", which is what stopped a login screen appearing on every cold start and after every browser round trip.
nodes.languageNotes: A @Volatile `hasHandledRedirect` flag lets an OAuth callback win a race against the asynchronous stored-token read instead of being overwritten by it.

nodes.name: AuthUiState
nodes.summary: The sealed auth state. `Restoring` exists separately from `Loading` because "the stored session has not been read yet" is not the same as "we know who you are and are acting on it"; conflating them made the navigation graph fall through to the login branch on every launch.

nodes.name: AuthViewModel
nodes.summary: Holds `uiState` and the client id as StateFlows and drives the whole sign-in lifecycle. The AniList repository is optional so callers that only have the token store can still construct it, at the cost of storing a token unverified.

nodes.name: checkCurrentAuth
nodes.summary: Reads the stored client id and token once and settles the initial state. It bails out if a redirect has already been handled, because otherwise the disk read could write Unauthenticated after the callback wrote Authenticated and silently drop a successful sign-in.

nodes.name: handleAuthRedirect
nodes.summary: Classifies the deep link AniList redirects to: a success stores the token, a cancelled consent screen gets a plain sentence instead of an alarming error, and a plain launcher start is not treated as a failed callback (which used to surface "No access token found in redirect" on a normal cold start).

nodes.name: saveToken
nodes.summary: Normalises whatever the user pasted, clears the previous session's caches so a stale viewer snapshot cannot vouch for a new token, saves it, then asks AniList for the viewer and undoes the save if the answer is INVALID_SESSION. Storing an unverified token is what used to produce a dashboard that said "Session expired" for a session that never worked.

nodes.name: dismissAuthError
nodes.summary: Moves an `Error` state back to `Unauthenticated` and only ever away from `Error`. Error used to be terminal while the sign-in card disabled its connect button on error, so backing out of AniList's consent screen left no way to retry without killing the process.

nodes.name: LoginScreen.kt
nodes.summary: The unauthenticated entry screen: hero, a two-tab bar switching between the OAuth card and username scanning, the client-id and manual-token dialogs, and the demo entry point. Tab selection and the typed username are saveable because the tabs live in an AnimatedContent that disposes the tab it animates away from, which used to wipe a half-typed username and the chosen tab on rotation.
nodes.languageNotes: The demo button shares one MutableInteractionSource with `bouncyPress` so the press comes from the button's own clickable and cancels when the gesture becomes a scroll.

nodes.name: LoginScreen
nodes.summary: Builds the login scaffold and routes the two tabs to OAuthCard or UsernameScanCard, remembering the authorization URL per client id so a crossfade does not rebuild it. The demo caption underneath spells out what "sample data" actually opens, because the button alone read as a test fixture.

nodes.name: RefreshIntervalPreferences.kt
nodes.summary: Makes the saved-list cache window a user setting and supplies the pure staleness arithmetic both the foreground check and the background timer use. It exists because the list used to be cached for a flat hour with nothing observing the app returning to the foreground, so finishing a title elsewhere produced the same dashboard until the hour elapsed.
nodes.languageNotes: A Flow for the setting plus a @Volatile plain mirror, because the repository's non-suspend cache lookup cannot read DataStore; the mirror is updated inside `onEach` on the same emission that reports the value.

nodes.name: RefreshInterval
nodes.summary: The selectable cache windows, each carrying its storage string and staleness threshold. MANUAL_ONLY is modelled as an interval no clock can outgrow (Long.MAX_VALUE) so every comparison needs no special case; unknown stored values fall back to the default rather than throwing, because the preferences file outlives the build that wrote it.

nodes.name: isRefreshDue
nodes.summary: Decides whether a list loaded at a given time is stale, taking the clock as an argument so the boundary is testable. A negative age (the wall clock moved backwards) counts as due, because treating it as "not yet" would pin the cached list for as long as the clock stayed behind.

nodes.name: millisUntilRefreshDue
nodes.summary: Returns how long a background timer should sleep, or null for ALWAYS and MANUAL_ONLY because both are decided by the foreground check alone. Scheduling ALWAYS on a loop would re-fetch continuously, since a zero interval is due the instant it is measured.

nodes.name: RefreshIntervalPreferences
nodes.summary: The DataStore-backed store for the chosen refresh interval, plus the plain `currentStalenessMillis()` the repository reads. The mirror exists because the obvious alternatives are worse: runBlocking on the main thread is a deadlock waiting for AniList, and making the repository suspend would push a DataStore read onto every list lookup the cache is meant to avoid.

nodes.name: SettingsButton.kt
nodes.summary: The single button component every Settings action is drawn with. Settings had five hand-written buttons across three files at heights of 50, 48 and the Material default, with mismatched corners and 14/16/18dp icons; one component with one height and one corner radius makes the emphasis a variant instead of an accident of which file a button was written in.
nodes.languageNotes: Explicit disabled container/content colours, because M3's 12% surface overlay disappears against a surfaceContainerLow card and a disabled button reads as a rendering bug.

nodes.name: SettingsButtonVariant
nodes.summary: The four emphasis levels a settings action can carry - filled for the section's main action, tonal for a peer, outlined for something the user may decline, text for a link or a repeatable action. It replaces per-file styling as the thing that expresses hierarchy.

nodes.name: SettingsButton
nodes.summary: Draws one of the four Material button types at a fixed 48dp (40dp for text links), with an 18dp icon slot and an optional explicit test tag so restyling cannot silently detach an existing test. The press effect shares one interaction source with the button's own clickable so starting a drag does not leave it squashed.

nodes.name: AniSequelWidgetProvider.kt
nodes.summary: The profile-activity home-screen widget: the viewer's avatar, handle and latest entry, opening the app on the profile's Activity tab. It extends AppWidgetProvider directly because a former forwarding receiver read EXTRA_APPWIDGET_ID while the system sends EXTRA_APPWIDGET_IDS, so no update was ever applied to a freshly added widget.
nodes.languageNotes: `onReceive` calls `super` first for the synchronous placeholder paint, then uses `goAsync()` so the process survives the cover fetch that replaces it.

nodes.name: AniSequelWidgetProvider
nodes.summary: The manifest-registered receiver for the activity widget. It also exposes `updateAll` for the app to call after it knows a count moved, since the platform cannot be told before its next scheduled broadcast.

nodes.name: renderWidget
nodes.summary: Builds the RemoteViews for the activity tile, hiding the title and handle when there is nothing to name and falling back to a transparent placeholder cover. The fallback is deliberately not the app name, which read as a headline for a show nobody could have watched.

nodes.name: openActivityPendingIntent
nodes.summary: Builds the tap target that opens MainActivity with the profile-activity extra. It uses request code 0 and no instance-specific data so all copies of the widget share one PendingIntent; passing the widget id (as it once did) made N widgets hold N intents for the same destination.

nodes.name: FeaturedSequelWidgetProvider.kt
nodes.summary: The large "Featured Sequel" widget: the top missed sequel as a poster, what it is a sequel to, and how many are waiting, so the decision to open the app can be made from the home screen. Its update path and `goAsync()` cover fetch are shared with the other providers through WidgetUpdater.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses request code 3 so its PendingIntent is distinct from the three older widgets even though all point at the dashboard.

nodes.name: FeaturedSequelWidgetProvider
nodes.summary: The manifest-registered receiver for the featured-sequel tile, plus the `updateAll` entry the app calls after a dashboard recompute changes the top recommendation.

nodes.name: renderWidget
nodes.summary: Builds the poster tile, dropping the parent line entirely when there is nothing the recommendation is a sequel to - the placeholder string would have rendered as a sentence with its subject missing. The placeholder cover uses the entry's stored dominant colour.

nodes.name: ArrivingSequelsWidgetProvider.kt
nodes.summary: The "arriving soon" widget: count of airing/upcoming sequels, the first one's poster and title, and the viewer's handle. Tapping it just opens the app, because the dashboard is the start destination and already shows the arriving section at the top - the deep-link extra it used to carry was never read.
nodes.languageNotes: The PendingIntent deliberately carries no extra; the removed EXTRA_WIDGET_OPEN_ARRIVING documented a deep link that did not exist.

nodes.name: ArrivingSequelsWidgetProvider
nodes.summary: The manifest-registered receiver for the arriving-sequels tile, plus `updateAll` for app-initiated refreshes of every placed instance.

nodes.name: renderWidget
nodes.summary: Builds the arriving tile, hiding the title when nothing is arriving rather than letting the app name stand in for a show that is not coming.

nodes.name: TokenCipher.kt
nodes.summary: Encrypts the AniList bearer token at rest, because a plaintext token in DataStore is a credential for the reader's whole account and anything able to read the app's private directory could lift it. The key is an AES-256 keystore key rather than one derived from a password, since there is no password to derive from and a stolen-then-reset phone should invalidate it.
nodes.languageNotes: Stored form is `base64(iv):base64(ciphertext)`; a fresh IV per encryption is mandatory for GCM. Decryption failures return null and delete the unusable key so the next save can create a fresh one.

nodes.name: TokenCipher
nodes.summary: The two-method contract for token encryption, with `decrypt` returning null rather than throwing so an invalidated key becomes "no usable session" instead of a crash on every launch.

nodes.name: KeystoreTokenCipher
nodes.summary: The AndroidKeyStore implementation: AES/GCM/NoPadding under a non-exportable 256-bit key that is hardware-backed where supported and invalidated when the device's secure lock is removed. Any decrypt failure forgets the key so the install is not stuck failing every write.

nodes.name: UsernameScanCard.kt
nodes.summary: The read-only "scan any public profile" card on the login screen: a username field and a scan button that needs no session. The typed value is hoisted to the caller so it survives the tab crossfade that disposes this card.
nodes.languageNotes: Shares one MutableInteractionSource with `bouncyPress` so beginning a scroll on the button cancels the press instead of leaving it visibly squashed.

nodes.name: UsernameScanCard
nodes.summary: Renders the scan card and only fires the scan callback for a non-blank trimmed username, which is what keeps a stray tap from opening an empty profile dashboard.

nodes.name: RateLimitNotice.kt
nodes.summary: The app-wide channel that turns an HTTP 429 into one visible notice. A rate limit used to reach the UI only as a per-screen error, so a detail sheet offered a retry button while nothing said retrying immediately was guaranteed to fail; MainActivity collects this flow and shows one toast wherever the request came from.
nodes.languageNotes: Check-and-record happens in one synchronized block because reports arrive on OkHttp worker threads; the clock is a parameter so the dedupe window is testable without sleeping.

nodes.name: RateLimitNotice
nodes.summary: Process-wide singleton holding the deduplicated notice flow. A 20-second window collapses the burst of parallel 429s one screen produces into a single message, so "wait a minute" does not become the noise the reader is trying to get past.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Raises a notice unless one was accepted within the dedupe window, emitting the server's Retry-After seconds (or null when it gave none). Only accepted reports move the timestamp - otherwise a user retrying once a second would push the window forward forever and the notice would never appear.

nodes.name: AppLockPreferences.kt
nodes.summary: Stores whether the app asks for the device's biometric or PIN before showing the reader's list. It is off by default because a lock nobody asked for is a wall between someone and their own data, and there is deliberately no "unlocked" flag - a lock that survived a process restart would let a once-unlocked phone stay unlocked forever.
nodes.languageNotes: A single booleanPreferencesKey behind a Flow; the class comment records why the absent unlocked-flag is a decision rather than an omission.

nodes.name: AppLockPreferences
nodes.summary: Reads and writes the app-lock toggle. Settings writes it and MainActivity reads the same DataStore to decide whether to draw the gate, so the switch and the lock cannot disagree about whether the feature is on.

nodes.name: AniSequelApplication.kt
nodes.summary: The Application subclass: supplies Coil with the app's tuned ImageLoader so a wall of posters does not re-download cover art on every scroll back, and owns the single process-wide auth repository. The repository used to be built in MainActivity.onCreate, so each rotation produced a second one whose token cache and DataStore reader disagreed with the retained ViewModel.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements ImageLoaderFactory and lazily constructs AuthRepositoryImpl once per process.

nodes.name: AniSequelApplication
nodes.summary: Process entry point that exposes `authRepository` and `newImageLoader()`. Making the repository application-scoped is what keeps the token cache, the DataStore instance and NetworkClient's per-repository service cache consistent across configuration changes.

nodes.name: AuthRepository.kt
nodes.summary: The session-storage contract: token and client-id flows, the synchronous in-memory token the auth interceptor reads without touching disk, and the save/clear calls. The comment on `cachedAccessToken` states the invariant that matters - after a clear it must be null, or a revoked token keeps being sent with every request.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately has one non-suspend accessor so the OkHttp interceptor can attach a token without blocking on DataStore.

nodes.name: AuthRepository
nodes.summary: Interface every auth consumer depends on, so the ViewModel, the network client and tests can share one session store without knowing it is DataStore plus an encrypted token.

nodes.name: MainActivity.kt
nodes.summary: The app's only Activity: hosts the Compose tree, owns the optional app-lock gate, routes the anisequel://oauth deep link into the auth ViewModel, hands onResume to the updater and passes the widget's profile-tab request into the composition. Most of the code is about ordering the framework does not give for free - read the lock preference before drawing the navigation tree, arm the gate in onStop rather than onPause, and keep FLAG_SECURE set for as long as the preference is on.
nodes.languageNotes: Compose state (`mutableStateOf`) for the lock and widget flags because both are read during composition; the process-scoped UpdateController is held through a WeakReference so a rotated-away Activity cannot be kept alive by it.

nodes.name: MainActivity
nodes.summary: Wires the whole app: builds the auth repository, the theme and lock preferences and the auth ViewModel, then draws AniSequelTheme, AppLockGate and AppNavigation in that order. Also decides when the lock arms (onStop, not onPause) and when the updater may draw a dialog over the lock.
nodes.languageNotes: Declared `singleTask` in the manifest, which is why the widget's second tap arrives through onNewIntent and never through onCreate.

nodes.name: AppLockStateViewModel
nodes.summary: Holds exactly one flag, `unlockedSinceLaunch`, so the unlocked state survives a configuration change but not process death. A plain field on the Activity re-armed the gate on every rotation, so the reader unlocked, rotated and was asked again; a ViewModel dies with the process, so a cold start is still locked.

nodes.name: requestUnlock
nodes.summary: Shows the platform BiometricPrompt with BIOMETRIC_WEAK or DEVICE_CREDENTIAL and clears the gate on success. androidx.biometric is deliberately not a dependency because minSdk 31 already has setAllowedAuthenticators. Fails open when the device has no secure lock, and clears `biometricPromptVisible` in a catch so a prompt that cannot be shown does not leave the Unlock button dead until the Activity is recreated.
nodes.languageNotes: The visible-prompt flag exists because a credential prompt can stop the Activity on some OEMs, and the resulting onStop would otherwise re-lock the app mid-authentication.

nodes.name: applySecureFlag
nodes.summary: Adds or clears WindowManager FLAG_SECURE from the stored lock preference rather than from the gate being visible. The system snapshots the recents thumbnail as the task leaves the foreground, so a flag added in onStop can arrive after the snapshot; the accepted cost is that the reader cannot screenshot their own list while the lock is on.

nodes.name: handleDeepLinkIntent
nodes.summary: Forwards an anisequel://oauth intent to AuthViewModel. Called from onCreate only when savedInstanceState is null, and from onNewIntent otherwise: the Intent stays attached to the Activity, so a rotation used to replay the same callback and re-save the same token, or re-show the same error.

nodes.name: EditSettingsTab.kt
nodes.summary: The Settings > Edit tab: AniList Client ID, list refresh interval, the dashboard's arriving-row knobs, the app lock, and a Sign out that really signs out. Each card is here because a specific behaviour was wrong - a flat one-hour list cache, a dead-end sign-in error, a Save button that looked disabled - and the KDoc records which.
nodes.languageNotes: Every control animates on the shared tokens in ExpressiveMotion; the refresh chips are a FlowRow rather than a segmented bar because five unequal labels clip in equal halves.

nodes.name: EditSettingsTab
nodes.summary: Composes the Edit tab's cards and the sign-in/out button. The button used to only navigate back, so the sign-out button signed the user out of nothing and left them authenticated one screen away; it now calls logout when the state is Authenticated.

nodes.name: ListRefreshCard
nodes.summary: Lets the reader pick how stale the cached list may be before it is re-read on return to the foreground. The setting exists because of a bug: nothing watched for the app resuming and the list was cached for a flat hour, so closing and reopening showed an identical dashboard until the refresh button was tapped.
nodes.languageNotes: The reset button appears through AnimatedVisibility keyed on FastSpatialSize rather than the Int token, because expandVertically is typed on FiniteAnimationSpec<IntSize>.

nodes.name: ArrivingSectionCard
nodes.summary: The two dashboard switches for the airing and upcoming rows. Hiding and compacting answer different questions: hiding removes the section and every poster load on the path to search, while compact keeps the information in artwork-free rows. Compact is disabled while the section is hidden, where it would mean nothing.

nodes.name: AppLockCard
nodes.summary: The app-lock switch, disabled with the reason written into its subtitle when the device has no secure lock. The platform credential prompt has nothing to ask for without one, and offering a switch that would silently fail open is the worse version of the same truth.

nodes.name: RefreshIntervalChip
nodes.summary: One interval pill. Container, label, border colour and border width animate on the shared springs because the control used to be four `if (selected)` reads and snapped while everything around it travelled.
nodes.languageNotes: Border width rides the spatial curve and colours ride the colour-effects curve: a width is geometry.

nodes.name: ClientIdEditor
nodes.summary: The Client ID field with its Use default and Save actions. Three faults are fixed here and recorded in the KDoc: an OutlinedTextField label notched the top stroke into the label text, Arrangement.End left Save looking disabled, and a second developer-clients link duplicated the one RedirectUrlHint already offers.
nodes.languageNotes: A non-numeric value is surfaced as an error rather than accepted, because AniList Client IDs are numbers and a rejected one fails at the authorize step instead of here.

nodes.name: SnapshotStore.kt
nodes.summary: The disk tier under the repository's in-memory caches. Without it every cache lived for exactly one process, so a kill - including Android reclaiming the app while the user signed in through the browser - re-bought the whole list, the viewer profile and every opened title from AniList. A file is never trusted: a parse failure, a model change or another release's format tag is a miss and the file is deleted.
nodes.languageNotes: One Mutex serialises reads and writes; JSON encode and decode run on Dispatchers.IO because a completed list is multi-megabyte and the read sits on the cold-start path.

nodes.name: SnapshotStore
nodes.summary: Keeps one JSON file per `kind`, keyed by an arbitrary string, bounded to MAX_BYTES_PER_KIND per kind and written atomically through a temp file and a rename. A value read back is returned with the moment it was written, so reading a snapshot never extends its own life.
nodes.languageNotes: `formatTag` (the release version code) and `nowMillis` are constructor-injected so a test can prove that a snapshot from another release is a miss and can move the clock without sleeping.

nodes.name: SnapshotFile
nodes.summary: The on-disk envelope: layout schema version, the release that wrote it, and the entries. Each payload is the value's own JSON kept as a string, so the file's shape cannot depend on the shape of any model and a stored snapshot either parses into today's model or is a miss.

nodes.name: AniListSnapshots
nodes.summary: The one SnapshotStore for the process. Two repositories exist in the running app - the auth ViewModel's and the dashboards' - and two stores would each hold a parsed copy of the same file, so the copy that did not just clear would re-persist the signed-out person's list on its next write.
nodes.languageNotes: Holds a File derived from the application context, never the context itself, so it cannot leak an Activity.

nodes.name: read
nodes.summary: Returns the stored value with its write timestamp, or null when absent, older than the caller's ttl, or unparseable into the requested type. An unparseable payload is dropped rather than left, because those bytes will never parse and would buy a file read per open to answer the same no.
nodes.languageNotes: A ttl of Long.MAX_VALUE is the repository's "manual only" case - an interval no elapsed clock reaches, so no special case is needed here.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Stores one value under a key and rewrites that kind. The caller may pass `storedAtMillis` so the repository stamps its memory cache and the disk copy with one clock reading and the two can never disagree about the age of the same answer.

nodes.name: writeAll
nodes.summary: One file rewrite for many entries. Cover fetches arrive a dozen at a time for one bio, and storing them one by one would re-serialise and re-write the whole kind a dozen times for one screen.

nodes.name: removeKind
nodes.summary: Drops a kind from memory and disk, which is what a mutation calls. Leaving the pre-mutation copy on disk would have the next lookup resurrect exactly the stale list the mutation was supposed to invalidate.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads one kind's file and rejects it wholesale when it cannot be parsed or when its schema or format tag is not this build's, deleting the file so the next launch does not pay for the same parse to reach the same answer. The app version is part of the key because a file from the previous release can parse into today's models and still be missing a field the new query asks for.

nodes.name: NetworkClient.kt
nodes.summary: The single place HTTP clients are built: one memoised Retrofit service for the AniList GraphQL endpoint, one process-wide Moshi shared with the snapshot store, and one Coil image loader tuned for a wall of posters. The memoisation exists because the app used to build two full client stacks per launch, paying for two connection pools, two dispatcher pools and a second TLS handshake on a cold start.
nodes.languageNotes: No KotlinJsonAdapterFactory: every data model is @JsonClass(generateAdapter = true), so the reflective factory - and kotlin-reflect under R8 - was dead weight.

nodes.name: NetworkClient
nodes.summary: Owns the process-wide Moshi, the cached API service and the image loader. The service cache is keyed on repository identity, not merely non-nullness, because the service is bound to the AuthInterceptor that reads that repository's token.

nodes.name: createApiService
nodes.summary: Returns the cached service when it was built for the same repository identity, otherwise evicts the previous client's connections and shuts its dispatcher down before replacing it - a superseded client would otherwise leak its thread pool and keep-alive sockets for the whole session.
nodes.languageNotes: Double-checked on a plain `Any` lock with @Volatile fields, because the fast path runs from the composition on every launch.

nodes.name: buildApiService
nodes.summary: Assembles the OkHttp and Retrofit stack: RateLimitInterceptor installed before AuthInterceptor so a retried request is re-authorised, a 90-second call timeout because readTimeout resets on every arriving byte, a 60-second keep-alive for the dashboard's bursts, 16 max requests against a per-account limiter, and body logging only in debug with the Authorization header redacted.
nodes.languageNotes: The interceptor order is load-bearing: the two addInterceptor calls used to be reversed, so the rate-limit retry proceeded down the chain and never passed through AuthInterceptor again.

nodes.name: createImageLoader
nodes.summary: Builds the Coil loader every poster goes through: a quarter-heap memory cache, a 128 MB disk cache, no crossfade, and a 16-per-host dispatcher because OkHttp's default of 5 is below a single relation row's card count - which is the literal "covers take ages to appear" case.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses ImageDecoderDecoder unconditionally: minSdk 31 makes the old API-28 guard and its GifDecoder fallback unreachable, and coil-gif has to stay because both decoders live in that one artifact.

nodes.name: OAuthCard.kt
nodes.summary: The sign-in card: what the connection gives you, an error banner, the Connect AniList Account button and the Paste Token / Client ID escapes. The button is deliberately never disabled by an error state - declining AniList's consent screen used to leave the only control that could restart the flow unusable, making a failed sign-in a dead end.
nodes.languageNotes: Each pressed control is given its own MutableInteractionSource so bouncyPress sees the press cancelled when the scrolling column claims a drag, instead of squashing through the whole drag.

nodes.name: OAuthCard
nodes.summary: Draws the login card and clears the previous error before opening the browser, because the banner describes a past attempt and must not outlive it. Shows a loading indicator in place of the button while the callback is being processed.

nodes.name: openCustomTab
nodes.summary: Opens the authorize URL in a Custom Tab and falls back to a plain ACTION_VIEW intent when the Custom Tabs intent cannot be launched, so a device without a supporting browser is not left with no way to sign in.

nodes.name: AuthRepositoryImpl.kt
nodes.summary: DataStore-backed session storage: the bearer token is encrypted through the keystore before it is written, a plaintext token left by an older build is migrated once, a ciphertext the current keystore cannot decrypt is removed, and an in-memory mirror keeps AuthInterceptor from blocking an OkHttp thread on disk for every request.
nodes.languageNotes: The token cipher is constructor-injected so the migration and invalidation paths can be tested on the JVM, where there is no AndroidKeyStore.

nodes.name: AuthRepositoryImpl
nodes.summary: The only implementation of AuthRepository, created once in MainActivity.onCreate. Also owns DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID, this app's own AniList developer client: authorizing against anyone else's id delivers the token to their app and sign-in can never complete.
nodes.languageNotes: `cachedToken` is written by an onEach on accessTokenFlow as well as by every write, so a cleared token cannot be handed out again even if a collector misses the change.

nodes.name: prepareStoredToken
nodes.summary: The one-shot plaintext migration and the keystore-invalidation recovery. A legacy token is encrypted and removed in a single transaction; if encryption fails it is left in place and still served, because losing a working session is worse than the plaintext that was already there. An undecryptable ciphertext is removed rather than retried, since retrying leaves the app permanently signed out and permanently writing failed decryptions.
nodes.languageNotes: The equality check inside the invalidation edit stops a concurrent sign-in's fresh token from being deleted by a stale read.

nodes.name: readToken
nodes.summary: Reads the encrypted token first and the legacy plaintext second. The fallback is not a second storage format the app ever writes - it keeps the session alive on the single launch where the migration could not encrypt.

nodes.name: SettingsScreen.kt
nodes.summary: The Settings scaffold and its three-tab host: Info, Theme and Edit behind an ExpressiveTabBar. Tabs cross over with fade and scale on the shared spring tokens, and the default SizeTransform is dropped on purpose - animating the container height while a leaving tab settled its own scroll is the shape the reported crash had.
nodes.languageNotes: The AnimatedContent transitionSpec keeps its brackets around the `togetherWith` halves because an infix call binds looser than `+`, and `using(null)` would otherwise attach to an ExitTransition.

nodes.name: SettingsScreen
nodes.summary: Hoists the selected tab in saveable state, draws the top bar and divider, and dispatches to the tab composables. Receives the reachability probe as a defaulted suspend lambda so previews and the demo route compile and report UNKNOWN instead of pretending the API is up.

nodes.name: AniListOAuth.kt
nodes.summary: The AniList OAuth contract in one place: the redirect URI that must match both the manifest intent filter and the AniList developer page, the implicit-grant authorize URL, redirect parsing and the recovery of a token from a sloppy paste. The KDoc exists because the failure mode is invisible - a wrong redirect URL sends the token to a web page and sign-in simply never completes.
nodes.languageNotes: The authorize URL carries only client_id and response_type: adding redirect_uri or state makes AniList answer unsupported_grant_type and reject the flow.

nodes.name: AniListOAuth
nodes.summary: Holds the redirect URI, authorize endpoint and developer settings URL, and the pure functions that build and read the OAuth exchange. Kept free of Android state so the parsing is testable.

nodes.name: authorizationUrl
nodes.summary: Builds the implicit-grant authorize URL from a client id. It deliberately sends no redirect_uri: AniList delivers the token to whatever URL is registered for the client, which is why REDIRECT_URI is documented to the user instead of transmitted.

nodes.name: parseRedirect
nodes.summary: Reads access_token or error out of the redirect, preferring the fragment and falling back to the query, and URL-decodes the values because tokens can contain `=` or `+`. Returns NoCallback for a launch that is not ours, which is what a launcher start looks like.

nodes.name: extractToken
nodes.summary: Recovers a usable token from anything the user pasted - a bare token, `access_token=...`, the whole redirect fragment or URL, quotes, a `Bearer ` prefix. Every form stored verbatim is a token AniList rejects, which surfaced as "Session expired" for a session that was never invalid. Prose is rejected rather than trimmed at its first space, because "I think it worked?" would otherwise be stored as "I".
nodes.languageNotes: Splits on the first '=' only, since '=' is also base64 padding and splitting on all of them silently truncated tokens.

nodes.name: RedirectResult
nodes.summary: The three outcomes of an OAuth callback: Success with a token, Error with the code and description AniList supplied when consent was declined, and NoCallback for anything that is not our redirect.

nodes.name: AppLockGate.kt
nodes.summary: The curtain drawn over the whole navigation tree while the optional app lock is on. It is an app gate rather than a per-screen check because every route - deep link, widget intent, restored back stack - lands underneath one overlay, and the first screen that forgot a check would be a screenshot of someone's watch history.
nodes.languageNotes: The tree stays composed underneath (a lock is a curtain, not a restart) but its semantics are cleared while locked, since an accessibility service can traverse content hidden behind a sibling.

nodes.name: AppLockGate
nodes.summary: Draws the lock overlay and keeps the navigation tree alive beneath it. Swallows every pointer event that is not the Unlock button - an opaque Surface hid the tree but did not consume touches, so taps still reached live controls - and sends Back to the background instead of dismissing the gate.

nodes.name: ChangelogRepository.kt
nodes.summary: Reads the app's own release notes out of assets/changelog.json. The notes used to be a hardcoded list that went stale and was a third copy alongside the GitHub release body and update.json; the Info tab and the release workflow now read the same file, so the two consumers cannot drift.
nodes.languageNotes: Parsed synchronously on the calling thread and cached, because the asset is a few hundred bytes of local file read once per Info-tab composition.

nodes.name: ChangelogRepository
nodes.summary: Loads and caches the bundled changelog and answers the three questions its callers ask: the newest notes, the notes for a specific version, and the newest-first history. A missing or malformed asset degrades to an empty changelog instead of taking the Settings screen down.

nodes.name: Changelog
nodes.summary: The root of the asset: the list of version blocks the rest of the class reads.

nodes.name: ChangelogVersion
nodes.summary: One released version and the notes a user would want before updating. Every field is nullable because the file is hand-edited and shipped inside the APK: a malformed entry degrades to a version with no notes rather than throwing at read time.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Parses the asset once and keeps it for the life of the process, since a file-backed asset cannot change while the process lives and re-reading it per composition would repeat work already done.

nodes.name: latestWithNotes
nodes.summary: The newest block with usable notes - deliberately not the block matching BuildConfig.VERSION_NAME. The release workflow derives the version it publishes, advancing the patch past the newest published release, so no changelog can be written ahead of the number the build will use.

nodes.name: versionsWithNotes
nodes.summary: Newest-first versions that actually have notes, skipping empty blocks so the history never renders a heading with nothing under it.

nodes.name: MissedSequelsWidgetProvider.kt
nodes.summary: The home-screen widget for the missed-sequel count, the top entry's poster and title, and the viewer's handle. Artwork and state go through the shared WidgetUpdater, which is where goAsync() keeps the process alive across a cover download instead of letting the launcher kill it mid-update.
nodes.languageNotes: The click PendingIntent carries no routing extra: the dashboard is already the start destination, and an EXTRA_WIDGET_OPEN_DASHBOARD nobody read was removed rather than left as a false promise.

nodes.name: MissedSequelsWidgetProvider
nodes.summary: Hooks the widget lifecycle (onUpdate, onReceive) into WidgetUpdater, sharing the cover-fetch and render path with the other three providers. onReceive resolves its own ids when the broadcast carries none, so a provider refreshed by an explicit update is treated the same as one the launcher asked for.

nodes.name: updateAll
nodes.summary: Re-renders every instance of this provider, called when the data behind the widget changes rather than when the launcher asks, so a completed scan reaches the widget without waiting for the next refresh cycle.

nodes.name: renderWidget
nodes.summary: Builds the RemoteViews from the cached widget data, hiding the title and handle rows when there is nothing to name and substituting a colour-derived placeholder when no cover was fetched. Showing the app name in the title slot used to read as a headline for a show nobody was missing.

nodes.name: RedirectUrlHint.kt
nodes.summary: Spells out the exact Redirect URL the user has to register with AniList, next to a link to the developer page where it goes. Without it a wrong redirect fails invisibly: the token is delivered to a page that will not load and the app waits forever for a callback that never arrives.

nodes.name: RedirectUrlHint
nodes.summary: Renders the redirect URI in monospace with the explanation that a mismatch means the browser opens a page that never returns to the app. The developer-settings action is a SettingsButton rather than a raw TextButton so the one action inside the panel matches every other action on the screen.

nodes.name: LoginHero.kt
nodes.summary: The login and onboarding header: gradient brand mark, the app name, a one-line pitch and the icon carousel that names the four things the app does. The mark carries no entrance animation any more - an animateFloatAsState(1f -> 1f) was composing a spring and a graphicsLayer every frame to render it at the scale it already had.

nodes.name: LoginHero
nodes.summary: Draws the hero and delegates the movement to IconCarousel, which is real motion rather than an animation of a constant.

nodes.name: ArrivingPreferences.kt
nodes.summary: The two knobs behind the dashboard's Currently arriving rows, exposed as one Flow so the dashboard applies both in a single read and never draws a hidden header over a shown row. Read through the flow rather than a stored value, so a change in Settings reaches the dashboard without anything being rebuilt.
nodes.languageNotes: Demo and public-profile dashboards construct without a preferences object and fall back to the shipped defaults - they exist for one visit, not for remembering a person.

nodes.name: ArrivingPreferences
nodes.summary: Owns the anisequel_arriving_prefs DataStore: reads both switches as one settings object and writes each one independently, with a reset back to the shipped defaults.

nodes.name: ArrivingSettings
nodes.summary: Both preference values at once, defaulting to section shown and full poster cards. Exists so one emission carries both answers, which is what keeps the dashboard from splitting between a hidden header and a visible row.

nodes.name: setShowArrivingSection
nodes.summary: Turns the whole airing-and-upcoming section off or on. Hiding it removes the rows above search and, with them, every poster load on the path to the list.

nodes.name: setCompactArrivingCards
nodes.summary: Switches the arriving rows between poster cards and plain rows. Compact is the data-and-battery choice: the artwork is the entire cost of those cards.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Removes both keys rather than writing the default values, so the DataStore stays empty and a future change to the shipped defaults is picked up instead of being pinned by a stale write.

nodes.name: AuthInterceptor.kt
nodes.summary: Attaches the AniList bearer token to every request. The token used to be read from DataStore inside intercept(), blocking an OkHttp thread on disk I/O for every request - several per screen; it now comes from the repository's in-memory mirror, which sign-in and sign-out keep in step.
nodes.languageNotes: Falls back to runBlocking { getAccessToken() } at most once per process, for the first request before the token flow has been collected.

nodes.name: AuthInterceptor
nodes.summary: Adds `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when the repository has one and leaves the request untouched when it does not, which is what makes the signed-out dashboard work against AniList's public queries.

nodes.name: InfoHero.kt
nodes.summary: The Info page hero and the docked bar that replaces it on scroll. Leads with the poster artwork rather than AniList's banner because the dashboard list query never fetches `bannerImage`, so a banner-led hero started as a grey slab for every sheet opened from the dashboard; the artwork is drawn sharp and the legibility work is done by a bottom-weighted gradient scrim, because 26dp of blur turned the poster into an impression of itself.
nodes.languageNotes: Collapse progress is passed as a `() -> Float` and read inside `graphicsLayer`, so scrolling the page transforms the hero in the draw phase instead of recomposing it and its list siblings each frame.

nodes.name: InfoHero
nodes.summary: Draws the routine artwork backdrop, the gradient handover into the page surface, the poster with the title lockup and the fact chips (relation, studio, score, status, format), plus the overlaid open/close pill. Reads the extracted cover seed first and falls back to AniList's colour, so backdrop, cover shadow and buttons cannot be three different readings of the same image.

nodes.name: InfoFloatingBar
nodes.summary: The docked bar that takes over once the hero scrolls away: a title pill that is both a scroll-to-top button and a progress wash, plus the same open-on-AniList and close controls. AnimatedVisibility is driven by a `derivedStateOf` at the call site so the crossing recomposes once instead of every scrolled frame.

nodes.name: HeroIconButton
nodes.summary: A 48dp icon target inside a hero pill. Deliberately not an `IconButton` so the pill owns the surface, divider and ripple clipping; the size was raised from 46dp to the platform minimum because these are the controls reached one-handed at the bottom of the screen.

nodes.name: HeroChip
nodes.summary: A translucent capsule over artwork. Passing an `onClick` makes it a button with a brighter rim and a press spring, because over a busy poster nothing else distinguishes a tappable chip from the four plain facts beside it.

nodes.name: SequelDetailSheet.kt
nodes.summary: The modal sheet that shows one title's Info page and, when the session can write, the viewer's own entry. Collapsed from three content tabs to two destinations (reading vs editing) behind an ExpressiveNavigationBar, and owns the anime colour-adaptation write: extract the cover seed, recolour the app, schedule the revert on dismissal.
nodes.languageNotes: Scroll state and the in-progress edit draft are hoisted above `AnimatedContent` because it disposes the destination it animates away from; the list state is keyed on media id so walking a relation does not inherit the previous title's scroll offset.

nodes.name: SequelDetailSheet
nodes.summary: Hosts the sheet: resolves the cover seed, persists the anime accent and its revert schedule, and switches between the Info page and the entry editor. The theme effect is keyed on `ThemeSettings.isLoaded` because reading the flow's initial value made recolouring depend on whether DataStore beat the tap, which was the reported intermittent 'sometimes it works'.

nodes.name: themeWrite
nodes.summary: Runs a DataStore theme write with failures swallowed. An uncaught throw from a full disk or corrupt file killed the sheet's coroutine and force-stopped the app on opening a title; a colour that failed to save is a survivable cosmetic outcome, so cancellation is rethrown and everything else is dropped.

nodes.name: AccentColourSection.kt
nodes.summary: One Settings card holding the whole accent story: the wallpaper toggle, the brand palettes and the custom hue chips. Every picker clears the overrides that outrank it in Theme.kt, because an ignored override let a card light its check mark for a colour the app was not drawing.
nodes.languageNotes: Selection state is computed from four independent preferences per control; `animateColorAsState` drives the swatch border toward a constant so it settles instead of restarting.

nodes.name: AccentColourSection
nodes.summary: Draws the dynamic-colour switch, the wallpaper preview row, the palette grid and the hue row, and writes the preference changes that make the chosen source actually win. Turning dynamic colour on also steps the anime layer off, for the same reason a palette pick does.

nodes.name: PaletteCard
nodes.summary: One brand in the palette picker, washed with that palette's own primary/secondary as a gradient so two similar blues are told apart by colour family rather than by reading the label.

nodes.name: HueChip
nodes.summary: One custom accent as a round chip, with the check drawn white or black according to the hue's own luminance so the mark stays visible on both a jade and a crimson swatch.

nodes.name: MaterialColorSchemes.kt
nodes.summary: Pure-Kotlin Material 3 tonal-spot scheme generation: one seed in, 36 roles out for light and dark. Knows nothing about Compose so the palettes and their contrast can be tested on the JVM. Adds a chroma floor so a washed-out cover still produces a recognisable hue, and an opt-out from tinted surfaces so a standing custom accent does not repaint the brand's neutrals.
nodes.languageNotes: Fixed tone ladder (40/80 primaries, 6/98 surfaces) is the accessibility argument: the same text/background pair holds contrast for any hue, which HSL lightness cannot promise.

nodes.name: MaterialScheme
nodes.summary: A complete Material 3 scheme as plain ARGB ints. Deliberately free of Compose types so it can be generated and contrast-tested on the JVM; `role(name)` gives tests and diagnostics a lookup by Material's own role name.

nodes.name: MaterialColorSchemes
nodes.summary: The tonal-palette builder. Holds the tunable constants that encode the design decisions: the brand hue used when a seed has no usable chroma, the chroma floor, and the WCAG AA ratio the readable-on choice is made against.

nodes.name: tonalSpot
nodes.summary: Builds one scheme from a seed using Material You's tonal spot rules: primary at the seed's hue, secondary at reduced chroma, tertiary rotated 60 degrees, neutral from the seed or the brand. Always produces both light and dark so the anime layer can respect the user's Light/Dark/System choice instead of forcing dark.

nodes.name: readableOn
nodes.summary: Picks the foreground for a filled role by contrast rather than by Material's fixed tone: tone 100 on tone 40 fails 4.5:1 for a yellow or lime seed, so the darkest and lightest tones are tried when the preferred one is not readable.

nodes.name: ThemePreviewCard.kt
nodes.summary: The Theme tab's live preview: a gradient band drawn from the scheme's own primary/secondary/tertiary, a pill naming the active colour source, an interactive mock title card that exercises the press springs, and five role swatch dots. The pill's precedence order mirrors Theme.kt so it cannot name a colour the app is not drawing.
nodes.languageNotes: Mock plan/watch buttons are local `mutableStateOf` flags: the card is a demonstration, not a writer, so tapping them animates without touching AniList.

nodes.name: ThemePreviewCard
nodes.summary: Renders the accent as the app would render it, including the anime case, and labels which source won (retained anime colour, wallpaper, custom hue, then palette). The ordering is load-bearing: listing the custom hue above the wallpaper labelled the card with a colour the app was not drawing.

nodes.name: ActivityCalendarCard.kt
nodes.summary: The profile's 'days with finished things' heatmap. Uses five intensity steps off the scheme's `primary` role instead of a hardcoded green ramp, because a fixed ramp is exactly what becomes unreadable under a wallpaper-derived light palette; the grid scrolls horizontally rather than dropping its oldest weeks to fit.
nodes.languageNotes: Cells are drawn on one Canvas rather than as hundreds of composables; month labels, weekday gutter and cells share a Column so the row alignment is the layout instead of three hand-tuned siblings.

nodes.name: ActivityCalendarCard
nodes.summary: The card shell: header with the change count and weeks shown, the grid, and the legend. Legend stops and cell ramp come from one declaration so the legend cannot demonstrate something the cells do not do.

nodes.name: CalendarGrid
nodes.summary: The scrolling grid, opened at the newest column. Waits for a non-zero `maxValue` before scrolling because scrolling to a zero maximum happens before measurement and lands on the oldest week instead.

nodes.name: MonthHeaderRow
nodes.summary: Month names spanning the columns they start in: each label is given every column up to the next label, with the last running to the end, so the spans sum to the cells' width and a short February cannot push a label over the wrong month.

nodes.name: WeekdayGutter
nodes.summary: Monday, Wednesday and Friday letters beside their rows. Rows are Sunday-first, so the letters go at indices 1, 3 and 5; drawing them from the label list directly put 'M' beside Tuesday, which screenshot review does not catch.

nodes.name: ActivityCellsCanvas
nodes.summary: Draws every day cell in one Canvas, mapping intensity to an alpha ramp off `primary`. Carries a single content description for the whole grid, since hundreds of individual cells would be unusable with a screen reader.

nodes.name: CalendarLegend
nodes.summary: The Less-to-More strip under the grid, sampling the same `colorFor` ramp the cells use so the legend cannot drift from the data it explains.

nodes.name: JokeToastHost.kt
nodes.summary: A self-dismissing joke toast that appears at a random interval on the bar's three pages. The wait runs only while the Activity is resumed and is cancelled rather than paused with the screen, so a joke cannot come due in the background and be waiting on return; the first wait is minutes rather than the old fifteen, which meant most sessions never saw it at all.
nodes.languageNotes: The gate effect is keyed on lifecycle only, not on `enabled` — keying on both restarted the wait on every page move and starved the feature entirely.

nodes.name: JokeToastHost
nodes.summary: Schedules the joke, picks a line different from the previous one, and animates a bottom-anchored pill in from below on the spring tokens. Scale is read inside `graphicsLayer` and clamped to the slide's window because AnimatedVisibility disposes its content when the exit finishes.

nodes.name: WavyProgressBar.kt
nodes.summary: The Info page's wavy determinate progress bar, where the wave's height is the progress. Hand-drawn rather than Material's `LinearWavyProgressIndicator` because that component separates amplitude from track and cannot express 'the wave you are standing on is how far you have watched'.
nodes.languageNotes: Track and fill are one path drawn twice with a clipRect; building the fill as its own wave made it sit at a different height from the track it was meant to be the start of.

nodes.name: WavyProgressBar
nodes.summary: Animates the fill up from zero once per bar and draws the trail with a travelling phase. The entrance flag is `rememberSaveable` and the phase is held as a State read only in the draw lambda: a plain `remember` replayed the whole fill on scroll-back, and a composition-time read recomposed the card on every frame of a loop that never ends.

nodes.name: wavePath
nodes.summary: Builds the sine path by sampling `WaveGeometry.offset` at 96 straight segments, which is sub-pixel at phone width. The geometry itself lives in domain/motion so the shape can be unit-tested without a device.

nodes.name: IconCarousel.kt
nodes.summary: The rotating icon rail on the sign-in screen, cycling the app's own icon vocabulary over a gradient tile. Uses a plain AnimatedContent rather than a pager so only one 44dp icon is measured and drawn per frame on a screen that should cost almost nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: The delay loop is keyed on icon count and interval, not on the current index, so its own tick cannot restart it; progress-dot widths are painted in `drawBehind` rather than measured.

nodes.name: IconCarousel
nodes.summary: Advances the icon on a cancellable timer and crossfades with a scale morph, with stretched progress dots beside it. Cancellation on leaving the screen is the whole lifecycle story: tabs Sign In and nothing keeps ticking.

nodes.name: CoverColorRepository.kt
nodes.summary: Extracts a theme seed from a cover image's pixels through Coil plus the domain quantizer, instead of trusting AniList's single dominant colour, which is computed over the whole file and often matches the background wash rather than the artwork. Falls back to nothing on purpose: null means the caller uses AniList's colour or the brand.
nodes.languageNotes: 128px decode with `allowHardware(false)` — a hardware bitmap cannot be read with `getPixels`, and Coil returns one on API 31+; a small sample also avoids a multi-megabyte allocation per sheet open.

nodes.name: CoverColorRepository
nodes.summary: Process-wide seed cache keyed by poster URL so opening the same title twice decodes once. Capped at 64 entries: only the open sheet's URL is ever read, and an unbounded map over a long session is a leak with extra steps.

nodes.name: extract
nodes.summary: Returns a seed for a URL or null when the image cannot be read, treating null as a normal result rather than an error so a bad cover never crashes a detail sheet. Cancellation is rethrown because Coil throws it when the sheet closes mid-decode, and swallowing it would apply a fallback colour to a sheet that is gone.

nodes.name: DynamicThemeBuilder.kt
nodes.summary: The boundary between the pure colour science in domain/color and Compose's ColorScheme. Replaces an HSL builder that derived only a few roles and copied the rest off the brand scheme, so the anime theme read as a coloured button on the usual app and its light scheme was unreachable because dark mode was forced.
nodes.languageNotes: `toColorScheme` copies onto the brand scheme as a base so a Material role added in future keeps a brand value rather than Material's purple baseline.

nodes.name: DynamicThemeBuilder
nodes.summary: Compose-facing entry points for seed-derived themes: hex parsing and scheme construction. Kept thin so the tone ladder exists in exactly one place and can be tested off-device.

nodes.name: createDynamicSchemes
nodes.summary: Generates a light and a dark ColorScheme from one seed. `tintSurfaces` is the difference between an accent and a theme: the anime layer tints surfaces because it is opened for a specific show, while a custom accent must not move surfaces the user never asked to change.

nodes.name: parseHexColor
nodes.summary: Turns a stored hex string into a Compose Color, delegating the parsing to `ArgbHex` so the preference layer and the theme layer cannot disagree about what a stored colour means.

nodes.name: AnimatedColorScheme.kt
nodes.summary: Cross-fades all 36 colour roles between schemes instead of cutting, so opening a title reads as the app taking on the show's colour rather than being handed a second theme in the same frames the sheet is animating in.
nodes.languageNotes: Every role is animated, not just primary: animating a handful made the un-derived roles snap at the end, which looked like a flash. This is the one place a per-frame recomposition is the accepted cost.

nodes.name: rememberAnimatedColorScheme
nodes.summary: Returns the target scheme with each role eased toward it on `ExpressiveMotion.ThemeColorEffects`. There is no conditional early return even under the instant motion style, because inserting and removing 36 animation slots would reset them to their targets mid-switch.

nodes.name: CoverColors.kt
nodes.summary: Session store of extracted cover seeds, keyed by poster URL. A snapshot map rather than a model field because the seed is read by the sheet and wanted by a hero several composables below it: threading a new field through every card would have made extraction the AniList model's problem.
nodes.languageNotes: A `mutableStateMapOf` means the hero reading the entry is invalidated when the pixels finish decoding, without the sheet recomposing its whole page. Capped at 96 URLs in insertion order.

nodes.name: CoverColors
nodes.summary: The store itself: put by URL, read back as hex or Color, plus a clear() kept for tests. Values are normalised to hex strings so re-putting the same seed is a no-op and the insertion-order queue cannot grow on a recomposition.

nodes.name: put
nodes.summary: Stores a seed and evicts the oldest URL past the cap. Safe to call on every recomposition: an unchanged value returns before touching the map, so it cannot invalidate the hero it is feeding.

nodes.name: color
nodes.summary: Reads the extracted colour for a URL as a Compose Color, or null before the decode has landed. Reading it in composition is what subscribes the hero's backdrop to the seed arriving.

nodes.name: ExpressiveMotion.kt
nodes.summary: The one place every spring in the app is named. Holds the spatial/effects/colour/Int/IntSize/IntOffset/Dp tokens whose physics switch on the user's MotionStyle, plus the bouncyPress and expressiveHoldGesture modifiers built on them. Exists because a dozen call sites had re-derived the same stiffness and damping inline, so two components animating the same interaction used two different curves.
nodes.languageNotes: ExpressiveMotion.speed is Compose snapshot state, not a plain var: as a var it was invisible to composition, so a Motion style change only reached whatever recomposed next. Each token is a `get()` that resolves through a private helper, so INSTANT snaps, SMOOTH drops overshoot and CHILL keeps it.

nodes.name: ExpressiveMotion
nodes.summary: Token object for the app's hand-tuned motion. Every token is a typed FiniteAnimationSpec (Float, Color, Int, IntSize, IntOffset, Dp) because Compose's spec type is generic on the target, which is why animateColorAsState and animateIntAsState needed tokens of their own instead of the Float ones. Colour tokens are deliberately NoBouncy: an overshooting spring interpolates each channel past its endpoint and can render out of gamut.

nodes.name: bouncyPress
nodes.summary: Press-scale modifier applied at roughly two dozen call sites. The animated value is read inside graphicsLayer so a press invalidates only the draw phase, and it uses two specs by direction (PressSpatialIn down, PressSpatialOut up) because a single spring made a press read as a fade. When the caller passes its clickable's InteractionSource the raw pointer loop is not installed at all, so a fling no longer leaves the row squashed; the loop that remains for bare Buttons releases the press past touch slop for the same reason.

nodes.name: expressiveHoldGesture
nodes.summary: Long-press gesture with a spring press-scale and a haptic on hold, used for hold-to-plan controls. Built on the same shared press token rather than its own literal spring, so it cannot drift into feeling like a different button than bouncyPress.

nodes.name: TierBoardTiles.kt
nodes.summary: The paint half of the tier board: a tier row's tinted fill and colour gutter, the positional drop caret, one poster tile with its caption and score badge, and the lifted ghost that follows the finger. Split from the board's drag maths and geometry when the two grew past the file limit together, so a change to what the board draws rarely touches how it is dragged.
nodes.languageNotes: Every animated value is read inside graphicsLayer or animate*AsState toward a settled constant; sizes handed to the ghost are pre-multiplied by zoom so the tile under the finger is the tile that was picked up.

nodes.name: tierRowFill
nodes.summary: Mixes the tier colour into the surface instead of painting it over. The row used to be the tier colour at 0.92 alpha, which on six rows produced six saturated bars where every cover sat on a different coloured field; the tint keeps the colour as an identity and leaves the solid colour to the label gutter.

nodes.name: TierRowStrip
nodes.summary: One tier row: a solid colour gutter with a vertically centred label and member count, and a tinted body that says "Drop titles here" when empty so a drop target is announced. Highlight animates colour and border width but never the row's size, because growing a row mid-drop would reflow every tile under the finger; below a 44dp gutter the label drops to labelSmall and the count is omitted rather than drawn clipped.

nodes.name: TierDropCaret
