nodes.summary: The bar that says where inside a row a dropped tile will land, which the row highlight alone cannot express once drops are positional. A capsule rather than a stretched polygon because RoundedPolygon.toShape() renders a stretched Pill as an ellipse.

nodes.name: TierPosterTile
nodes.summary: One poster with its optional caption and AniList score. The caption defaults under the poster because AniList covers carry their own typography, and the on-cover placement draws the name over a gradient scrim with the score badge moved to the opposite corner so the two never overlap. Score 0 is suppressed because AniList answers 0 as readily as null and a badge reading "0" claims a title is terrible rather than unrated.

nodes.name: TierDragGhost
nodes.summary: The poster under the finger, drawn as a sibling after the board geometry so it lands on top (a Layout has no z-index). Translation, scroll compensation and lift are read inside graphicsLayer so a pointer move costs a draw invalidation rather than a re-place of the whole board; scrollShift exists because auto-scroll moves the board under a finger that has not moved.

nodes.name: InfoMetaRowsSection.kt
nodes.summary: The three disclosure rows on the Info page - Titles, Synonyms, Producers - each opening its own bottom sheet. They are rows rather than cards so the page stays short while the complete list stays one tap away, and Producers is defined as the studios AniList marked non-main, which is the production committee rather than the animation studio.
nodes.languageNotes: The sheet body uses verticalScroll rather than LazyColumn: ModalBottomSheet does not scroll its own content, and a title with fifteen synonyms drew past the fold with everything below unreachable.

nodes.name: InfoMetaRowsSection
nodes.summary: Entry point for the three meta rows: derives the title pairs, synonyms and non-main studio names from the media node, returns nothing at all when all three are empty, and swaps one shared ModalBottomSheet between them. The producers row is absent rather than listing the animation studio as its own producer when a payload carries no isMain flags.

nodes.name: MetaRowButton
nodes.summary: The tappable row that opens a sheet, with an optional count. Wears a downward chevron rather than the app's SequelArrow, because that arrow means "there is another title this way" on sequel cards and a row that opens a sheet was promising navigation it does not do.

nodes.name: TitleRow
nodes.summary: One alternative title with a 48dp copy control that acknowledges the tap for COPY_CONFIRMATION_MILLIS. The acknowledgement is per row rather than one flag on the sheet, because a single flag would light a tick on all four rows and claim four names had been copied; the clipboard is the platform's, since Android only started drawing its own "Copied" chip in 13 and this app's floor is 12.

nodes.name: ThemePreferences.kt
nodes.summary: Persists every appearance choice - theme mode, palette, custom hue, true black, canvas colour, motion style and the temporary anime layer - in one DataStore preferences file, exposed as a single ThemeSettings Flow so the theme applies them in one read. Holds the process-scoped revert timer for the anime layer, which must outlive the detail sheet that started it.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses preferencesDataStore with a private Keys object; ThemeSettings carries an isLoaded flag because DataStore reports "not read yet" and "user chose the default" as the same value, and without it every cold start painted the default theme then repainted.

nodes.name: ThemeMode
nodes.summary: Light/dark/system choice with a stable storage string. fromStorage falls back to SYSTEM rather than throwing, because a preference file written by a newer build can hold a value this build has never heard of and a theme preference is not worth refusing to start over.

nodes.name: MotionStyle
nodes.summary: Instant / Smooth / Chill, the setting that selects both a compiled Material MotionScheme and the physics of the app's own ExpressiveMotion tokens. fromStorage maps the pre-rename values "expressive" and "standard" onto Chill and Smooth instead of silently resetting a reader's choice.

nodes.name: ThemePreferences
nodes.summary: The appearance repository. Reads all preferences as one ThemeSettings value rather than a Flow per switch, because the theme wraps the whole app and needs a value up front, and keeps the anime-layer revert job on the application context so the timer is not tied to an Activity that may be gone by the time it fires.

nodes.name: ThemeSettings
nodes.summary: Immutable snapshot of every appearance preference, including the isLoaded flag that distinguishes a chosen light theme from an unread one. One object rather than eleven separate flows, so a theme change is one recomposition rather than a wave of them.

nodes.name: setAnimeThemeActive
nodes.summary: Opens or closes the anime colour layer and, when Retain is on, writes the cover hue as the custom accent in the same transaction. Written as one edit because every transaction emits a new ThemeSettings and re-themes the app: two calls recoloured twice inside the detail sheet's entrance animation. Switching off always drops the cover colour, which used to survive and be restored by the next enable.

nodes.name: scheduleAnimeThemeRevert
nodes.summary: Starts the process-scoped timer that clears the temporary anime layer after the sheet has closed. This used to live in a LaunchedEffect inside the detail sheet, so dismissing the sheet cancelled it and "5 Minutes" became indistinguishable from Retain; a new title or Retain cancels the previous job so only one layer is ever pending.

nodes.name: ExpressiveNavigationBar.kt
nodes.summary: A floating capsule navigation bar where only the selected destination grows a label. Exists instead of Material's NavigationBar because a stock bar under the page's top tab bar would draw the same control twice at two sizes; the growing label is what distinguishes "switching pages" from "switching tabs of one page".
nodes.languageNotes: SELECTED_WEIGHT is 2.3 rather than a taste value: it is the weight at which a 360dp phone still fits "Activity" whole while every unselected item keeps its 48dp tap target. Selection scale and press scale multiply into one graphicsLayer so neither recomposes the bar over the list scrolling beneath it.

nodes.name: NavigationDestination
nodes.summary: One destination: label, vector icon, test tag and an optional iconUrl. The image slot exists only for the main bar's Profile tab, where the destination is the signed-in viewer's own avatar, and it is sized to the icon exactly because the bar's width arithmetic is computed against a 22dp icon.

nodes.name: ExpressiveNavigationBar
nodes.summary: Draws the capsule bar, hands the extra width to the selected item and fires a haptic then onSelect on tap. The bar fills its parent and redistributes width rather than resizing, which is what keeps the overall bar stable while one item springs open.

nodes.name: NavigationItem
nodes.summary: One destination: icon or avatar, an AnimatedVisibility label when selected, and the pill's colour and scale animations. The ripple is suppressed because it fights the spring that is simultaneously widening the capsule, and defaultMinSize keeps an icon-only item at the 48dp tap target.

nodes.name: ThemeTab.kt
nodes.summary: The Settings theme page, ordered as three questions - how the app looks, where its colour comes from, how it moves - with a live preview hero and a trailing Reset appearance. Keeps only the index and the lighter sections; the heavy colour sections live in their own files so this one stays readable.
nodes.languageNotes: Collects ThemePreferences.settings with a default ThemeSettings initial value, then treats "anything differs from the defaults" as the condition for showing Reset appearance.

nodes.name: ThemeTab
nodes.summary: Composes the theme settings page: preview, appearance, background, accent, anime colour and motion, then a Reset appearance button that only appears once something actually differs from the shipping defaults.

nodes.name: CanvasChip
nodes.summary: One canvas colour choice as a pill chip with a leading dot of the real colour. A null hex means "follow the theme" and is drawn in the current surface colour; an unparseable stored value falls back to dark grey rather than leaving the dot invisible.

nodes.name: InfoExtrasCard.kt
nodes.summary: The Info page's Extras card: full artwork, trailer, copy link and share. Every row is an action the app really performs, because an "Episodes" or "Comments" row would be a control that leads nowhere; Copy link was the missing one, since sharing handed the title to another app and left no way to get the URL out.
nodes.languageNotes: Both intents are wrapped in runCatching so a device with no YouTube or no chooser target does not crash the title page; the clipboard is the platform ClipboardManager rather than Compose's deprecated-in-flight LocalClipboardManager.

nodes.name: InfoExtrasCard
nodes.summary: Builds the Extras card from a media node, hiding the trailer row when the node has no trailer and delegating the copy action to CopyLinkRow. Trailer and share both go through ACTION_VIEW and ACTION_SEND intents guarded by runCatching.

nodes.name: CopyLinkRow
nodes.summary: Copies the AniList URL and confirms it by crossfading the whole row into "Link copied" for COPY_CONFIRMATION_MILLIS. The confirmation exists because Android only draws its own "Copied" toast from 13 while this app supports 12, where a silent copy looks like a tap that did nothing; the effect is keyed on the flag so a second tap restarts the window instead of leaving the row stuck.

nodes.name: AnimeColourSection.kt
nodes.summary: The Settings section for content-based dynamic colour: while a detail sheet is open the app borrows the cover's quantized colour, and Retain makes that hue the app's own accent afterwards. Shows a live swatch of the colour currently driving the scheme so the feature is never a mystery while it is active.
nodes.languageNotes: The revert picker indexes the stored seconds against a list rather than clamping: the old coerceAtLeast(1) turned a real 0 into 1, so "Immediately" could never be selected or displayed.

nodes.name: AnimeColourSection
nodes.summary: Two switches and a revert-duration picker. Turning Retain off has to end the retained state as well as clear the hue, because the anime layer outranks every other colour source and clearing only the accent left the scheme unchanged; the picker is dimmed rather than ignored while retaining, since there is nothing to revert to.

nodes.name: MainTabs.kt
nodes.summary: The app's bottom-bar contract: the three main pages, their destinations, which routes answer to which tab, how much bottom clearance a scrolling page leaves, and how a tap switches pages instead of pushing one. Lives in one file so the enum, the bar and the route mapping cannot drift about what "the second tab" is.
nodes.languageNotes: MainBarClearance is the bar's own height only; the system navigation inset is read from WindowInsets at composition time because a gesture bar, a three-button bar and a cutout are three different heights, and hardcoding one produced an end-of-list bounce.

nodes.name: MainTab
nodes.summary: Home, Library and Profile as an enum rather than an index, because the bar, the route mapping and the tap handler are three places that must agree and an index agreed by convention drifts silently when a destination is added.

nodes.name: mainTabDestinations
nodes.summary: Derives the bar's destinations from MainTab.entries so the bar's order and the enum's order are one fact, substituting the viewer's avatar for the Profile glyph when there is a session and keeping the glyph when there is not, so the bar never renders a hole.

nodes.name: mainTabForRoute
nodes.summary: Maps a route to a tab, or null for the screens pushed from a tab (Settings, tier list, studio, someone else's profile) so the bar hides rather than claiming a selected tab the reader did not choose. Home has two routes because the demo runs without a session, and the profile matches its registered pattern rather than a literal.

nodes.name: MainBar
nodes.summary: Wraps ExpressiveNavigationBar, owns its own navigation-bar inset because it is the one element always pinned to the bottom edge, and converts a selected index back into a MainTab. The bar only reports which tab was chosen; it never navigates.

nodes.name: navigateToMainTab
nodes.summary: A tap on the bar switches pages instead of stacking them: popUpTo Home with saved state, launchSingleTop and restoreState, so Back from any tab lands on Home and returning to a tab restores what it showed. Resolves Home from the session state, and replaces the demo dashboard with a demo profile rather than stacking on it.

nodes.name: mainBarClearance
nodes.summary: The bar's height plus the device's real navigation inset, read from WindowInsets during composition. A constant was tried and produced the "bounce back" snap when a list reached its end and the padding disagreed with where the bar actually was.

nodes.name: CoverColorQuantizer.kt
nodes.summary: Picks a single Material theme seed out of a cover's pixels using M3's 5-bit histogram and Score rules, without the heavy quantizer dependency. Greys are dropped and gradients are scored by hue neighbourhood, which is what makes the result look designer-chosen and stops a black-and-white cover from producing a grey app.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Kotlin with no Android imports so the scoring can be unit-tested against a hand-built histogram; transparent pixels are skipped rather than composited onto white.

nodes.name: CoverColorQuantizer
nodes.summary: Stateless object exposing seedFrom over a pixel array. Deliberately returns one seed rather than four swatches: the tonal-palette builder derives secondary, tertiary, surfaces and outlines from one hue, so a small secondary swatch would only make the scheme inconsistent.

nodes.name: seedFrom
nodes.summary: The public entry point: quantizes then scores, returning null for a grey image so the caller can fall back to AniList's own colour instead of inventing one.

nodes.name: quantize
nodes.summary: Bins opaque pixels into a 5-bit-per-channel histogram, filling the low three bits from the top so each bin's representative value sits in the middle of its range rather than at its darkest corner.

nodes.name: score
nodes.summary: Ranks a histogram with a reduced port of M3's Score: population proportion weighted 0.7, chroma against a 48 target, hue excitedness measured over 15 degrees either side, and a chroma-5 cutoff that drops greys. Kept separate from quantize so it can be tested with a hand-built histogram instead of a bitmap.

nodes.name: DashboardHeader.kt
nodes.summary: The dashboard's two header pieces: the franchise search field with its animated clear button, and the "Missed Sequels" section header with a count badge and the active sort name. Both are capped to the page's max content width so they line up with the cards below on a tablet.
nodes.languageNotes: The clear button only exists while the query is non-blank, and it fades/scales in with BouncySpatial but out with FastSpatial, so dismissing it does not overshoot.

nodes.name: DashboardSearchBar
nodes.summary: The franchise/sequel search field, pill-shaped with a search glyph and a clear button that appears only when there is text to clear and fires a haptic on tap.

nodes.name: DashboardSectionHeader
nodes.summary: The "Missed Sequels" heading with the recommendation count and the currently applied sort, so the list's order is legible without opening the filter sheet.

nodes.name: InfoMotion.kt
nodes.summary: The Info page's staggered card entrance plus the three constants that split the hero-to-docked-bar handover. The stagger is capped so the last card starts within a third of a second, and it is skipped entirely under MotionStyle.INSTANT because an entrance delay is itself motion.
nodes.languageNotes: The played flag is rememberSaveable, not remember: a LazyColumn keeps saved state for items it disposed, so a plain remember replayed the whole stagger on the way back up the page. The effect stays in the composition and checks the flag inside itself, since wrapping it in if (!played) would cancel the running spring.

nodes.name: sectionReveal
nodes.summary: Modifier that fades and lifts one Info card into place after an index-based delay, running the animation in graphicsLayer so the stagger costs no layout pass while the sheet is still settling. Returns the receiver unchanged under INSTANT, and marks itself played before the spring so a card scrolled out mid-animation does not replay on return.

nodes.name: WaveGeometry.kt
nodes.summary: The arithmetic behind the Info page's wavy episode-progress bar. It sits in domain rather than beside the Canvas because the drawing is not assertable and every visible mistake in the control is a mistake in these numbers - a wave at full height at 0% draws a wobble on a title nobody has started.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a real sine rather than a chain of cubics, because a cubic approximation of one period drifts a few percent at the crests and the crests are the part of the curve the eye follows.

nodes.name: WaveGeometry
nodes.summary: Stateless sine-wave helpers for the progress bar, kept pure so a test can pin the amplitude and offset rules without rendering anything.

nodes.name: amplitude
nodes.summary: Wave height at a given progress, never zero even at rest: the track is drawn as the same wave, so a zero here would make an untouched title's track a ruled line while every other title's is a wave.

nodes.name: offset
nodes.summary: Cross-axis offset of the wave at x, as a sine of the wavelength and phase so the travelling motion is a function of the caller's animated cycle fraction rather than of a frame clock the test would have to fake.

nodes.name: ArgbHex.kt
nodes.summary: The single parser and formatter for the hex ARGB strings the theme preferences store. It lives in domain because three layers now touch the format - the detail sheet stores an extracted seed, the theme builder parses a preference, and the cover-colour store round-trips the same string - and two hand-rolled parsers is how a preference written by one half stops being readable by the other.
nodes.languageNotes: Accepts RRGGBB or AARRGGBB with or without a leading #, and always formats back as six digits because alpha is not part of a theme seed.

nodes.name: ArgbHex
nodes.summary: Stateless hex/ARGB conversion object shared by the theme builder, the preferences and the cover-colour path.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary: Turns a stored hex string into an opaque ARGB int, returning null for anything that is not six or eight hex digits. Six-digit values get an opaque alpha added, so a colour read back from storage is never accidentally transparent.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Writes an ARGB int back as #RRGGBB with a fixed Locale, so a persisted theme colour does not acquire locale-specific digits or a stray alpha channel.

nodes.name: InfoTalent.kt
nodes.summary: The cast, crew and franchise rows of the title page, and the start of every tap that opens a person or a related title. The open callbacks are nullable rather than defaulted to no-ops, because a default no-op is a lie the card cannot detect: it would draw a tappable card on a host that never wired a store and the tap would do nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: LazyRow itemsIndexed keys append the position because AniList can credit the same character twice and a repeated LazyRow key is a hard IllegalArgumentException that closed the app while the title page opened.

nodes.name: InfoCharactersSection
nodes.summary: The cast row: character portrait, alias, role, age and gender beside the Japanese voice actor. Character and actor side by side is the point, because a cast list without the actor is a list of names the synopsis already gave; only the Japanese cast is requested since that is the one track AniList has for essentially every title.

nodes.name: InfoStaffSection
nodes.summary: The crew row of portraits with the position each person held. It draws AniList's relevance order untouched rather than sorting, because that order already puts the original creator and the director first, which are the two credits a reader is looking for.

nodes.name: InfoRelationsSection
nodes.summary: The franchise row, whose cards replace the sheet's subject in place instead of stacking a second sheet. That was the resolution of the universal-info-page question: a chain of related titles stays walkable and there is still exactly one sheet with one visible close control, at the cost of a one-way relation.

nodes.name: DetailEditControls.kt
nodes.summary: The parts the entry editor is assembled from: the draft model, the state holder that survives tab switches, and the three row shapes the form is built from. Split out of DetailEditTab so that file stays about what the form edits rather than how a row is drawn.
nodes.languageNotes: Declarations are internal rather than file-private so the tab in the next file can use them while nothing outside ui.components.detail can; the draft keeps AniList's own score scale instead of normalising it to ten.

nodes.name: EntryStatusOption
nodes.summary: One AniList list status carrying the wording each medium uses for it. Both spellings exist because the labels were once shared between the two media, and a manga list that offers Watching instead of Reading is the failure this prevents.

nodes.name: EntryDraft
nodes.summary: The editable snapshot of one AniList entry. It carries scoreMax, scoreStep and scoreFormat so a save cannot rescale an 85/100 score to 8/100, and it carries progressVolumes it never edits because the save is a whole snapshot and an omitted field would be cleared on the server.

nodes.name: EntryEditState
nodes.summary: The edit form's state, remembered by the sheet rather than the tab. It sits one level up because AnimatedContent disposes the tab it animates away from, so state remembered inside the tab was rebuilt from nothing on every switch and fired a second request for an entry AniList had already answered.

nodes.name: EditorCard
nodes.summary: The one labelled control row the whole edit tab is built from, with an optional body underneath. Having a single row shape means a new field cannot invent its own spacing or icon size: it either is one of these or it is not a field.

nodes.name: DateRow
nodes.summary: The start or finish date row: tap to pick, and a clear control once a date is set. The clear target is a 48dp box around a 20dp glyph, because a small X inside a row that is itself clickable made clearing the date both the smallest target on the form and the one easiest to miss into the picker.

nodes.name: StepButton
nodes.summary: One side of the progress stepper at Android's 48dp minimum touch target. The glyph is unchanged from the 42dp version; only the box a finger has to hit grew, because these are the controls a thumb aims at while looking at a poster rather than at the form.

nodes.name: toEpochMillisUtc
nodes.summary: Resolves AniList's partial FuzzyDate to the earliest expressible UTC day so the date picker has one day to show. UTC matches BuildActivityCalendarUseCase, because the same entry has to open on the same day on two phones in different zones.

nodes.name: DetailEditTab.kt
nodes.summary: The Edit tab of the detail sheet: the viewer's own status, progress, score, both dates, privacy and notes. Every control moves a local draft and only Save writes, because saving per change would spend the account's request budget on a slider drag and make a mis-tap impossible to undo.
nodes.languageNotes: Fields scroll inside the tab with the two actions pinned below them; they used to be the last rows of the sheet's own scroll, which put Save changes roughly 170dp below the fold on a 640dp screen.

nodes.name: DetailEditTab
nodes.summary: Renders the staged entry form and the pinned Save/Delete bar. The progress row is hidden for a title that has not aired, because that slider opens on the episode count and invites a write about episodes that do not exist yet.

nodes.name: PannableBackdrop.kt
nodes.summary: A hero image that covers its box and can be pinched and panned. It computes its own fit because ContentScale.FillWidth scaled to the width and left the bottom of every media sheet as bare background, while ContentScale.Crop covered properly but could not be panned at all.
nodes.languageNotes: The transform arithmetic is plain Kotlin with no Compose in it so BackdropTransformTest can pin the rule that no edge of the picture may come inside the box; the transform is applied in the draw phase via graphicsLayer.

nodes.name: BackdropFit
nodes.summary: Whether the picture is scaled to cover its box or to fit inside it. FIT is currently reachable only through its parameters and its tests, and that is deliberate: the detail hero stopped using this component precisely because a fitted hero would expose its letterbox the moment the page scrolled.

nodes.name: PannableBackdrop
nodes.summary: Measures the container and the loaded image, applies the computed transform in a graphicsLayer, and gates panning on hasOverflow. It uses Modifier.transformable rather than detectTransformGestures because the latter consumes single-pointer drags unconditionally, which panned the hero instead of scrolling the sheet it sits in.

nodes.name: BackdropTransform
nodes.summary: Where the picture sits once the container, the image and the gesture are known: base scale times zoom, plus an offset clamped to half the overflow on each axis. The bounds are symmetric because the transform origin is the centre.

nodes.name: hasOverflow
nodes.summary: Whether the picture may take a single-pointer drag at all right now. It used to ask 'is any axis overflowing', which is a near-tautology for a cover fit, so the gate never declined, the hero ate every vertical drag aimed at it and then clamped the offset back to zero: the gesture was consumed and thrown away.

nodes.name: backdropCoverScale
nodes.summary: The larger of the two axis ratios, which is what cover means: the axis that runs out first decides the scale and the other is over-covered by exactly the slack the pan consumes.

nodes.name: backdropFitScale
nodes.summary: The smaller of the two axis ratios: the whole image inside the box with the slack on the longer axis left as letterbox. It lives beside the cover scale because the two are the same question answered in opposite directions.

nodes.name: FullScreenCoverViewer.kt
nodes.summary: The full-screen artwork viewer opened from a poster: pinch to 4.5x, double-tap zoom, pan clamped to the measured overflow, and a frame fitted to the artwork's own aspect ratio so a 2:3 cover is not letterboxed inside a window smaller than the hero it was opened from.
nodes.languageNotes: Pan limits are measured from the cover box rather than the hardcoded 300f/400f constants they used to be, so a tall cover cannot be dragged past its own edge on a narrow phone.

nodes.name: FullScreenCoverViewer
nodes.summary: A full-screen Dialog showing the cover over a near-black scrim with the format, status, HD tag, Romaji and English titles. Tapping outside while zoomed resets the zoom rather than dismissing, so a reader who zoomed in does not lose the viewer to a stray tap.

nodes.name: InfoCategoriesSection.kt
nodes.summary: The single Categories block: genres, weighted tags and the tags AniList hides behind a spoiler warning. Genres and tags were two cards spending two headers on what the reference presents as one heading, and the spoiler tags are collapsed rather than filtered out so the tag count printed on the page is not wrong.
nodes.languageNotes: The expanded and spoilers-shown flags are rememberSaveable keyed on media.id, because the section is a LazyColumn item and a plain remember reopened it collapsed after the reader scrolled away and back.

nodes.name: InfoCategoriesSection
nodes.summary: Draws genres as static chips, the strongest ranked tags plus a '+N more' chip, and a 48dp spoiler strip that reveals the flagged tags only when asked. A genre chip is deliberately not clickable: a chip that looks tappable and does nothing is worse than a label.

nodes.name: ExpressiveVisuals.kt
nodes.summary: The small expressive pieces: an animated count badge, an artwork placeholder, a full-surface loading overlay and the morphing empty-state orb. The orb swaps to a static composable when motion is Instant or the app is not resumed, so no clock keeps ticking behind a stopped Activity.
nodes.languageNotes: The Instant/resumed branch is between two composables rather than inside one, because an infinite transition cannot be skipped conditionally without changing the shape of the composition every time the motion style changes.

nodes.name: ExpressiveCountBadge
nodes.summary: The count pill beside a section header, animating between settled strings and capping at '99+'. The target only changes when the count crosses a threshold, so it animates to a value rather than restarting on every recomposition.

nodes.name: ExpressiveArtworkPlaceholder
nodes.summary: The tinted box with a muted film glyph shown while poster artwork loads, so an empty cover slot reads as waiting rather than as a broken image.

nodes.name: ExpressiveLoadingOverlay
nodes.summary: A full-surface centred loader with a message, used where a screen has nothing to draw yet. It wraps the app's own loading indicator so waiting looks like the rest of the app rather than like a stock M3 spinner.

nodes.name: ExpressiveEmptyOrb
nodes.summary: The empty-state orb, choosing between a static shape and a morphing one. The morph is what makes the empty state look hand-built rather than like an icon on a placeholder, and the static branch allocates no animation at all so an orb left composed in the background costs nothing.

nodes.name: AppVectorIcons.kt
nodes.summary: The single icon registry the app draws from, which is how the no-emoji, vectors-only rule is actually enforced: a screen either uses a name from here or it does not get a glyph. Entries are named for what a control means rather than for the shape it is drawn with, so a redraw does not rename a screen.
nodes.languageNotes: Every entry is a val on an object, so R8 only keeps the glyphs that are actually referenced; material-icons-extended names were verified against the sources rather than assumed, because a wrong import is a CI build failure.

nodes.name: AppVectorIcons
nodes.summary: The registry object itself: material glyphs plus the hand-authored vectors from AppCustomVectors and AppExtraVectors, grouped by screen with a comment wherever two destinations once shared one glyph and became indistinguishable at 22dp.

nodes.name: PersonStaffCredits.kt
nodes.summary: The two horizontal credit rows on a person's profile: the titles they worked on, carrying the role they held, and the characters they voiced. Split out of PersonProfileSheet because the card layout, cover sizes and tap targets change for different reasons than the sheet's chrome, hero and biography.
nodes.languageNotes: The poster boxes use MaterialTheme.shapes.medium, not ExpressiveShapes.pill: a pill on a 112x158 box is an ellipse, so every portrait had its corners rounded away and read as a placeholder.

nodes.name: ProfileAppearancesRow
nodes.summary: The 'Appears in' row of covers with the staff role under each title. The role is the fact the row exists for: TV says what a title is on anybody's page, Director says why this person is on this one.

nodes.name: ProfileVoicedCharactersRow
nodes.summary: The characters a staff member voiced, as a row of covers. It reuses the mic heading of the character page's 'Voiced by' because it is the same relationship read in the other direction, and it draws captions instead of tap targets when the host cannot open a character.

nodes.name: ExpressiveShapes.kt
nodes.summary: Shape tokens for the app: one decorative polygon for square artwork, capsule tokens for tabs and segmented controls, and the named corner-radius scale that replaced sixty-four inlined literals across fourteen values. Corners two dp apart read as two unrelated shapes, which is what makes screens feel drawn by different people.
nodes.languageNotes: pill is RoundedCornerShape(percent = 50) rather than RoundedPolygon.toShape(), because toShape stretches a square perimeter to the layout size and drew a 120x44 tab as a 120x44 ellipse; ExpressiveShapesTest guards the geometry.

nodes.name: ExpressiveShapes
nodes.summary: The token object. Only one polygon token survives because the other four had no call sites and each was a live reference the shrinker had to consider reachable; adding a shape back means adding a call site, not just a property.

nodes.name: expressiveShape
nodes.summary: Converts a decorative RoundedPolygon to a Compose Shape. Only valid on square, fixed-size artwork, because the result is stretched to whatever bounds it is drawn into.

nodes.name: MorphShape
nodes.summary: A Shape that interpolates between two MaterialShapes polygons. It takes the progress as a provider rather than a Float so the animated value is read in createOutline during the draw pass, instead of in composition where a Modifier.clip on an animated shape recomposed its caller on every frame of the morph.

nodes.name: SequelPoster.kt
nodes.summary: The 104x152 poster with the format pill, a score badge for well-rated titles, and a dominant-colour placeholder that opens the full-screen artwork on hold or tap. It also owns the AniList cover-colour parser the rest of the card family tints its placeholders with.
nodes.languageNotes: The placeholder is one solid colour rather than the full-bleed gradient it used to paint on every poster, which AsyncImage then overdrew completely: a second draw per poster in a scrolling wall of covers.

nodes.name: SequelPoster
nodes.summary: Draws the poster, its format tag and a score badge once the score clears 75, and hands the whole card to the full-screen viewer. A badge below that threshold would put a mediocre score over artwork the reader is scanning by eye.

nodes.name: toCoverColorOrNull
nodes.summary: Parses AniList's '#RRGGBB' cover colour, returning null for missing or junk values. It is internal rather than private so the parent-cover thumbnails and the detail sheet tint their placeholders the same way instead of each re-implementing the parse.

nodes.name: SequelStatusChip.kt
nodes.summary: The airing-state chip and the small info chip used on sequel cards. Each status carries its own icon as well as its own colour, because encoding the difference in hue alone made Airing and Upcoming the same shape in two greens: unreadable for a colour-blind reader and in a grayscale screenshot.
nodes.languageNotes: SequelInfoChip deliberately has no animateColorAsState: the target was a constant, so the animation only allocated a clock and recomposed every frame inside a card that recomposes on every scroll frame.

nodes.name: SequelStatusChip
nodes.summary: Maps AniList's airing status to a label, a container colour and a semantic icon: a radio button for the state that is live now, a clock for one that has not started, a pause for Hiatus, a check for Finished and an X for Cancelled.

nodes.name: SequelInfoChip
nodes.summary: A neutral icon-and-label chip for facts that are not a status, such as format or episode count. Its tint is read straight from the theme because a colour animation toward a constant can never run.

nodes.name: InfoExternalLinksSection.kt
nodes.summary: The title's official links as capsule chips, deduplicated and filtered to drop entries with no site or URL and to exclude STREAMING, which Where to Watch already owns. Listing Crunchyroll in both made the page look like it had two copies of the same section.
nodes.languageNotes: AniList's externalLinks is community-editable, so a link missing a site name or a URL is dropped rather than drawn as a chip that opens nothing.

nodes.name: InfoExternalLinksSection
nodes.summary: Renders one chip per official link, each 44dp tall so the taps that leave the app are not the smallest targets in a wrapping row, and hands the URL to the shared open-or-copy helper.

nodes.name: InfoWhereToWatch.kt
nodes.summary: The services AniList says carry this title, as name-plus-outbound-arrow chips rather than brand logos, because the app has a vectors-only rule and the site name is the part that carries the meaning. A service with no browser to answer the tap still leaves the URL on the clipboard.
nodes.languageNotes: It is its own card rather than a row in Extras because availability is a fact a reader deciding what to watch needs above the synopsis, while Extras is what the page can do with a title.

nodes.name: InfoWhereToWatchCard
nodes.summary: Draws the Where to Watch card with a region caveat and one 48dp chip per streaming service, sized for a wrapping row where a miss lands on the neighbouring service.

nodes.name: EngagementAction.kt
nodes.summary: One icon-and-count control for likes, comment counts and reply counts. It was private to the activity card until a second caller appeared; re-declaring it inside the comments sheet would have been four visual details free to drift apart, and the drift is invisible until two controls meant to match do not.
nodes.languageNotes: Long press runs through combinedClickable with hapticFeedbackEnabled = false and a hand-played LongPress, because the modifier performs its own long-press haptic and leaving both on would buzz twice.

nodes.name: EngagementAction
nodes.summary: A like, a comment count or a reply count as one 48dp control with an optional long press for the list of people who liked it. Its enabled flag is load-bearing: a signed-out reader gets isLiked == null rather than false, and a heart that renders and does nothing is the one state this control must never be in.

nodes.name: SavedCopyPill.kt
nodes.summary: The 'Saved copy' badge that marks a screen painted from the device's snapshot because the network did not answer. Painting the cache instead of a spinner is a better cold start, but it created a new way to mislead: a list from yesterday drawn exactly like a list from a minute ago.
nodes.languageNotes: The caller's modifier goes on the pill rather than on AnimatedVisibility, because padding on the wrapper would reserve a permanent gap under the username for a badge that is not drawn. The clock glyph is used rather than a Wi-Fi slash since staleness can come from a 500, a timeout or a dead host.

nodes.name: SavedCopyPill
nodes.summary: A pill that springs in when a screen falls back to saved data and springs out faster when a live answer lands, so the app reads as having caught up rather than as a balloon deflating.

nodes.name: QuickAddPreferences.kt
nodes.summary: DataStore-backed settings for the quick-add button: the hold duration that turns Planning into Currently Watching, and whether the horizontal swipe gesture is enabled. Both the read and the write normalise the duration to 3 or 5 seconds, so a stale or hand-edited value cannot arm a timer nobody chose.
nodes.languageNotes: One preferencesDataStore delegate per file, exposed as a Flow of a settings snapshot; the persisted value and what the UI draws cannot disagree because the same coercion runs on both paths.

nodes.name: QuickAddPreferences
nodes.summary: The repository the Settings card and the dashboard's quick-add control read and write. It is the only owner of the hold-duration and swipe keys, so the gesture's timing is a stored preference rather than a constant compiled into the button.

nodes.name: QuickAddSettings
nodes.summary: The immutable snapshot the UI collects: the hold duration in seconds and whether swiping is enabled, with the millisecond conversion done once here so callers do not each multiply by a thousand.

nodes.name: SectionHeading.kt
nodes.summary: The icon-and-title heading over a row that bleeds to the screen edge, rather than over a card. It moved out of the Info page's talent file when the person sheet needed the same heading, because a second copy is how two sheets start to disagree about what a heading looks like.
nodes.languageNotes: The horizontal inset arrives on the modifier rather than being applied here, because hardcoding 20dp silently doubled the inset where the page had already padded it.

nodes.name: SectionHeading
nodes.summary: An accent icon and a bold title, with the title marked as a semantics heading so TalkBack can jump between the cast, crew, relations and rankings landmarks instead of reading them as four more stops in a linear read.

nodes.name: ScoreBadge.kt
nodes.summary: AniList's community score over a poster as a capsule. One component rather than the three private copies it replaced, because those copies had already drifted to three paddings and two shapes across posters a reader can see within two taps of each other, which read as unreliability rather than as design.
nodes.languageNotes: The scrim is Color.Black rather than a theme colour because the artwork beneath it is arbitrary; the badge is deliberately not accent-tinted like the role pill, so a value does not read as another label.

nodes.name: ScoreBadge
nodes.summary: The score pill drawn over artwork. It is the one number a poster cannot carry, and it belongs where the eye already is rather than in the text stack below the cover.

nodes.name: TierPlacementSheets.kt
nodes.summary: The four bottom sheets the tier board opens - move a poster, add unranked titles, manage tiers and rename a label. Split out of a screen file that had passed 1,500 lines because a sheet's job is to hand one decision back to the caller while the board's is to arrange posters, and the two change for different reasons.
nodes.languageNotes: Everything is `internal` except the shared rename field; the add-titles flow deliberately keeps both steps inside one ModalBottomSheet because two sheets presented at once is the documented way to reach 'only one sheet can be presented'.

nodes.name: TierPlaceSheet
nodes.summary: The sheet that moves one already-placed title between tiers. It opens on the cover rather than on the title alone, because a sheet about a poster that showed only a string read as being about the wrong thing.

nodes.name: TierAddTitlesSheet
nodes.summary: The 'start empty' route: pick an unranked title, then pick its tier, both inside one sheet. Picking a title replaces the sheet's contents instead of opening a second sheet, and returns to the unranked list after each placement so filing one title flows into the next.

nodes.name: TierManageSheet
nodes.summary: Rename, add, recolour, band and remove tiers, plus the one undoable destructive action ('empty every tier'). Removing a tier drops its entries instead of promoting them, and the confirmation says so in the reader's terms because a bare 'Delete tier?' would cost somebody an afternoon of ranking to one tap.

nodes.name: TierManageRowActions
nodes.summary: The bundle of callbacks one tier row may invoke, kept together so the row itself stays about laying out a caption, swatch, band and two buttons. Remove is a request to open the confirmation, not to delete, because the dialog needs the member count and the sheet's shared pending state.

nodes.name: TierRenameField
nodes.summary: A short text field with confirm and cancel, shared by tier and list renaming so a row caption and a list name cannot drift to different rules. The character cap is displayed rather than silently enforced, because a field that stops accepting input reads as a broken keyboard.

nodes.name: ProfileStateViews.kt
nodes.summary: The waiting and failure states for the Profile, Library and activity feed: a deliberately quiet error body with two honest exits, a 'still counting' note for the window between the profile and the media list, and three skeletons shaped like the rows they stand in for.
nodes.languageNotes: Skeletons take a hoisted `State<Float>` shimmer phase so one driver animates a whole stack; the error body seeds its joke from a remembered attempt counter because the ViewModel does not republish Loading on a retry.

nodes.name: ProfileLoadingView
nodes.summary: A spinner and a sentence, not shimmer cards: the profile is one header and a few rows whose shape depends entirely on what the person pinned, so a skeleton of the wrong shape would be a lie for the length of the fetch.

nodes.name: ProfileErrorView
nodes.summary: The calm failure body for the Profile and Library pages. It replaced the dashboard's full-screen error theatre, which over content somebody was already reading pushed the retry button off-screen and read as a production that happened to their list; a dead session offers sign-in instead of a retry that would fail identically.

nodes.name: PendingDataNote
nodes.summary: 'Still counting' for the window in which the profile has arrived but the media list has not. Rendering zeroes there would be a wrong answer rather than a wait, and a spinner over the whole tab would discard the charts that did arrive.

nodes.name: ActivityFeedSkeleton
nodes.summary: The activity feed's waiting state drawn as the cards that are coming. The tab used to show a lone spinner where twenty-five dense rows were about to appear, so opening it twice looked like two different screens; the feed is the one place whose row shape is known in advance.

nodes.name: CommentRowsSkeleton
nodes.summary: Three comment rows' worth of shimmer for the comment sheet, with per-row name and body widths varied so the stack reads as text arriving rather than as a table of grey rectangles.

nodes.name: PersonRowsSkeleton
nodes.summary: An avatar and a name per row for the likers sheet and the Social tab, parameterised on avatar size, avatar shape and padding because those are the only ways the two lists differ.

nodes.name: TierTray.kt
nodes.summary: The unranked pool drawn as a fixed shelf under the board, with long-press drag into a tier. It is deliberately outside the shared domain layout because the pool is the workspace you rank from, not part of the exported tier list, and drops are resolved in window pixels because the tray and the scrolling board have different origins.
nodes.languageNotes: Pointer maths is done in window pixels with density read outside the pointerInput block; the drag holder is hoisted so the ghost can be a sibling of the board rather than a child of the clipping Surface.

nodes.name: TierTrayDrag
nodes.summary: The in-flight tray drag, hoisted so the tray can write it and the screen's overlay can read it. It keeps the finger position and the poster's top edge separately, and remembers where in the tile the finger landed so the ghost keeps the same grip instead of snapping to the tile's left edge.

nodes.name: TierRowBand
nodes.summary: A tier row's top and bottom in window pixels, published by the board so the tray can test a release against real positions instead of converting between two coordinate spaces.

nodes.name: tierRowAt
nodes.summary: Which tier row a release at a window position lands in, or null. A null means un-file the title, which is a real instruction here - dropping a poster back into the tray is how a mis-drop is undone - and a near miss in a gap snaps to the nearest edge within a slop while a deliberate miss files nothing.

nodes.name: TierTray
nodes.summary: The bottom-pinned pool of unranked posters. It is pinned rather than placed after the last row so it stays reachable for the whole ranking session and the screen can reserve exactly its height, and its header is a full-width tap target that opens the name-based picker for when the two-hundredth title is too far to swipe.

nodes.name: trayItemAt
nodes.summary: Which poster slot a long-press landed on, answered by arithmetic over equal-width slots rather than a scan. It returns an index so the answer cannot go stale, and `internal` so a test can pin it against the same constants the tray lays posters out with - the two drifting apart picks up the poster next to the finger.

nodes.name: TierTrayGhost
nodes.summary: The poster being carried out of the tray, drawn as a sibling of the board because the tray's Surface clips its content. The lift is applied in graphicsLayer so it costs a repaint rather than a recomposition, and it carries no caption because a caption under a moving poster is unreadable at any speed.

nodes.name: ProfileActivityCard.kt
nodes.summary: One row of the profile activity feed: a blurred, downscaled cover behind the card, a 2:3 poster, a status pill, a progress sentence and the like/comment controls. The blur and the 220px decode budget exist because a sharp crop fought the card's own text and a full-resolution decode per scrolling row was the busiest thing the feed did.
nodes.languageNotes: Coil requests are remembered by (coverUrl, context) so recompositions hit the cache, and the blur relies on Modifier.blur's API 31 render effect, which is the app's whole supported range.

nodes.name: ActivityCard
nodes.summary: The feed's card: blurred ambient cover, poster, status pill and the like/comment row. Manga is detected case-insensitively because the model documents `type` as the discriminator the feed depends on, and the press spring shares one interaction source with clickable so scrolling does not leave the card squashed.

nodes.name: activityDetail
nodes.summary: The sentence under the status pill: 'Episode 7 of 24' while watching, the format alone when there is no progress. Progress is only paired with a total when the media node actually has one, since 'Episode 7 of 0' is worse than no second line, and manga is worded as chapters because the query never fetches a manga's chapter total.

nodes.name: formatLabel
nodes.summary: Spells AniList's MediaFormat enum the way a person writes it. `format.lowercase()` produced 'Tv' on every feed row without progress, because the field is an enum name rather than a word.

nodes.name: AppExtraVectors.kt
nodes.summary: The custom ImageVector glyphs that need more drawing than a single path: franchise branch, double check, calendar clock, grass tuft and library shelf. Every one carries a comment recording what the previous geometry did wrong at the size it actually renders, since these are hand-drawn and the failures are invisible until the icon is 16-22dp.
nodes.languageNotes: Vectors are built lazily with ImageVector.Builder and SolidColor(Color.White) so the theme tint applies; no PNG, SVG, XML drawable or emoji is involved.

nodes.name: AppExtraVectors
nodes.summary: The object holding the five hand-drawn vectors, kept apart from AppVectorIcons so the file that only aggregates icons stays readable. The glyphs cover the franchise relation branch, completed/synced badge, next-airing countdown, the 'go touch grass' off-ramp and the Library destination.

nodes.name: ArrivingCard.kt
nodes.summary: The 'currently arriving' card for airing or announced anime, the artwork-free compact list used for lower data and battery cost, and the meta line that says which episode is next or when a show starts.

nodes.name: ArrivingCard
nodes.summary: A 148dp poster card for one arriving title, with the cover's own dominant colour as the placeholder tint and the next-episode countdown riding on the artwork so the schedule is visible before the poster loads.

nodes.name: CompactArrivingList
nodes.summary: The same arriving titles as a text-and-swatch list with no artwork, for the lower data and battery mode; dividers are drawn between rows but not after the last one.

nodes.name: arrivalMeta
nodes.summary: The one-line schedule label under the status chip: 'Ep 7 / 24', 'Airing now', 'Starts <date>' or 'Start date TBA', degrading at each missing field rather than printing a partial sentence.

nodes.name: TierBoardToolbar.kt
nodes.summary: The two pills that float over the tier board - undo/redo/export and lock/zoom stepper - split out of the chrome file once the lock and export actions joined them, because a zoom step recomposes this file and nothing above it.
nodes.languageNotes: Controls are 36dp Boxes with clickable rather than IconButtons, because material3 wraps IconButton in the 48dp minimum interactive component and Modifier.size only shrinks the glyph's box.

nodes.name: TierHistoryControls
nodes.summary: Undo, redo and export at the bottom of the board rather than in the app bar: a drop is made with a thumb near the bottom, so the control that takes it back belongs within reach, and the bar already carries the list name, filter and tier editor. Undo and redo stay drawn and disabled when their stacks are empty, because a control that appears under a thumb gets pressed by accident.

nodes.name: TierZoomControls
nodes.summary: The lock plus zoom out/percentage/in stepper. The percentage is a button as well as a readout because the common case after pinching to an unreadable zoom is 'put it back', and 36dp buttons exist because seven 48dp controls would need over 400dp and not fit beside the board on a 360dp screen.

nodes.name: CompactTierButton
nodes.summary: One 36dp icon in the floating pills. A plain IconButton cannot be this small because material3 enforces the 48dp minimum interactive component, so a Box with clickable is the honest way to ask for a smaller target while the icon's content description keeps it the same control to TalkBack.

nodes.name: UserOverviewUiState.kt
nodes.summary: The profile screen's state contract, split from the ViewModel so the screen can read what it switches over without scrolling through the load pipeline. Success flattens AniList's nested favourites into five lists and carries the whole anime list the Library page reuses, so adding a tab of hundreds of entries cost no extra request.
nodes.languageNotes: Comments on isLibraryLoading, libraryError and isCached each record a shipped failure: zeroes presented as an answer, a failed list fetch flattened to 'no list', and a cached page presented as live.

nodes.name: UserOverviewUiState
nodes.summary: The sealed Loading/Success/Error contract for the profile's Home and Stats tabs; every branch is something the screen switches over, and none of them holds a repository, coroutine or behaviour.

nodes.name: UserOverviewUiState.Success
nodes.summary: The loaded profile: flattened favourites, AniList's aggregates, the three distributions AniList does not aggregate, the activity calendar and the flattened anime list. isLibraryLoading, libraryError and isCached distinguish a list still counting, a list that could not be read and a page served from disk, because each of those was once shown as a confident wrong answer.

nodes.name: UserOverviewUiState.Error
nodes.summary: A failed profile load, carrying whether a retry could work and whether the session is dead, plus the optional classified AniList failure so the screen can pick specific words instead of a generic message. kind is nullable so demo mode and older construction paths do not have to invent a classification.

nodes.name: ProfileStatsSummaryCard.kt
nodes.summary: The six-number summary of a list, laid out as two rows of three so it reads as three pairs - how much, how long, how highly rated - instead of a column of six figures that becomes a scroll of its own.

nodes.name: SummaryCard
nodes.summary: Renders anime count, episodes, watch time, mean score, standard deviation and manga count from the loaded profile. 'Days Watched' is derived from AniList's minutes because nobody wants their total minutes, and the first cell is labelled 'Anime' rather than 'Total' because it sits beside a manga count it does not include.

nodes.name: ProfileComponents.kt
nodes.summary: The shared building blocks of the profile tabs: section headers, the four pinned-favourites rows and the empty line they all fall back to. Extracted so the seven headers across four tabs and the two people rows cannot drift into different shapes, sizes or captions.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Compose: LazyRow and FlowRow carousels, Coil AsyncImage with vector placeholders, and bouncyPress wired to a shared MutableInteractionSource so a press cancels when a row scroll starts.

nodes.name: ProfileSectionHeader
nodes.summary: Icon tile plus title plus optional trailing count, matching the Settings screen's section header. Shared rather than redeclared because the profile has seven of these and a favourites header should look like the Settings heading above it; marks the title as a TalkBack heading since the tabs are long.

nodes.name: FavouriteMediaRow
nodes.summary: Horizontal LazyRow of pinned anime or manga covers, capped at the profile content width so a 200dp cover does not fill a tablet. Titles sit under the artwork instead of on a gradient because AniList covers already carry their own vertical typography.

nodes.name: FavouriteCharacterRow
nodes.summary: The pinned-characters row. Takes the tapped person rather than a URL, because where the tap goes is the screen's decision - the in-app profile sheet when a repository exists, the browser only as fallback; it previously took a URL and was the one row that left the app.

nodes.name: FavouriteStaffRow
nodes.summary: The pinned-staff row, split back out from characters because a character is a figure an account likes while a staff member is a professional whose work they follow. Captions the person's primary occupation, falling back to the favourites count rather than the word Staff.

nodes.name: FavouriteStudioRow
nodes.summary: Pinned studios as wrapping capsule chips that open the studio page by AniList id. Capsules rather than portraits because studios have no image, and the chips became buttons because they looked exactly like controls while being the only favourites row that went nowhere; a studio with no id is drawn as inert text.

nodes.name: EmptyFavourites
nodes.summary: The one 'nothing here yet' block every favourites row falls back to, so an empty row on the profile looks the same wherever it appears.

nodes.name: TierBoardChrome.kt
nodes.summary: Everything around the tier board rather than on it: progress header, filter/orphan notices, the two distinct empty states and the gesture legend. Split out of the screen file because that file was simultaneously doing gestures, geometry and explanation, and the toolbar left for its own file once lock and export pushed this one past a reviewable length.
nodes.languageNotes: All internal-visible composables plus one pure formatting function; the progress bar is drawn as two boxes rather than a LinearProgressIndicator so the track and indicator only need one capsule restyle.

nodes.name: TierBoardHeader
nodes.summary: Ranked-of-total line, an animated progress capsule and the Add action. The bar exists because a ranking is a quantity of work and 'almost done' versus 'just started' should read at a glance; the undo label shares the subtitle slot so it does not cost a second row of chrome that pushes the first tier off screen.

nodes.name: TierNotice
nodes.summary: One line of informational reporting with a close button only when there is something to close; the orphan notice has none because it reports the current state of the data, not a message someone sent.

nodes.name: TierFilterNotice
nodes.summary: The 'N titles hidden by filters' strip with a way back into the filter sheet. Dismissless by design: dismissing it would not change what is hidden, so it goes away when the filters do.

nodes.name: TierBoardNotices
nodes.summary: Owns the three lines the board can show above its rows, including the rule that the filter notice is suppressed while the filtered empty state already explains the same thing. Uses AnimatedContent for the dismissible message so dismissing shrinks the text instead of collapsing an empty box.

nodes.name: TierFilteredEmptyState
nodes.summary: The board when every ranked title is hidden by filters. Kept distinct from the unranked empty state because offering the seeding button here would invite someone to overwrite a list they already built.

nodes.name: TierEmptyState
nodes.summary: The unranked empty state, offering both ways out: seed from AniList scores or place titles by hand. States the unscored count before the button, because seeding correctly skips unscored titles and a person expecting 271 posters should be told where the other twelve went.

nodes.name: TierBoardLegend
nodes.summary: The gesture legend under the board, which says the one non-obvious thing: releasing off every row takes a title out of the list. It exists because a long press and a pinch are both invisible, and it swaps to lock instructions when drag is locked.

nodes.name: tierListSubtitle
nodes.summary: Builds the subtitle under the screen title as counts rather than a claim, with 'library has not loaded yet' as its own case so '0 of 0 ranked' never reads as a statement about the person's account.

nodes.name: ProfileHeaderCard.kt
nodes.summary: The identity head of the profile: a 260dp pannable banner with a bottom-weighted scrim, an overlapping squircle avatar, the username, cached-copy and membership chips, two count tiles and a quieter strip of derived totals. The banner height and the avatar's off-scale 24dp radius are both deliberate and documented against a past sweep that 'tidied' them.
nodes.languageNotes: Consumes UserOverviewUiState.Success directly and delegates the pannable artwork to PannableBackdrop; the avatar's two borders (surface ring plus hairline outline) exist because the ring alone vanished on a dark banner.

nodes.name: ProfileHeaderCard
nodes.summary: Composes the profile head: banner, overlapping avatar, name, saved-copy pill, identity chips, Anime/Manga tiles and the summary strip. The avatar overlaps the banner's bottom edge because the overlap is what ties the portrait to the artwork instead of reading as two stacked blocks.

nodes.name: HeaderSummaryStrip
nodes.summary: Episodes, watch time and mean score as one quiet card rather than three more tiles, because those answer 'how much did it amount to' - a fact about the person's time - not 'how many lists'. Uses the same formatters as the Stats tab so the header and the charts cannot disagree.

nodes.name: Banner
nodes.summary: The banner artwork with its scrim, or a themed gradient and sparkle mark when the account has no banner. The scrim's stops stay at low alpha above the midpoint because the backdrop is pannable, so a heavy scrim would darken different artwork depending on where the reader stopped dragging.

nodes.name: IdentityMetaRow
nodes.summary: Membership, last-updated and joined dates as wrapping capsule chips, replacing the two stacked rows they used to cost while keeping the membership line first and emphasised.

nodes.name: HeaderStat
nodes.summary: One count tile with a coloured icon chip, so Anime and Manga are distinguishable at a glance without reading the labels.

nodes.name: ProfileStatsTab.kt
nodes.summary: The Stats tab, which deliberately mixes two sources on one screen: AniList's aggregate User.stats for status/format/score/genre/tag, and local tallies of the downloaded media list for country, release year, watch year and episode bands, none of which AniList publishes in aggregate. Keeps section and scroll state hoisted so a tab switch does not lose either.
nodes.languageNotes: Contributes items into a single LazyColumn per section rather than nesting a child LazyColumn, so a section swap replaces the list instead of creating a second viewport.

nodes.name: ProfileStatsTab
nodes.summary: The tab's composition root: a loading note while entry tallies are still being counted, the section selector, and the chosen chart group. Section and list state are parameters because a remember inside the tab would be disposed with it on every tab switch.

nodes.name: overviewCharts
nodes.summary: Emits every distribution read in one pass: summary, score, episode, status, format, and conditionally country, release year and watch year. Kept as a named LazyListScope extension so the section `when` reads as three destinations instead of seventy lines of cards.

nodes.name: genreChart
nodes.summary: The genre table, rendered even when empty because 'nothing recorded yet' is a true answer to the question the chip asked; the card used to be added conditionally, which made the section unable to exist at all.

nodes.name: tagChart
nodes.summary: The tag table, unconditional for the same reason as the genre chart and with a wider label column because tag names run long.

nodes.name: ScoreDistributionCard
nodes.summary: The score chart, coloured per row by score band so scanning it shows which scores are high rather than only which are common - which is why BarChartCard takes a barColor override.

nodes.name: FormatDistributionCard
nodes.summary: Format as a segmented strip plus a share table rather than a bar chart, because the four formats are shares of one whole and the comparison people make is between parts.

nodes.name: scoreColor
nodes.summary: Maps a score fraction onto the app's status colours so the 'high score' green in the chart is the same green as the success chip elsewhere.

nodes.name: ProfileChartComponents.kt
nodes.summary: The reusable chart primitives for the Stats tab: the shared six-slot palette, the card shell every chart is built from, the segmented status strip, the generic bar chart and one bar row. Written once because four hand-written card headers had already settled at three different heights.
nodes.languageNotes: Bars animate their width with animateFloatAsState and draw in the draw phase via drawBehind; each row collapses its label and count into one clearAndSetSemantics description because a bar is a picture a screen reader cannot see.

nodes.name: chartSlotColor
nodes.summary: The six-slot chart palette, walked in order so the first status segment and the first format bar are the same colour and the two cards are comparable at a glance. Uses theme roles rather than hardcoded hex because a fixed ramp stops being readable on a light wallpaper-derived theme.

nodes.name: ChartCard
nodes.summary: The Stats tab's card shell: icon tile, title, optional trailing count and arbitrary content. Written once so every chart header lands at the same height instead of the three heights the hand-written ones had drifted to.

nodes.name: StatusDistributionCard
nodes.summary: Status as a horizontally scrolling row of count chips over one share strip, rather than four bars, because the question is what the list is made of. The chips scroll instead of wrapping so the card is the same height for every account.

nodes.name: SegmentStrip
nodes.summary: A Canvas strip of share-proportional segments with a 1% floor, because one entry in three hundred is about a pixel and a zero-width segment is not there at all - the documented constant existed but was unused, so those statuses stayed invisible. One content description covers the whole strip since a picture needs a sentence.

nodes.name: BarChartCard
nodes.summary: The generic horizontal bar chart used for episodes, country, years, genres and tags. Bar widths come from BucketTally.share computed in the use case, so every chart on the tab scales identically and a chart of years is comparable to a chart of episodes.

nodes.name: BarRow
nodes.summary: One labelled bar with a 2% minimum share and a single semantic description. Shared with the score chart, which is the same row with a different colour per row instead of one hue.

nodes.name: ProfileHomeTab.kt
nodes.summary: The Home tab: header card, markdown About bio, then one section per pinned favourites kind. Pinned anime and manga open the in-app detail sheet, and characters and staff open the same in-app profile sheet a title's cast rows use, with the browser kept only as the fallback when no repository exists.
nodes.languageNotes: Takes nullable onOpenCharacter/onOpenStaff callbacks rather than no-ops, because a portrait that looks tappable and does nothing is worse than one that opens the AniList page; the LazyListState is hoisted by the screen so AnimatedContent disposal does not reset scroll.

nodes.name: ProfileHomeTab
nodes.summary: Assembles the Home tab as one LazyColumn of keyed items, emitting each favourites section only when it has content and a single empty block when nothing is pinned. Characters and staff stay two sections because they are two different bonds, not one list of people.

nodes.name: StudioTitleCard.kt
nodes.summary: One title on a studio's shelf: poster, name under the artwork, and a format/count line. Deliberately not SequelPoster, which is built around a MissedSequel and a 'you have not seen this' story - forcing a studio's two hundred bare credits into that shape would mean inventing a fake parent for each.
nodes.languageNotes: Tap opens the detail sheet and hold opens the full-screen artwork via expressiveHoldGesture on the whole column, so the caption is part of the target; the poster tint is one solid colour because AsyncImage covers it immediately.

nodes.name: StudioTitleCard
nodes.summary: The shelf card itself: 2:3 poster with a tinted placeholder, score badge overdrawn in the corner because the score is how a reader picks which credit to open, and the title below the art so a gradient does not hide the one thing being scanned.

nodes.name: studioTitleMeta
nodes.summary: Builds 'TV · 12 eps' or 'Manga · 96 chs' and drops the count entirely when AniList does not know it, because a zero there is the API saying it has no count and '0 eps' would be a claim.

nodes.name: ProfileCard.kt
nodes.summary: The signed-in account card at the top of Settings: avatar, name, an explicit 'Signed in to AniList' badge and the anime entry count, with a button that opens the profile on AniList. The avatar falls back to a brand-mark vector so a 404 leaves a visible mark rather than an empty circle.
nodes.languageNotes: AsyncImage uses the same rememberVectorPainter for placeholder, error and fallback, so a slow or broken fetch never renders a blank circle.

nodes.name: ProfileCard
nodes.summary: Renders the ViewerProfile as a settings card and exposes one action, opening the AniList profile in the browser; the statistics row is omitted when AniList returned no anime count rather than showing a zero.

nodes.name: QuickAddSectionCard.kt
nodes.summary: Settings section for the quick-add gestures: the hold duration that promotes a Planning entry to Currently Watching, and the swipe-to-watch toggle. Reads and writes QuickAddPreferences through a collected StateFlow, with each write launched from a rememberCoroutineScope.
nodes.languageNotes: collectAsState with an explicit initial QuickAddSettings() so the first frame shows the defaults instead of a blank selector.

nodes.name: QuickAddSectionCard
nodes.summary: The card: a two-tab ExpressiveTabBar for the 3s/5s hold duration and a SwitchRow for swipe-to-watch, both writing straight through to the preferences repository. There is no local state, so the UI cannot disagree with what is persisted.

nodes.name: AniListMarkdownParser.kt
nodes.summary: Tokenizer and AST parser for AniList-flavoured markdown: headings, blockquotes, spoilers, checklists, img()/youtube()/webm() embeds, raw HTML image tags and AniList entity links. Every pattern is written against a failure a reader actually saw, and a bounded process-wide parse cache keeps the same bio from being re-tokenised by the profile card, the detail sheet and the comment thread.
nodes.languageNotes: A single `object` of pre-compiled `Regex` constants plus a synchronised access-ordered LinkedHashMap cache; HTML entities are decoded in one pass over the whole document because a chain of `replace` calls decodes `&lt;` twice.

nodes.name: AniListMarkdownParser
nodes.summary: The stateless-looking singleton that owns every block and inline pattern plus the 200-entry parse cache. It is an object rather than an instance because a parse must be free the second time it happens, wherever in the app that is.

nodes.name: parse
nodes.summary:
The public entry point: checks the cache, normalises line endings and `
` before decoding entities once, then walks the blocks. A failed parse returns one plain paragraph instead of propagating, because this runs on the Compose main thread over text nobody in the app wrote and used to force-stop the screen that was drawing it.

nodes.name: parseDecoded
nodes.summary: The block loop over already-decoded text, split from parse so a re-parsed `~~~center` slice is not decoded a second time. Every branch is required to advance the line cursor, and an unclaimed `|` line is emitted as a paragraph because the paragraph loop refuses pipe lines - the combination that used to spin the UI thread forever and ANR on a two-line table without a separator.

nodes.name: decodeHtmlEntities
nodes.summary: Turns the escapes AniList's rich-text editor leaves in a bio into the characters they name. One regex pass whose replacement is never re-scanned is what keeps `&lt;` printing as `<`; the previous replace-chain decoded it twice, and an undecoded `&` in an image query string made every such image 404.

nodes.name: parseInlines
nodes.summary: Collects a candidate match from every inline pattern and takes the one starting earliest, which is what keeps bold ahead of italic, `[![alt](img)](url)` ahead of a plain link, and inline images from leaving a stray `!` behind. Nesting is capped so a malformed run cannot recurse forever.

nodes.name: ActivityCommentsSheet.kt
nodes.summary: One activity's comment thread as a modal sheet with two modes - the list plus a pinned write bar, and a full editor - sharing one draft so Cancel never deletes what was typed. It also owns the reply-like control and hosts the manage dialog as a sibling window, and it only scrolls to a comment this session posted.
nodes.languageNotes: Explicit `fillMaxHeight` plus `weight(1f)` for the list: the sheet hands down a bounded height, and stating it is what keeps the composer pinned instead of pushed off-screen.

nodes.name: ActivityCommentsSheet
nodes.summary: The sheet itself: holds composing state, the draft, the reply target and the in-flight flag above both modes, because a post clears them and Cancel must not. Posting is gated on canPost while reading is not, since AniList serves replies to anyone but SaveActivityReply needs a session.

nodes.name: CommentsThread
nodes.summary: The thread half of the sheet: header, keyed LazyColumn and the bar that opens the editor. Split out because the loading, failed and empty branches each describe a whole screen rather than a row, leaving the sheet with only the draft and the mode switch.

nodes.name: CommentRow
nodes.summary: One comment: avatar, byline with relative time, markdown body, then a heart, a labelled Reply and - only on the viewer's own comment - the manage overflow. The heart is disabled rather than drawn as unliked when isLiked is null, because null means AniList did not answer.

nodes.name: clipDraft
nodes.summary: Applies ContentLimits to the text and to the selection together. TextFieldValue requires its caret to fall inside its own text, so clipping only the string throws from the constructor on a paste longer than the ceiling - and drops the IME composing range, which no longer describes anything.

nodes.name: InfoCards.kt
nodes.summary: The cards on a title's Info page - progress, synopsis, production details and the watched parent of a recommendation - all inside one shared InfoCard shell so a page of a dozen sections keeps one corner radius, inset and surface tone. Each card records the specific misread that shaped it, from a manga drawing an episode countdown to a synopsis toggle that appeared over nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the shared ExpressiveMotion.FastSpatialSize IntSize token for animateContentSize, because animating the synopsis height in one frame moved the button out from under the reader's finger.

nodes.name: InfoCard
nodes.summary: The container every Info section sits in: one shape, one inset, one surface tone, with an optional title row and trailing slot. Exists because the previous Specs tab mixed a trailer banner, bordered boxes and a bare grid on one scroll.

nodes.name: InfoProgressCard
nodes.summary: The viewer's progress as a wavy bar, and the next episode or chapter for a show that is still airing. It renders nothing when there is no progress rather than a 0% bar, since a zero bar is a claim about a title the viewer is not tracking at all.

nodes.name: InfoSynopsisCard
nodes.summary: The synopsis rendered through the app's markdown pipeline instead of stripped to plain text, so paragraph structure and the `(Source: ...)` credit line survive. Its expand toggle is gated on both the block count the renderer clips and the character hint, because a six-paragraph 200-character description used to lose two blocks with no cue at all.

nodes.name: InfoSpecsCard
nodes.summary: Production facts as a two-column grid with the main studio credits as tappable capsules. Only the isMain credits are drawn here because the Producers row owns the rest - drawing both printed Aniplex twice under two headings that looked like two different facts.

nodes.name: InfoParentCard
nodes.summary: The already-watched entry a franchise recommendation hangs off, with its own 2:3 poster rather than a bare title. A 48dp square crop used to cut the faces and the title off the parent's artwork.

nodes.name: StudioCreditChip
nodes.summary: One credited studio as a capsule that opens its page. Main credits are filled and the publishers and licensors are quieter rather than split into invented sections, and a credit with no id stays as a plain capsule because the name is still part of the answer.

nodes.name: PersonProfileSheet.kt
nodes.summary: A character's or a staff member's profile as a sheet over the title page, because a person is something you look at from a title rather than somewhere you go. One composable serves both kinds - the differences are which rows exist and what the heading says - and it swaps the person under an open sheet when a voice actor is tapped.
nodes.languageNotes: The body is keyed on `(kind, id)` so a swapped-in person does not inherit the previous page's scroll position; the height cap is a scrolling viewport rather than a clip.

nodes.name: PersonProfileSheet
nodes.summary: The sheet and its loading, failed and loaded branches. Nullable open-staff and open-character callbacks let a host without a repository draw those rows as captions instead of controls that could only fail.

nodes.name: LoadedPersonProfile
nodes.summary: The loaded body: hero, facts, voice actors, works, voiced characters, biography and an escape hatch to AniList, inside a capped vertical scroll. The works row comes before the biography because a long essay used to push the one row the page exists for below the viewport.

nodes.name: ProfileHero
nodes.summary: The portrait full-bleed behind a scrim that ends on the sheet's own container colour, with the portrait repeated as a rounded cover and the name over the artwork. Replaces an 84dp face clipped to a pill, a shape a portrait cannot be without losing its corners.

nodes.name: ProfileBiography
nodes.summary: The biography parsed through the same markdown pipeline the profile bio uses, and nothing at all when it is blank - a card with a heading over empty space is worse than no card.

nodes.name: ProfileVoiceActors
nodes.summary: Who performed a character, capped at four rows because a recast-heavy character otherwise turns a sheet into a wiki, each row opening that actor's own page in the same sheet when a callback is supplied.

nodes.name: AniListMarkdownBlocks.kt
