nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors widget_missed_sequels.xml structure exactly; the count and title are literals, the caption stays a string resource.

nodes.name: strings.xml
nodes.summary: The only string resource file in the app: the app name plus every piece of home-screen-widget copy. The widget descriptions are the sentences the Android 12+ widget picker prints under each tile, so they are written as descriptions of the tile rather than as repeats of the app name, and the `*_initial` entries are the placeholder text the RemoteViews layouts show in the gap between the tile being placed and its first update. Keeping the copy here rather than inline in Kotlin is what lets the picker, the initialLayout and the provider agree on one wording.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain `<string>` entries with `%1$s` positional formatting in `widget_featured_sequel_to`; the comments record which strings are picker copy versus initialLayout placeholders.

nodes.name: colors.xml
nodes.summary: Deliberately an empty `<resources />`. The stock template palette (purple_200/500/700, teal_200/700, black, white) was deleted because nothing referenced it — every colour the running app draws comes from Color.kt through the Compose theme. A second attempt to duplicate the launcher icon's blues here was also reverted: AAPT does not follow `@color` references into a `<gradient>` `<item>` inside a `<vector>`, so the icon's values had to stay literals and the copy would only have been a second brand palette able to drift. The file survives with its comment so the next reader does not re-add either set.
nodes.languageNotes: The entire content is a comment; the element is self-closing and empty on purpose.

nodes.name: themes.xml
nodes.summary: Defines the single platform theme the manifest applies to the activity, `Theme.MyApplication`, derived from `android:Theme.DeviceDefault.NoActionBar`. It exists so the window has no ActionBar before Compose draws its own top bar, and it deliberately pulls in no AppCompat or Material XML theme — the Material 3 Expressive look is entirely Compose-side, so a heavy XML theme would only be a second, drifting styling system.
nodes.languageNotes: One `<style>` with an `android:` platform parent, so no support-library theme dependency is needed.

nodes.name: update_file_paths.xml
nodes.summary: Declares the only two directories the app's FileProvider will hand to another app: files-path/updates for the downloaded release APK and cache-path/exports for the tier-board PNG. Both entries exist because a broad provider path would let any app naming the authority read downloaded releases or exported boards, and because each root must match exactly where the writer puts the file: the update root was left on cache-path after downloads moved to private files storage, so FileProvider.getUriForFile threw at runtime on the first Install press and every update reported 'This device has no app installer' while the download itself had succeeded. UpdateFileProviderPathsTest reads this file and compares the root with the directory UpdateManager actually writes to so the two cannot drift apart again.
nodes.languageNotes: No namespace and no schema declaration: FileProvider reads <paths> with the two root elements; the long comment records the shipped #61 regression that made the update root load-bearing.

nodes.name: widget_anisequel.xml
nodes.summary: AppWidgetProvider metadata for the profile-activity widget: a 2x2, resizable tile refreshed every 30 minutes that shows the user's current activity count. The header documents the three attributes that were wrong on a device: a missing initialLayout left the tile blank until the first onUpdate, a configure pointing at the AppWidgetProvider (not an Activity) made launchers report the app as not installed, and a previewImage duplicated previewLayout and was unreachable at the app's API 31 floor. The 40dp minimum height is deliberate so the count survives squashing while cover and title clip first.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain appwidget-provider XML with targetCellWidth/Height plus both min and max resize bounds; it is the reference declaration the other three widget files copy.

nodes.name: widget_featured_sequel.xml
nodes.summary: Metadata for the Featured Sequel widget, the one tile built to show a poster rather than a number, which is why it starts at 4x2 cells instead of 2x2. It repeats the declaration contract established by widget_anisequel.xml after the shipped v1.0.42 failure: initialLayout always present, no configure attribute pointing at the AppWidgetProvider, and previewLayout instead of previewImage because the app's floor is API 31.
nodes.languageNotes: Same attribute set as the other widget declarations; only geometry, layout and description references differ.

nodes.name: backup_rules.xml
nodes.summary: Pre-API-31 backup rules that exclude the DataStore directory, which holds the AniList OAuth access token. With the default empty rules the whole app data directory is uploaded to the user's Google backup and restored onto other hardware, carrying a live session token to a device the user has not protected the same way; re-signing in is one tap, so the exclusion costs nothing.
nodes.languageNotes: full-backup-content with a single <exclude domain="file" path="datastore/"/>; superseded by data_extraction_rules.xml from API 31, which is this app's floor.

nodes.name: data_extraction_rules.xml
nodes.summary: Android 12+ backup and device-transfer rules that keep the AniList OAuth token out of both cloud backup and direct device-to-device transfer, for the same reason as backup_rules.xml: a live session token should not land on another machine. Both halves of the file exclude the DataStore directory, so neither transfer path can carry the credential.
nodes.languageNotes: data-extraction-rules requires the exclusion to be repeated under cloud-backup and device-transfer; the two blocks are not inherited from each other.

nodes.name: widget_arriving_sequels.xml
nodes.summary: Metadata for the Arriving Sequels widget, a 2x2 resizable tile refreshed every 30 minutes that lists sequels whose release window has just opened. It carries no explanatory comment because it is a straight copy of the declaration contract in widget_anisequel.xml: initialLayout for the pre-onUpdate state, no configure component, previewLayout rather than previewImage.
nodes.languageNotes: Same geometry and 1800000 ms update period as widget_anisequel.xml; only layout, preview and description references change.

nodes.name: widget_missed_sequels.xml
nodes.summary: Metadata for the Missed Sequels widget, a 2x2 resizable tile refreshed every 30 minutes showing sequels the user has not picked up. It is the mirror of widget_arriving_sequels.xml and follows the same declaration contract as widget_anisequel.xml, with the layout and preview references swapped.
nodes.languageNotes: Identical attribute set to widget_arriving_sequels.xml; the only differences are the @layout and @string references.

nodes.name: Release changelog
nodes.summary: The changelog the app ships: 62 releases from 1.5.6 back to 1.0.22, newest first, each entry a title plus a paragraph of user-facing detail (358 entries in total). It feeds the Settings > Info "What's new" card and the release manifest, and it is pinned from both sides - ChangelogTest checks the format and that versions descend, VersionBaselineTest checks the newest version against gradle.properties, BASELINE_VERSION_NAME and update.json - which is why a feature change and a version bump have to land in the same commit.
nodes.languageNotes: One "versions" array of {version, entries: [{title, detail}]}. There are no timestamps and no version codes: the version string is the only key, so array order is the contract.

nodes.name: TierList.kt
nodes.summary: The pure domain model behind the profile's Tier List: tier definitions, candidate projections, placements, the filter that narrows them, score seeding and the placement edit. Deliberately free of Android, Compose and coroutines because one arrangement is drawn three ways - Compose on screen, a PNG by the board exporter and an SVG by the exporter's writer - and independent arrangements of the same list are exactly how a screen and its export start disagreeing. There is no position field: the ordered assignment map is the order.
nodes.languageNotes: Placement order is carried by rebuilding a LinkedHashMap, and every helper returns the same instance when nothing changed - a fresh equal value would be a new StateFlow value and recompose the board's whole arrangement.

nodes.name: TierDefinition
nodes.summary: One tier row: a stable id, an editable label, a packed ARGB colour and an optional AniList score floor. The id rather than the label is the identity so renaming "A" to "Excellent" does not orphan every entry filed under it, and the score floor lives on the tier because the module-level map of the six standard ids it replaced meant a custom tier could never have a band at all.

nodes.name: TierCandidate
nodes.summary: The handful of fields the board needs from a list entry, projected out so this layer does not depend on the AniList data models and so the exporters can be tested with literals instead of a nested object graph. listStatus and airingStatus stay as AniList's own uppercase tokens rather than enums, because an enum would need a translation layer whose only job is to be wrong for the status AniList adds next.

nodes.name: TierAssignment
nodes.summary: Which tier each media id sits in, as a map rather than a list of pairs so the screen can answer one lookup per frame while a card is being dragged. An entry absent from the map is unfiled, which is a legitimate state - it is what an empty tier list is - not an error to repair.

nodes.name: TierFilter
nodes.summary: What the board is currently holding back: list statuses, airing statuses, genres and studios, plus the switch for the studio section. Statuses are stored as hidden sets so a status AniList adds tomorrow stays visible without a code change; genres are a shown set because "only these" is the useful question for an open per-title vocabulary. Planning is hidden by default because a board of unscored, unwatched titles was what the screen used to open on.

nodes.name: seedFromScores
nodes.summary: Files scored candidates into the tier whose score floor they clear, highest floor first so the first floor a score passes is the tier it belongs to. Tiers without a floor are never assigned to, and unscored titles are returned unfiled rather than dropped into the bottom tier - that would present a judgement nobody made in the same typography as the ones they did.

nodes.name: withPlacement
nodes.summary: Files a title at a chosen position in a tier, or unfiles it when the tier is null. Dropping onto another poster has to mean "here, above this one" - the old move only knew a tier, so the title landed wherever its id happened to sit in the map. An anchor that is absent, or that is the dragged tile itself, resolves to the end of that tier rather than the end of the whole map.

nodes.name: withoutOrphans
nodes.summary: Drops every placement naming a tier that no longer exists, which is the invariant the feature rests on: a title is either in a tier that exists or in none. Storage can hold the other state - a document saved before a row was removed, or one written by an older build - and the repair belongs here because the board, the exports and the library's counts all read the same map.

nodes.name: onlyFor
nodes.summary: Keeps only the placements whose media id survives the active filter, preserving stored order, while keeping ids the library has no entry for. Hiding those would both drop a placement nobody filtered out and let the "hidden by filters" count blame the filter for a title it never judged.

nodes.name: Hct.kt
nodes.summary: A pure-Kotlin port of the parts of Google's material-color-utilities the app needs - CAM16, viewing conditions, HCT and the sRGB gamut solver - so Material 3 tonal palettes are derived by perceptual tone instead of HSL lightness. It exists because the HSL-derived palette let a yellow seed produce a primary at tone 40 that white text could not sit on while a blue seed at the same HSL lightness was comfortable; HCT's tone is CIELAB L*, so the 10/90 container pairs stay safe whatever hue the cover art is.
nodes.languageNotes: No Android imports, so the whole colour path is testable on the JVM. The gamut solve is two bounded bisections (18 tone steps, 10 chroma steps) and tonal palettes memoise tones because primary and surfaceTint ask for the same value.

nodes.name: Hct
nodes.summary: The HCT triple and its two conversions. fromInt takes tone straight from the colour's CIELAB L*, and from() reduces chroma rather than clipping channels when the requested triple falls outside sRGB - per-channel clipping preserves tone but not hue, which is how a saturated orange at tone 90 turns pink.

nodes.name: TonalPalette
nodes.summary: One hue and chroma sampled at any tone, memoised per tone. A scheme asks for the same few tones from each palette several times - primary and surfaceTint are the same colour - and the gamut solve is the expensive part of building a theme; the palette is immutable, so the cache can never go stale.

nodes.name: ColorMath
nodes.summary: The sRGB, XYZ and CIELAB arithmetic plus the WCAG relative-luminance and contrast-ratio helpers the colour types share, kept internal so the public types do not have to expose it. linearized and delinearized apply the sRGB transfer function on the 0..100 scale CAM16 expects.

nodes.name: ViewingConditions
nodes.summary: The CAM16 viewing conditions the palette is defined under: D65 white, a 200-lux adapting field, a 50% grey background and an average surround - a phone screen rather than a print shop. The rgbD factors are the chromatic-adaptation factors themselves and not scaled by each cone response; mixing the two produced a correct-looking luminance and a hue several degrees off Material's own output.

nodes.name: Cam16
nodes.summary: The two CAM16 dimensions HCT keeps, hue and chroma, plus the J/chroma/hue inverse the solver needs. Lightness is deliberately absent: HCT takes its tone from CIELAB L* because CAM16's J is not perceptually uniform with it, and the unused brightness, colourfulness and UCS coordinates are left out so solving one tone does not pay for them.

nodes.name: HctSolver
nodes.summary: Maps an HCT triple back into sRGB by bisecting for the CAM16 J that yields the requested tone and, when that colour lands outside sRGB, bisecting chroma down until it fits. The official library solves the same problem analytically in CAM16-UCS; the result agrees to within a rounding step and the search is easier to verify.

nodes.name: ApkDownloader.kt
nodes.summary: Streams a release APK into a `.part` file and continues one that is already there via a Range header. Split out of UpdateManager because an interrupted download restarting from zero (#64) was a second reason to change a class that was already over 500 lines judging releases: this half owns headers, offsets and buffering, verifies nothing and renames nothing, so only UpdateManager may move a file into its final name.
nodes.languageNotes: Blocking OkHttp call - the caller owns the dispatcher. Progress is emitted per 32 KB rather than per 8 KB read, so a 2.6 MB APK costs ~80 progress callbacks instead of ~325 recompositions of the dialog.

nodes.name: ApkDownloader
nodes.summary: The transfer itself: one request starting at the current offset, a single retry from zero when the server answers 416, and a size bound at twice the manifest's declared size so a URL serving something that is not the APK cannot fill the user's storage. The retry is bounded at one on purpose - looping on a broken server would spend a phone's battery.

nodes.name: planResume
nodes.summary: The pure decision of how a response lines up with the bytes already on disk. A 200 answering a request that carried a Range header means the body starts at byte zero, so appending it would put a megabyte of one release on the front of another - no length arithmetic catches that, so the plan discards the `.part` instead.

nodes.name: ResumePlan
nodes.summary: The three answers to "the server did not do what the Range header asked": where the response starts in the finished file, whether it is appended, and whether the existing `.part` is unusable. Kept apart from the transfer because this is the part of resuming that is easy to get subtly wrong and impossible to see.

nodes.name: TransferResult
nodes.summary: What one transfer into the `.part` produced: the byte total on success, or a message a person can read on failure. Sealed so the caller has to handle both, because the failure text is what the update dialog shows verbatim.

nodes.name: DemoDataProvider.kt
nodes.summary: The offline fixture shown when no AniList account is connected: a viewer, five completed franchises whose sequels are missing, two original titles for the arriving rows, and list entries spread over the trailing weeks so the profile's activity calendar has something to draw. Dates and the airing countdown are computed relative to today because a fixture pinned to a fixed year rots into looking like a broken feature.
nodes.languageNotes: Builds the AniList object graph by hand (MediaNode, MediaRelations, StudioConnection, MediaRelationEdge) so the relation walk has real SEQUEL edges to traverse; daysAgo() and airingAt are derived from Instant.now() at load time.

nodes.name: DemoDataProvider
nodes.summary: The single entry point for the demo account: a fake viewer and a media list collection shaped exactly like the GraphQL response, so every screen downstream cannot tell the difference between the demo and a real list.

nodes.name: getDemoViewer
nodes.summary: The fake viewer (OtakuExplorer, id 999999) with real AniList CDN artwork, so the profile screen has an avatar and a banner to draw without a network call.

nodes.name: getDemoMediaList
nodes.summary: The fixture list: Completed entries for Demon Slayer, Jujutsu Kaisen, Kaguya-sama, SPY x FAMILY and Frieren, each carrying its sequel as a SEQUEL relation so the missed-sequel walk finds something, plus a currently airing original and an unreleased one so the arriving section is populated and the countdown stays alive however old the build gets.

nodes.name: MutationCoalescer.kt
nodes.summary: Collapses a burst of writes for one key into the settled value, 600 ms after the taps stop. Built for the controls that follow the title editor - a progress stepper and a score slider - where a reader taps `+` five times in a second and AniList allows about thirty requests a minute; keyed per media id because two titles being edited at once are two writes and merging them would drop one.
nodes.languageNotes: Three concerns tracked per key (pending, inFlight, committed) under one plain lock; the job-identity check before committing is what stops a cancellation that lost the race from recording a newer value under an older job.

nodes.name: MutationCoalescer
nodes.summary: The coalescer: submit schedules a debounce, a write that lands records the committed baseline, and a failure is never retried here because the request may have landed and a second one would apply the change twice - the caller's result handling owns that decision.

nodes.name: submit
nodes.summary: Queues a value, cancelling any write still inside the window, and reports whether it changed the pending work. Two suppress rules matter: a value equal to the committed one with nothing in flight sends zero requests (like -> unlike -> like), and a value already in flight drops the queued compensation - but a revert while a different value is in flight must still be sent, which is the race that once lost a revert typed while the earlier request was on the wire.

nodes.name: flush
nodes.summary: Waits for the pending write for a key, including one already in flight, so a closing screen can let the last tap land before reporting the save complete. Before it counted in-flight work, closing after the debounce had elapsed returned immediately even though the request was still on the wire.

nodes.name: UserFilterOptions.kt
nodes.summary: The dashboard's filter vocabulary and its criteria object: sort order, airing status, format, relation kinds, hidden media ids and the two "this year" toggles. FilterCriteria.isNarrowing is the single definition of "filters are active" because three copies had drifted apart - the quick filter's version forgot hideAlreadyPlanned and the relation set, so a user who hid already-planned entries saw an unfiltered-looking dashboard with results missing.
nodes.languageNotes: Plain data classes and enums with no Android imports; every field has a default, so one criterion can be flipped without constructing the whole object.

nodes.name: FilterCriteria
nodes.summary: One immutable snapshot of what the dashboard is showing, plus the isNarrowing predicate the badge, the "Filtered" row and the empty-state choice all read. hiddenMediaIds is deliberately excluded from that predicate: hiding an anime is a standing decision about that anime rather than a view of the list, so it must not light a badge that never goes away.

nodes.name: SequelSortOption
nodes.summary: The five orders the sequel feed can be sorted by, each carrying its own display name so the sort sheet and the sort itself cannot disagree about the label.

nodes.name: StatusFilter
nodes.summary: The airing states a sequel can be narrowed to, including Hiatus and Cancelled. Those two were drawable on a card and unselectable in the filter - a dead end whose only route was scrolling the unfiltered list - so the enum was widened to the five statuses AniList actually has plus ALL, in the order the sheet draws them.

nodes.name: LibraryPreferences.kt
nodes.summary: Remembers the Library tab's own view choices - media type, status filter, sort and direction - in a dedicated DataStore. They used to be remember-style state inside the tab, which dies when the profile screen's AnimatedContent disposes the tab it animates away from, so every trip to Activity and back reset a narrowed "Completed, newest first" view to "All, list order". Only the choice is stored, never the resulting data: two caches answering "what does this person track" is how one of them starts lying.
nodes.languageNotes: preferencesDataStore delegate named anisequel_library_prefs; each value is exposed as a Flow<String?> where null means "never chosen", which is a real state rather than a missing default.

nodes.name: LibraryPreferences
nodes.summary: The four remembered choices and their setters, plus clearType and reset. reset exists partly as the Robolectric seam - every test shares one application context and this file lives on disk, so a stored choice would leak between them - and partly as the body of a future "reset library view" action.

nodes.name: setSort
nodes.summary: Writes the sort and its direction in a single DataStore edit because they are one choice. A torn pair would leave lastSort set with no direction, and treating a missing direction as ascending would silently re-answer a question the reader already answered.

nodes.name: RateLimitInterceptor.kt
nodes.summary: Absorbs the short rate-limit spikes AniList's burst limiter produces: on a 429 with a usable Retry-After it sleeps and retries exactly once, then hands the 429 back so the repository can report the real wait time. It is registered before AuthInterceptor, which makes it the outermost application interceptor, so the retry re-enters it and re-reads the bearer token - the difference between a retry that works after a token refresh and one that replays a stale Authorization header.
nodes.languageNotes: Injectable sleepMillis so the single retry path is testable without a real one-second sleep; MAX_RETRY_AFTER_SECONDS is 5, above which the penalty is reported to the user instead of hidden behind a spinner.

nodes.name: RateLimitInterceptor
nodes.summary: The interceptor itself. A negative Retry-After is treated as "no usable wait": it used to pass the upper-bound check (-1 is not greater than 5) and reach Thread.sleep(-1000), turning a "please slow down" 429 into an IllegalArgumentException thrown out of intercept on the OkHttp worker.

nodes.name: UpdateFormatting.kt
nodes.summary: The updater's two display formatters, kept out of UpdateManifest.kt so a pure display concern is not filed next to a policy decision - the wire model and the strings a person reads in one file meant UpdateManifestTest had to import a UI helper to check a unit conversion.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure top-level functions with no Android imports. isNewerThan deliberately stays on the manifest: it is a fact about a manifest relative to the installed build and already has dedicated tests.

nodes.name: formatBytes
nodes.summary: Human-readable size for the "12.4 MB" line under the update button. A null or negative size reads "unknown size" rather than a number the manifest did not actually declare.

nodes.name: formatRate
nodes.summary: Human-readable speed for the download line, empty below 1 KB/s. "Not moving" and "we do not know yet" are different things to read, and printing a rate that is really an absence of one would tell the user their download had stopped.

nodes.name: FlexibleStringAdapter.kt
nodes.summary: A Moshi adapter that accepts a JSON number, string, boolean or null where a String is declared. AniList types ListActivity.progress as a String - one episode or a range like "1 - 10" - but fixtures and alternative feeds serialize it as a number, and Moshi's default string adapter throws JsonDataException on the wrong token, which failed the whole query rather than one field.
nodes.languageNotes: An object extending JsonAdapter<String>; unknown tokens are skipped and answered as null instead of throwing, and writes are a plain string or null.

nodes.name: FlexibleStringAdapter
nodes.summary: The adapter: string and number tokens both go through nextString(), booleans through toString(), null stays null and anything else is skipped. Lenient on read so one loosely-typed field cannot take down a whole GraphQL response.

nodes.name: domain README
nodes.summary: The rule for the domain layer: anything decidable without a screen, a network call or a Context lives here and is therefore testable on a plain JVM. It states the no-Android-imports rule, the one-decision-per-use-case layout (usecase, tier, studio, motion) and the guidance that a ViewModel grown too large is fixed by extracting a value type here rather than by exposing more internal state.

nodes.name: MediaNodeDisplay.kt
nodes.summary: The single home for every display derivation read off a MediaNode and its edge types, so a recommendation row that wraps a parent and a bare arriving/activity node render through the same detail components instead of one of them inventing a fake parent. It also humanises every raw AniList enum (format, status, relation type) in one place, because each of those leaked into the UI as TV_SHORT, RELEASING or UNKNOWN at some point.
nodes.languageNotes: Extension properties on MediaNode, MediaRelationEdge and MediaCharacterEdge; private Regex constants strip AniList HTML and the (Source: …) line; no Android imports.

nodes.name: AniListModels.kt
nodes.summary: The Moshi wire model for every AniList document the app sends, with each field typed to what the server actually answers rather than what the schema name suggests, and with MediaNode.withDetail carrying the merge of a lazily fetched detail response over a thin summary node.
nodes.languageNotes: Every type is @JsonClass(generateAdapter = true) for KSP codegen; @Json(name = …) pins the wire name where the Kotlin name cannot match (season, private, staffMedia).

nodes.name: PersonProfile.kt
nodes.summary: Character and staff profile payloads plus the single sealed state the shared person sheet renders, including the flattening of edge-based media connections into filmographies and voice-actor rows so one composable can draw either kind of person.
nodes.languageNotes: Moshi wire types and mapped view types sit side by side; toLoadedState extensions convert either payload into PersonProfileState.Loaded.

nodes.name: ApiStatus.kt
nodes.summary: Turns an AniList failure or reachability probe into a verdict a reader can act on, replacing the one-size-fits-all 'Connection error' copy whose 'try again' advice was wrong for half the failures it covered. It also carries the error screen's voice: per-kind headlines, explanations and large deterministic joke pools so a retry loop does not repeat itself.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Kotlin enums, data classes and extension functions with no Android imports; joke selection is seeded by a caller-supplied string so recomposition cannot reshuffle it.

nodes.name: TierListCodec.kt
nodes.summary: The tier list's line-based on-disk format as pure functions, moved out of the Android DataStore class so the one part that can silently lose somebody's rankings is testable on the JVM. Every reader skips what it cannot parse and keeps what it can, because the failure mode of a strict parse here is not a crash but a successful load of an empty list.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately not JSON or a serialization library: pipe/comma/semicolon separated lines with a backslash escape, plus explicit legacy-shape handling.

nodes.name: AniSequel Gradle build
nodes.summary: The app module's build: compileSdk 36.1 with a minSdk 31 floor, an applicationId that cannot be changed because every install is pinned to it, R8 plus resource shrinking for release, and a dependency list that scopes preview tooling to debug builds only.
nodes.languageNotes: Version falls back to BASELINE_VERSION_NAME/CODE when gradle.properties is unreadable; VersionBaselineTest keeps the two copies in step. Signing falls back to the debug key when no release keystore is present.

nodes.name: TierListSvg.kt
nodes.summary: Writes an already-computed TierListLayout out as a standalone SVG, so an export is geometry and text rather than a screenshot that blurs. Posters are embedded as data URIs instead of linked because many viewers refuse remote hrefs, which would open the file as empty tiles.
nodes.languageNotes: Hand-built string output with XML escaping and Locale.ROOT number formatting; the palette is injected so this layer keeps no Android or Compose theme dependency.

nodes.name: ActivityEngagement.kt
nodes.summary: The reply-and-like payloads for the activity feed, kept apart from the feed's own parse types because these exist only while a comment sheet is open or a like is in flight and change only when the engagement features change.
nodes.languageNotes: Moshi data classes for the ActivityUnion, LikeableUnion and reply mutations, plus one mapped ActivityLikeState that resolves AniList's nullable count to zero once.

nodes.name: AndroidManifest.xml
nodes.summary: Declares the network, biometric and install-packages permissions, the singleTask MainActivity with its anisequel://oauth callback filter, the four home-screen widget receivers and the FileProvider the updater hands APKs to. The widget receiver entries are AppWidgetProviders directly because a forwarding BroadcastReceiver read EXTRA_APPWIDGET_ID, which the system never sends, so the widget never got its first update.
nodes.languageNotes: REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES is declared but only makes the app allowed to ask; the grant is per-app in Settings and is never prompted for at launch.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: The contract for the data layer: what each subpackage may import, why a field is only asked for when it is rendered, why one bad GraphQL argument costs the whole response, why ids must be keyed with their media namespace, and which snapshots survive a restart and for how long.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown tables for the package map and the snapshot windows, plus the invariants a change to the layer has to preserve.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: The contract for the presentation layer: composables take data and callbacks and never hold a NavController, transforms animate in the draw phase, remember needs keys, springs come from ExpressiveMotion, and capsules are percent-rounded shapes rather than stretched polygons.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown with a package table and a short ViewModels section; each rule names the shipped defect that produced it.

nodes.name: proguard-rules.pro
nodes.summary: The narrow R8 safety net for this app's own reflection surfaces: Moshi's generated adapters and @JsonClass models, Retrofit's generic signatures, and coroutine stack traces. Without it a minified release builds green and parses nothing at runtime.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately contains no -keep rule on androidx.compose: shrinking is on precisely because there are none.

nodes.name: AiringCountdown.kt
nodes.summary: Formats an AniList airingAt timestamp as 'in 3d' / 'in 5h' / 'in 30m' / 'now', shared by every surface that counts down to a next episode so two of them cannot drift into different units for the same number.
nodes.languageNotes: AniList sends seconds since the epoch while the arithmetic is in milliseconds; a null result means the episode already aired or nothing is scheduled.

nodes.name: formatLabelOf
nodes.summary: The one format-to-words mapping, shared by the title page's Details grid and a person profile's appearance row so the two cannot print TV_SHORT and TV Short side by side. Unrecognised values are passed through rather than relabelled, because an unfamiliar word is an honest signal and a confident wrong label is not.

nodes.name: StudioCredit
nodes.summary: One studio credit with the isMain flag that separates the animation studio from the publishers sharing the field; the id is nullable because a credit that came from a flat list has a name that cannot be tapped rather than one that opens the wrong studio.

nodes.name: studioCredits
nodes.summary: Reads the studio edges when AniList sent them and falls back to the flat node list, marking unranked credits as main so a title is never dimmed as studio-less on an older or thinner response, then sorts main first.

nodes.name: relatedMedia
nodes.summary: The relation row's membership and order: same-medium edges plus the cross-medium ADAPTATION/SOURCE pair, with CHARACTER edges kept only when a music video is involved, then ranked spine-adaptation-music-side material and dated oldest first so the twelve-card cap shows sequels instead of an arbitrary dozen spin-offs.

nodes.name: metaLabel
nodes.summary: The one-line fact strip under a related title - format, length, year, and status only when the status is news - built from the cleaned labels rather than raw enums and reading chapters or volumes for manga so a manga relation card stops losing its length.

nodes.name: descriptionBody
nodes.summary: Strips AniList's '(Source: …)' attribution, which the markdown renderer otherwise prints as the last paragraph of every synopsis and counts toward the Read more threshold; only a line that is nothing but the credit is removed, so prose that mentions a source survives.

nodes.name: synopsis
nodes.summary: The description as plain prose for card bodies and length measurement: HTML tags and leftover whitespace removed, delegating to descriptionBody first so the provenance line is not measured as part of the text.

nodes.name: detailFor
nodes.summary: Looks a fetched detail up by id but only accepts it when the media namespace matches, which stopped a manga relation sharing a numeric id with an open anime from painting the anime's synopsis and cast over it. A typeless summary is the one accepted exception, because discarding the answer is how profile pinned titles opened blank.

nodes.name: MediaNode
nodes.summary: The one media shape every query reuses, from a list entry to a full detail page, with withDetail merging a lazily fetched response over a thin summary without letting null fields erase what the list query already knew. Field types follow what the server sends, which is why season is a string after Moshi threw on WINTER and took out the only call that fetches a user's list.

nodes.name: MediaTitle
nodes.summary: The four title forms AniList returns, with displayTitle preferring English for list rows and bestTitleOrNull omitting the Unknown Title placeholder for surfaces that already know the media resolved.

nodes.name: MediaCoverImage
nodes.summary: The cover sizes plus AniList's dominant colour, which tints a placeholder so a view waiting on art is recognisably the right show; bestUrl prefers extraLarge because a 230px large is upscaled in the detail hero.

nodes.name: SimpleMediaListEntry
nodes.summary: The viewer's own list entry as embedded in a media node, carrying progress, score and the account's scoreFormat so the editor's slider can be built from one object instead of guessing its scale from the value.

nodes.name: UserStatistics
nodes.summary: The per-medium breakdown of a user's list, now carrying the format, release-year, genre and tag distributions because the deprecated stats.favoured* fields answer HTTP 500 for the whole document and the profile charts had nothing left to draw.

nodes.name: MediaEntryEdit
nodes.summary: One edit to a list entry as a type rather than a ten-argument call, because each null means something different to AniList - do not change it for status, clear it for a date - and that decision belongs in one place instead of at every call site.

nodes.name: Deleted
nodes.summary: The shared object both delete mutations answer with, modelled as an object with a boolean rather than a flattened boolean because Moshi rejected the real shape and a delete the server had already performed was reported to the caller as a failure.

nodes.name: MediaExternalLink
nodes.summary: One external link with the type discriminator that separates a streaming service from a wiki or a Facebook page, kept for every kind so a future social row does not need a second query.

nodes.name: CharacterProfile
nodes.summary: One character as their profile page, with age kept as a string because AniList writes values like '23 (Physical), 77 (Actual)' and an Int would either fail to parse or truncate the joke, and facts ordered the way a person is introduced rather than sorted.

nodes.name: StaffProfile
nodes.summary: One crew member or voice actor, shaped like CharacterProfile so both render through the same sheet, with staffMedia pinned to the media property by @Json after Moshi looked for a field named media and left every creator's Worked on row empty.

nodes.name: ProfileAppearances
nodes.summary: A person's media connection, kept as edges because the edge is where the role and the voice actors live, with titlesFor collapsing the one-edge-per-credit shape into a filmography so twelve edges stop producing four posters.

nodes.name: ProfileAppearance
nodes.summary: One title in a person's row, carrying the media type so a tap opens the right namespace's detail sheet and the staffRole copied off the edge, since the credit lives on the edge while the row draws nodes.

nodes.name: StaffCharacterMedia
nodes.summary: The characters a person voiced, flattened from every edge and de-duplicated, because a staff page that only listed productions could say where a voice appears but never who it was.

nodes.name: PersonProfileState
nodes.summary: The closed set of states the one person sheet can render - closed, loading, loaded, failed - kept apart per payload so the sheet reads facts and appearances without null-checking which kind of person it is showing.

nodes.name: toLoadedState
nodes.summary: Maps a character payload onto the sheet's loaded state, filtering aliases that repeat the name and reading the Japanese-then-English voice credits off the media edges.

nodes.name: toLoadedState
nodes.summary: Maps a staff payload onto the same loaded state, passing primary occupations into titlesFor so a title credited twice keeps the role the person is known for, and filling the Voiced row from the other connection.

nodes.name: ApiReachability
nodes.summary: The distinction the error screen draws the moment something fails - online, slow, rate limited, offline, down, not answering, unknown - because 'connection error' meant the internet, AniList, the token and a build bug all at once. UNKNOWN stays its own value since a probe that could not run has proved nothing.

nodes.name: ApiErrorCopy
nodes.summary: The error screen's voice for one failure kind: headline, explanation and a pool of quips, with quipFor choosing deterministically from a caller seed so recomposition cannot reshuffle the line but a retry can land on a different one.

nodes.name: ApiStatusSnapshot
nodes.summary: One probe result, with latency present only when the request actually completed, which is what lets the status strip say 'came back in 240 ms' instead of merely 'reachable'.

nodes.name: friendlyCopy
nodes.summary: Maps each failure kind to its headline, explanation and joke pool, naming the culprit Ani-chan so the screen has a subject to be fond of, and sharing one large pool across every 'it did not answer' kind because the reader only cares that nothing came back.

nodes.name: friendlyCopy
nodes.summary: Copy for a probe result, where there is no exception to classify; reachable results get their own pool so 'Ani-chan is awake' never appears among the lines used when everything is on fire.

nodes.name: toReachability
nodes.summary: The reachability a failure already proves before any probe runs: a rejected session or a 404 is AniList talking to us, so the strip can answer immediately instead of leaving a spinner up for a check that can only agree.

nodes.name: isWorthProbing
nodes.summary: Gates the diagnostic probe to the failures that leave reachability genuinely ambiguous, so a rate limit is not answered with another refused request and a definite answer is not restated.

nodes.name: encodeTiers
nodes.summary: Writes the tier rows as label|colour|id|floor, escaping the label because it is free text and a row renamed to 'S, best of' used to split into two unparseable chunks and shift the rest of the list around it.

nodes.name: decodeTiers
nodes.summary: Reads tiers in the three- or four-field shape and falls back to the standard six when nothing is readable, because a list with no rows has nowhere to drag anything while a template is one rename away from being the person's own.

nodes.name: decodeAssignment
nodes.summary: Reads the mediaId:tierId placements into an insertion-ordered map, which is also the list's order, and drops a dangling media id rather than guessing a tier nobody chose.

nodes.name: decodeDisplay
nodes.summary: Reads the drawing preferences field by field so a build that stored the zoom but not the title position still gets its zoom back, and treats a non-finite zoom as absent because it would make the board's layout maths produce NaN and draw nothing.

nodes.name: encodeTierListDocument
nodes.summary: Writes one saved list as five lines with the display line last, so a reader from before that line existed sees exactly the four lines it knew; the document id is deliberately absent because a value that is also a key can disagree with itself.

nodes.name: decodeTierListDocument
nodes.summary: Reads a document, returning null only when the key genuinely holds nothing; a blank name line keeps the placements and takes the base name, and a missing updatedAt reads as never-written so an old document sorts to the bottom instead of claiming it was just touched.

nodes.name: legacyTierListDocument
nodes.summary: Converts the pre-library install's two preference keys into one document, returning null when neither exists so a fresh install is not greeted with an empty list it never made; the decision lives here so the store's migration is two lines of plumbing.

nodes.name: TierListSvg
nodes.summary: The SVG writer for a computed tier layout, holding the escaping and number formatting that make an exported document well-formed in every locale and viewer.

nodes.name: Palette
nodes.summary: The colours an export draws with, injected rather than read from the Compose theme so this layer stays Android-free and a dark-phone export can still be a light document.

nodes.name: write
nodes.summary: Renders the layout as an SVG: rows the person has not deleted, tiles with embedded data-URI posters, captions read from the layout rather than re-derived, and XML escaping on every string because a title containing & or < otherwise produces a document a renderer shows as nothing.

nodes.name: ActivityReply
nodes.summary: One comment on an activity; the text stays raw AniList Markdown until it is expanded, and the author reuses FollowUser because it is the same id-name-avatar selection a followers row asks for.

nodes.name: ActivityDetail
nodes.summary: The activity a comment sheet opens, with like and reply counts plus the thread; an id that resolves to another union member reads as an empty thread rather than an error.

nodes.name: ToggleLikeResult
nodes.summary: The flat shape both toggleable LikeableUnion members share, so one type decodes either and the union typename is not requested because nothing branches on it.

nodes.name: DeleteActivityReplyData
nodes.summary: The reply deletion payload, reading the shared Deleted object; the removed reply is not echoed back so the sheet drops it by the id it sent.

nodes.name: ActivityLikeState
nodes.summary: The mapped like answer with the union wrapper and nullability stripped off, resolving AniList's null count to zero once here rather than at each of the two places that draw it.

nodes.name: AiringCountdown
nodes.summary: The shared countdown formatter, existing as one object so a missed-sequel card and an arriving row cannot end up printing 'in 3.5d' and 'in 3d' for the same episode.

nodes.name: format
nodes.summary: Formats the remaining time in the largest whole unit that still reads as a countdown, returning null once the episode has aired or nothing is scheduled so callers can skip the row instead of drawing 'now' forever.

nodes.name: ExpressiveControls.kt
nodes.summary: The Material 3 Expressive selection controls: tab bar, two segmented bars and a filter chip. Every animation is a spring from ExpressiveMotion read in the draw phase, and each control carries the semantics role a screen reader needs to say what is selected.
nodes.languageNotes: Animate scale with animateFloatAsState and apply it inside Modifier.graphicsLayer so a frame invalidates draw only; the tab bar suppresses the ripple and multiplies press and selection scale into one graphicsLayer.

nodes.name: SegmentedOption
nodes.summary: One segment of the polygon segmented bar: a label plus an optional vector icon. Exists so a caller can put a glyph next to a filter name without the bar having to accept two parallel lists.

nodes.name: ExpressiveTabBar
nodes.summary: The app's top-level tab strip, with a capsule that springs and recolours on selection. The ripple is deliberately suppressed because a bounded ripple spreading across a capsule that is simultaneously scaling and changing colour fights the spring, so the scale is the press feedback instead.

nodes.name: ExpressivePolygonSegmentedBar
nodes.summary: Segmented bar of icon-and-label options inside a pill container. Its labels are capped at two lines with no overflow on purpose: the earlier maxLines = 1 was TextOverflow.Clip, which cut a long option name through a letter on a control where picking the wrong segment edits the wrong setting.

nodes.name: ExpressiveSegmentedBar
nodes.summary: Text-only segmented control whose outer corners round more than its inner ones so the group reads as a single capsule. Corner radii animate rather than jump, which is what makes a selection feel like one control moving instead of two rectangles swapping colour.

nodes.name: ExpressiveStateChip
nodes.summary: Filter chip that morphs corners and padding on selection and reports its own checked state to accessibility. minTouchTargetHeight is opt-in because the chip is only about 30dp tall and widening every filter in the app would have resized the whole UI to fix the few call sites where it is a tab selector.

nodes.name: AniListMarkdownInlines.kt
nodes.summary: Turns the inline token tree into a styled AnnotatedString: emphasis, code, links, mentions, inline images and tappable inline spoilers. Links route through the app's own handler so they open in a Custom Tab, and nested markup renders as markup instead of printing its source.
nodes.languageNotes: The link callback is held in rememberUpdatedState because the AnnotatedString is itself remembered, so capturing the lambda would freeze the first composition's reference.

nodes.name: buildInlineAnnotatedString
nodes.summary: The single inline renderer used by paragraphs, table cells, headers and truncated bios. Its spoiler reveal is rememberSaveable per paragraph because the paragraph is disposed with its LazyColumn item, and a reader who opened a plot point has already chosen to read it.

nodes.name: InlineSpoilers
nodes.summary: Per-call cursor over a paragraph's inline spoilers, pairing each obscured run's reading-order index with the reveal set. The index has to be per call because one paragraph is rendered as several Texts, each with its own reveal set.

nodes.name: AniListMarkdownModel.kt
nodes.summary: The AST for AniList-flavoured Markdown plus the queries the renderer runs over it: which media covers a document references, and which links must be lifted out of a paragraph into cover cards. The inline tokens carry parsed children because a bold line whose text is a link is the normal shape of a bio.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Kotlin with no Compose imports, so the parsing and the cover-key extraction can be unit tested on the JVM.

nodes.name: MarkdownNode
nodes.summary: The block-level AST: headers, paragraphs, lists, code, tables, images, video, spoilers and AniList preview blocks. ImageBlock carries the raw size string because AniList writes img220(...) and the renderer, not the parser, decides the dp value.

nodes.name: InlineToken
nodes.summary: The inline token tree. Emphasis and link tokens carry children because modelling them as a flat string flattened an inner link into its own source text, which is the bug where a bio printed raw [Title](url) characters. MediaLink is separate from Link so the renderer can draw a cover card instead of an underlined title.

nodes.name: mediaCoverKeysIn
nodes.summary: Collects the media a document links to, in document order, so a cover lookup can be batched. It filters to anime and manga with a numeric positive id because a studio, character or user id lives in a different namespace, and asking Media(id:) for one returns an unrelated anime with a confidently wrong poster.

nodes.name: splitMediaLinks
nodes.summary: Separates a paragraph's text from the media links that become cards, descending into emphasis runs and link labels because the standard bio shape wraps the link in bold. An emphasis run left with no children is dropped rather than kept as an empty wrapper that would draw a blank line above the card.

nodes.name: mediaCoverKeyOrNull
nodes.summary: The single definition of "is this preview a media card", shared by the batch collector and the renderer so the two cannot disagree about which covers to fetch. Carries the type as well as the id, because an anime 1 and a manga 1 are different shows and collapsing them made both cards draw the same poster.

nodes.name: ShimmerLoading.kt
nodes.summary: The skeleton loading stack: one hoisted shimmer clock, a skeleton block and a card-shaped placeholder. The transition is hoisted because five cards each owning an infinite transition read their animated value during composition, which meant five full recompositions and five new gradient shaders per frame for the length of a network scan.
nodes.languageNotes: The phase is read inside Modifier.drawBehind, a draw-phase read, so a shimmer frame invalidates only the draw pass; theme colours are resolved outside the lambda because a DrawScope is not a composable scope.

nodes.name: rememberShimmerPhase
nodes.summary: The one shimmer clock a list shares, so the skeletons stay phase-locked and read as a single sweeping highlight instead of several unrelated ones. Callers hoist it where the list is built; the composable default keeps a lone card working with its own correctly scoped driver.

nodes.name: ShimmerBox
nodes.summary: One skeleton block, clipped to a shape and painted with the shared shimmer. Kept beside the shimmer background so there is one definition of what a skeleton looks like rather than one per screen.

nodes.name: ShimmerCard
nodes.summary: A card-shaped skeleton matching the poster row that replaces it, so the dashboard does not jump when real content lands. All of its boxes take the same hoisted phase so the sweep crosses the whole card as one.

nodes.name: UpdateDialogs.kt
nodes.summary: The launch-time update prompt and the download progress block. The dialog cannot be dismissed while a transfer is running because dismissing used to reset the state while the download kept going, so the prompt reappeared minutes later over whatever the user was doing.

nodes.name: UpdatePromptHost
nodes.summary: Draws the update dialog for exactly the states that have an action in them, and nothing at all for UpToDate or Failed, which the user already asked about on the Settings tab. Its confirm button changes meaning with the state so the label always names what the tap will do.

nodes.name: DownloadProgress
nodes.summary: Determinate progress bar with a percentage, byte count and transfer rate, falling back to indeterminate when GitHub's CDN sends no Content-Length. The rate is on screen because "downloading" alone is the one state a user cannot tell apart from a stalled transfer.

nodes.name: UpdateInstallation.kt
nodes.summary: The platform half of the updater: ask whether the app may install packages, where the grant lives, and fire the install intent. Deliberately holds no repository client, because an earlier version's unused UpdateManager default quietly built a second OkHttp client and thread pool per instance.
nodes.languageNotes: FileProvider.getUriForFile is wrapped in runCatching so a paths/file mismatch reports CouldNotOpen instead of crashing; the class is open so tests can substitute a fake.

nodes.name: InstallerLaunch
nodes.summary: Two outcomes for asking the installer to open, rather than a boolean. Collapsing the failure into one "no" is what turned a FileProvider misconfiguration into the app telling every user their phone could not install apps.

nodes.name: UpdateInstallation
nodes.summary: Holds the three platform questions the install flow must ask in order - may we install, where is the grant, which intents fire - in one place, because the sequencing is the logic. openInstaller tries ACTION_VIEW on the FileProvider URI and then ACTION_INSTALL_PACKAGE, which several OEM builds are the only handler for.

nodes.name: AniListMarkdownTable.kt
nodes.summary: Parses and draws Markdown tables from reviews, forum posts and bios. The table scrolls horizontally inside an outlined surface because a bio table has more columns than a phone has width, and wrapping cells would destroy the row alignment that makes it a table.

nodes.name: RenderTable
nodes.summary: Draws a parsed table block with a tinted header row and alternating row backgrounds. Cells are minimum 96dp wide and the whole table scrolls, so a long cell widens its column rather than squeezing the others.

nodes.name: tryParseTable
nodes.summary: Recognises a table at a line index by requiring a pipe in the header and a separator line made only of pipes, colons and dashes, then returns the parsed block and the index after it. The bounds check has a lower bound as well as an upper one because the index is a parameter and lines[-1] throws.

nodes.name: ExpressiveButtons.kt
nodes.summary: The primary action button with a contained loading morph and a spring press, plus a badged icon button. Both take their pressed state from the Material component's own interaction source so a drag that starts on the button does not spring it twice.

nodes.name: ExpressivePrimaryButton
nodes.summary: The app's high-emphasis action, which rounds into a true capsule while pressed or loading. PillCorner is half the 48dp height so the pressed shape is a capsule by measurement, and the same radius serves the loading state so a tap that becomes a request is one continuous change.

nodes.name: ExpressiveIconBadge
nodes.summary: Circular icon button with an optional count badge pinned to its top-end corner, used for the controls that also carry a status number. The badge is a pill background plus label text rather than a drawable so it themes with the rest of the surface.

nodes.name: EntryScore.kt
nodes.summary: Maps an account's AniList score format to the slider it needs: the top of the scale and the smallest step. Without the format the editor used to guess from the loaded value, so a POINT_100 account scored 8 got a 0-10 slider and a decimal account could not enter 8.5.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Kotlin, no Compose imports, so the scale arithmetic and quantisation are covered by JVM tests.

nodes.name: ScoreFormat
nodes.summary: The five score formats AniList accounts can have, each with its ceiling and step. fromApi is case-insensitive and returns null for an unknown format so a format AniList adds later degrades to the fallback guess instead of crashing the editor.

nodes.name: ScoreScale
nodes.summary: The ceiling and step a score slider is drawn with, derived once when the entry loads so a drag cannot change the scale mid-gesture. Above twenty steps the ticks are dropped and quantise does the snapping, because a hundred tick marks 3dp apart read as a dotted rule.

nodes.name: scoreScaleFor
nodes.summary: The scale to draw, falling back to the pre-format guess when the format is unknown - a save response carries no Viewer. The fallback step is halved to 0.5 so a value the form already prints is a value the form can set.

nodes.name: AniListMarkdownParagraph.kt
nodes.summary: Renders a paragraph as a Column of wrapped text runs with real images between them, because a Text can style a character but cannot draw a bitmap. A truncated paragraph falls back to one annotated Text since truncation and embedding are mutually exclusive.

nodes.name: RenderParagraph
nodes.summary: Chooses between one Text and a segmented flow: consecutive text tokens are grouped into a single Text per run so a line is not broken at every bold word, and each inline image reuses the block image renderer so there is one image treatment in the markdown stack.

nodes.name: CommentDraftEdits.kt
nodes.summary: The comment composer's format bar as pure string-and-selection edits. Extracted from the composable because every mistake here is an off-by-one - a cursor outside the markers, a reversed selection, an index past a truncation - and those are cases a JVM test pins in milliseconds.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Kotlin with no Android or Compose imports; the composable keeps only the mapping to TextFieldValue.

nodes.name: DraftEdit
nodes.summary: The text and selection after a format-bar action. Returning both together is the point: the edits all move the cursor as well as the text, and a caller that reconstructed the selection would reintroduce the off-by-ones this file exists to avoid.

nodes.name: wrapSelection
nodes.summary: Wraps a selection in markdown markers, or inserts the empty pair with the caret between them. A reversed selection is normalised rather than rejected because Android reports a right-to-left drag that way, and dropping it would make the button do nothing for half the gestures.

nodes.name: startReplyTo
nodes.summary: Prefixes a draft with @name, because AniList activity replies have no parent pointer and are threaded by the leading mention. The mention is added once and a blank author name leaves the draft untouched, since "@ " is a broken mention rather than a reply.

nodes.name: isAttachableImageUrl
nodes.summary: Accepts only absolute http(s) URLs with no spaces as an image attachment. The comment is shown to other people and the renderer only embeds absolute URLs, so anything else would be stored as literal text in the posted comment - worse than refusing the insert.

nodes.name: LoginDialogs.kt
nodes.summary: The two manual login dialogs: override the AniList OAuth client id, or paste a bearer token. Both exist because the app has no Play Services and no server, so an OAuth misconfiguration or a device without a browser has to be recoverable without reinstalling.

nodes.name: ClientIdDialog
nodes.summary: Lets the user replace the built-in AniList client id without a rebuild, which is the escape hatch when the shipped id is rate-limited or revoked. It saves only a non-blank value and shows the currently active id so the user can tell whether an override is in force.

nodes.name: ManualTokenDialog
nodes.summary: Accepts a bearer token copied from AniList by hand, the last-resort path when the browser round trip cannot complete. Multi-line input on purpose, since a pasted JWT is long and a single-line field hides most of it.

nodes.name: LibrarySelection.kt
nodes.summary: Resolves the Library tab's remembered view one level above the tab, in AppNavigation, because AnimatedContent disposes the tab it animates away from - so collecting the four preferences inside the tab re-asked DataStore on every visit and drew a spinner for a preference that had not changed.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines four DataStore flows into one emission so the four values move together and a half-restored selection cannot be drawn.

nodes.name: RememberedLibraryView
nodes.summary: The Library's remembered view: what the reader last chose plus the store its next choice is written to. answered = false is the only resolving state, which is what distinguishes "DataStore has not replied" from "this account never chose" - both used to emit null and the spinner never resolved.

nodes.name: rememberedSelectionFlow
nodes.summary: Combines the four stored preferences into one flow whose first emission always arrives, even when nothing is stored, so answered can tell "not answered yet" apart from "never chosen". Unknown stored enum names resolve to null so a preference written by another build shows the default rather than an empty list.

nodes.name: rememberLibrarySelection
nodes.summary: The composable entry point that subscribes once per process to the remembered selection and returns the resolving placeholder until the first emission. The flow is remembered on the store so a recomposition does not resubscribe to DataStore.

nodes.name: AppJokes.kt
nodes.summary: The pool of hobby jokes the random toast draws from, kept separate from the API failure pools because a line about backlogs during normal use must not read as a warning about AniList being down. Deliberately free of Android and Compose imports so the duplicate-free pool is pinned by a JVM test.
nodes.languageNotes: A plain Kotlin object with no Android imports; text is carried by words, not emoji, per the vectors-only rule.

nodes.name: AppJokes
nodes.summary: The joke pool and the two pickers over it. Keeping the strings in an object rather than in the toast composable is what lets the pool's size and uniqueness be asserted without a device.

nodes.name: pickDifferent
nodes.summary: Picks a line that is not the previous one, because the same joke twice in a row is what makes a random toast feel mechanical. The retry loop is bounded: a two-line pool cannot avoid a repeat forever and an unbounded search over a one-line pool would hang the caller.

nodes.name: AnimatedCounter.kt
nodes.summary: A number that rolls to its new value with spring physics and a vertical slide. The AnimatedContent is keyed on the settled count rather than the interpolated value, because keying on the animated value started a fresh enter+exit transition on every frame of the spring.

nodes.name: AnimatedCounterText
nodes.summary: The dashboard counter. Its text uses tabular figures because the digits interpolate every frame and proportional figures change the text width with them, re-measuring the counter and everything beside it on each frame of the roll.

nodes.name: InfoEditorial.kt
nodes.summary: The accent-bar section heading used by the redesigned title Info page, with an optional sub-line and trailing slot. It is a second heading composable rather than a parameter on SectionHeading because that one is an icon-and-label for a bleeding artwork row, and only the dressing differs.
nodes.languageNotes: The accent bar is a RoundedCornerShape(percent = 50) box, not a RoundedPolygon: a polygon stretched to 3dp wide is the ellipse AGENTS.md warns about.

nodes.name: InfoAccentHeading
nodes.summary: Draws a section title with a filled accent bar, an optional "2 openings · 2 endings" sub-line and an optional trailing control. The title carries the heading semantic so a screen reader can navigate the page by section.

nodes.name: OpenExternalUrl.kt
nodes.summary: The single way the app hands a URL to another app, with a clipboard fallback. It moved out of the settings package when the profile needed it too, because a second copy is how two implementations of "start an ACTION_VIEW and hope" end up disagreeing about FLAG_ACTIVITY_NEW_TASK.

nodes.name: openExternalUrl
nodes.summary: Fires an ACTION_VIEW intent and reports whether anything took it. Returning the outcome is what made the failure visible: the previous Unit-returning version discarded an ActivityNotFoundException at all eighteen call sites, so tapping a link in a bio did nothing at all.

nodes.name: openExternalUrlOrCopy
nodes.summary: Opens the URL, and when nothing can open it puts it on the clipboard and says so. A dead protocol link in somebody's bio still leaves the reader with the address, which is strictly more useful than a tap that does nothing and costs one clipboard write.

nodes.name: ExpressiveIndicators.kt
nodes.summary: The Material 3 Expressive loading and progress indicators: the morphing loader, its contained variant for buttons, and a thin wavy progress track for sequel rows. Thin wrappers exist so the experimental API opt-in and the test tags live in one place.
nodes.languageNotes: Opts into ExperimentalMaterial3ExpressiveApi per function rather than file-wide, so the opt-in does not leak to callers.

nodes.name: ExpressiveLoadingIndicator
nodes.summary: The indeterminate morphing loader, wrapped so the experimental opt-in and the test tag are not repeated at every call site.

nodes.name: ExpressiveContainedLoadingIndicator
nodes.summary: The contained loader used inside a button, where the morph needs a container backdrop to read as a busy state rather than a floating shape. ExpressivePrimaryButton substitutes it for the label while loading.

nodes.name: WavyProgressBar
nodes.summary: A thin determinate wavy track for a card's episode progress, distinct from the hand-drawn WavyProgressBar on the Info page where the wave's height is the progress. The duplicate name is deliberate and documented, because a card bar and a page bar are different controls.

nodes.name: TransferRate.kt
nodes.summary: A smoothed bytes-per-second reading over the last two seconds, rather than total bytes over total time. A whole-transfer average reads as slow on a connection that stalled for a minute and opens at an impossible rate on a resumed download, because the first callback already carries the previous attempt's bytes.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure arithmetic with the clock passed in as a parameter and no Android types, so it can be tested against readings a real network never produces on demand.

nodes.name: TransferRate
nodes.summary: Keeps a bounded window of byte-count readings and answers the rate across them, always retaining at least two samples so the first seconds of a download still show a number. A byte count lower than the last is treated as a restart and clears the history instead of averaging backwards.

nodes.name: InfoAiring.kt
nodes.summary: A minute-ticking countdown to the next episode that stops with the screen. The Info page used to call airingCountdown() once in composition, so a sheet left open across the airing boundary went on saying "airs in 5m" after the episode had aired.

nodes.name: rememberAiringCountdown
nodes.summary: A produceState clock that recomputes the countdown once a minute while the Activity is resumed and returns null when there is nothing to count down to. Gating on resume costs nothing because the producer recomputes from the current time rather than catching up through missed ticks.

nodes.name: StudioRoutes.kt
nodes.summary: The studio page's route, its two arguments and the builder every caller uses. The name travels beside the id so the top bar can read "Shaft" on the first frame, and studio() always writes the ?name= query because a composable() route matches exactly and a bare studio/12 would silently navigate nowhere.
nodes.languageNotes: The name is Uri.encode'd and defaulted to an empty string so a missing name is a valid route rather than an unmatched one.

nodes.name: StudioRoutes
nodes.summary: Route pattern, argument names and the builder for the studio destination. The route is deliberately not in the auth watcher's evacuation list because a studio is public AniList data, so a 401 should not throw a reader off a filmography they are reading.

nodes.name: ResumedState.kt
nodes.summary: One helper answering whether the Activity is resumed, used to gate the app's animation clocks. Two components had grown their own copy of the flag and the copies had already drifted - one was keyed on an argument so it restarted on navigation, the other had no gate at all and animated behind a stopped Activity.

nodes.name: rememberIsResumed
nodes.summary: Reports whether the screen is on screen right now, returning false for the first frame because nothing has confirmed it yet. Keyed on Unit on purpose: the answer is a property of the process, so a caller-specific key would only make the flag flicker for no reason.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Placement rules for shared presentation: what belongs at the components root versus detail, cards, expressive, icons, markdown and update, plus the rules that a component holds no screen logic, that one control has one declaration, and that springs come from ExpressiveMotion.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Placement rules for destinations: one directory per screen holding everything only that screen draws, the "would this file move if the destination moved" test, and the three traps - a screen holding a NavController, a tab drawing its own ModalBottomSheet, and state that must be hoisted across a tab switch.

nodes.name: NavigationActions.kt
nodes.summary: The one navigation helper every screen-to-screen hop uses, so a repeated tap cannot push the same destination onto the back stack again. Without launchSingleTop, three taps on a profile face left three copies of the same screen, three sets of ViewModels and three identical scroll positions.
nodes.languageNotes: An extension on NavHostController; destinations that need a different stack shape pass their own popUpTo and do not use this.

nodes.name: navigateSingle
nodes.summary: Navigates with launchSingleTop so a destination already on top is a no-op instead of another push. A double tap that arrives while the first transition is running is the same bug one frame later, so callers must not route around this with a raw navigate.

nodes.name: TierListImageExporter.kt
nodes.summary: Third renderer for the tier board: draws the whole visible assignment into one PNG from the same layoutTierList geometry the screen and the SVG writer use, because a screenshot of a scrolling column can only ever capture the viewport and the current zoom. Output scale is capped by pixel count, not title count, so a 300-title board exports slightly soft instead of failing with an OOM.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses android.graphics Canvas/Paint directly (no Compose), Coil for poster fetching in batches of eight, and a FileProvider cache directory contract shared with res/xml/update_file_paths.xml.

nodes.name: renderTierListImage
nodes.summary: Lays out and paints the board into a bitmap at a 1080-unit width, dropping placements whose title is no longer in the library so an export never draws a blank tile or promises a title count it does not contain.

nodes.name: shareTierListImage
nodes.summary: Writes the PNG into the cache's exports/ directory and hands its URI to a chooser. The cache rather than files, and exports/ specifically, because that is the only directory the app's FileProvider publishes - a file written elsewhere would throw from getUriForFile at the last step.

nodes.name: saveTierListImage
nodes.summary: Writes the PNG to Pictures/AniSequel through MediaStore with the IS_PENDING flag, deleting the row if the encode fails so a half-written image never appears in the gallery.

nodes.name: TierBoardLogic.kt
nodes.summary: Every board decision that is not "draw a thing": colour unpacking, zoom clamping, drop targeting, caret placement, drag auto-scroll strength and the viewport state holder. Extracted from a 1,500-line tier screen so the drag maths and the geometry can be tested by TierScreenLogicTest without a device, and each function records the shipped bug it prevents.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure Kotlin plus Compose snapshot state; no Android framework types, so the whole file runs on the JVM.

nodes.name: tierRowColor
nodes.summary: Converts the domain's packed 0xAARRGGBB long into a Compose Color by masking and shifting explicitly, because Color(Int) silently produces a transparent colour for the same bits and Color(Long) had to be relied on to survive a negative value read back from DataStore.

nodes.name: clampTierZoom
nodes.summary: Constrains a pinch to the renderable zoom range and maps NaN to the floor, because coerceIn passes NaN straight through and every offset downstream of a NaN scale produces a layout that never draws.

nodes.name: TierDrop
nodes.summary: The answer to where a release lands: a tier and a position inside it. Two fields rather than one because "put it in S" used to file a tile wherever its media id happened to sit; a null tierId is the instruction to take the title out of the list, not an error.

nodes.name: tierDropPlacement
nodes.summary: Resolves a release into a tier plus the tile it lands above, choosing the anchor within the line the finger is on so a two-line row can be dropped into its middle. The dragged tile is excluded from the anchors or a stationary finger would reorder the row under itself.

nodes.name: tierDropCaret
nodes.summary: Computes where the "it lands here" caret is drawn, or null when the drop clears the list. Excludes the dragged tile for the same reason the placement does - the two once disagreed mid-drag, so dragging the last poster of a row to the end of that row made the indicator vanish.

nodes.name: visibleTierItems
nodes.summary: Filters the lifted tile out of the drawn children. A named function because both the content lambda and the slot list must apply the identical rule: when the skip lived in only one of them the first long-press threw "TierGeometry emitted N children for N+1 slots" and killed the screen.

nodes.name: tierDragScrollStrength
nodes.summary: Returns a signed 0..1 scroll strength for a drag held near a viewport edge, deliberately a strength rather than a distance so a 120Hz device does not scroll twice as fast as a 60Hz one.

nodes.name: TierBoardViewport
nodes.summary: Mutable holder for the window-space viewport, board origin and per-row bands, published by the board and read once per frame by the drag coroutine. The rows are published rather than recomputed by the tray so only one component holds an opinion about the shared geometry.

nodes.name: Theme.kt
nodes.summary: The app's single theme entry point: resolves Light/Dark/System, wallpaper dynamic colour, a chosen static palette, custom accent, anime-derived layer, true black and custom background into one animated ColorScheme, then hands it to MaterialExpressiveTheme with the selected motion scheme.
nodes.languageNotes: Static schemes are built from Color.kt tokens; generated ones come from DynamicThemeBuilder and are remembered per parsed colour so a recomposition of the whole app does not re-derive the HCT transforms.

nodes.name: AniSequelTheme
nodes.summary: Composable theme wrapper taking a ThemeMode rather than a boolean so "follow system" is expressible, applying true-black and custom-background overrides before animating every colour role and installing the motion scheme. The motion style is written from a SideEffect so a discarded composition cannot leave a theme that never reached the screen.

nodes.name: StatusColors
nodes.summary: Airing/Upcoming/Missed colours Material 3 has no role for, with separate light and dark sets. They exist because the previous hardcoded green on a translucent chip measured about 2.6:1 in light mode.

nodes.name: AniSequelTheme
nodes.summary: The object half of the theme, exposing statusColors through a static CompositionLocal. The light set is named once and used as the local's default, because the old `else LocalStatusColors.current` read the local it was providing and only worked by accident.

nodes.name: TierBoardExportSheet.kt
nodes.summary: The "Export tier list" sheet: reports how many titles the image will actually contain, then runs share or save as one pipeline with two last steps. Failures (404 poster, oversized bitmap, no app accepting image/png) are rendered in place so an export never closes the app on a bad connection.
nodes.languageNotes: State lives in a plain remembered class rather than in the composable, so a recomposition mid-export cannot lose the busy flag or report the wrong action's failure.

nodes.name: TierExportSheet
nodes.summary: The sheet composable, kept to layout only. It takes the unfiltered ranked count as well as the visible assignment so it can tell "nothing ranked" from "filters hid everything" - the two empty states have different fixes and used to share one wrong sentence.

nodes.name: TierExportSession
nodes.summary: Holds the sheet's busy/error state and the single start path that renders, delivers and clears busy on every exit - including the null-bitmap and refused-intent paths that the two hand-written button lambdas used to forget.

nodes.name: TierExportOutcome
nodes.summary: The five terminal outcomes of an export with their user-facing messages, attached to the action rather than the caller so Share and Save cannot report each other's failure text.

nodes.name: TierBoardFilterSheet.kt
nodes.summary: The board's filter sheet: list status, airing status, genres and an opt-in studio section. Chips are lit when the status is *shown* because that is the reading people arrive with, and the sentence above them states the polarity outright since a control that has to be inferred gets used backwards.
nodes.languageNotes: Facet options are derived from the candidate list with remember(candidates), so a filter change alone never rebuilds the chip sets.

nodes.name: TierFilterSheet
nodes.summary: The sheet itself, height-bounded and vertically scrollable so a 300-title list's genre and studio chips cannot make the sheet taller than the screen and turn its bottom into a dead strip that swallows the dismiss gesture.

nodes.name: TierFacetChips
