nodes.summary: A FlowRow of genre or studio chips carrying each option's title count, which doubles as the answer to "which studio have I watched most" and as the section's sort key. Renders the empty text instead when the list returned no facets.

nodes.name: TierFilterGroup
nodes.summary: The fixed status-chip group, laid out as explicit two-column chunks rather than a flow row so two lists of different lengths still read as the same control.

nodes.name: ThemePalettes.kt
nodes.summary: The static accent palettes a reader can choose instead of the brand blue, each a matched light/dark role pair so a non-designer cannot land on a primary that cannot hold text. The six generated palettes are lazy because constructing one runs the HCT solver twice and nothing at startup needs the full list.
nodes.languageNotes: fromStorage is a when rather than a lookup into entries, so reading the one chosen palette at startup does not build the five that were not chosen.

nodes.name: ThemePalette
nodes.summary: One selectable accent family: a storage id, a display name and a matched light/dark ColorScheme pair, plus the companion holding the brand, hand-built and generated palettes and the id lookup used on startup.

nodes.name: ThemePalettePreview
nodes.summary: The three-colour dot trio the palette picker draws, taken from each palette's dark variant so the preview reads as the app's own chip rather than as a light-mode swatch.

nodes.name: WidgetCover.kt
nodes.summary: Hand-rolled cover-art loader for the RemoteViews widgets: a RemoteViews tile needs a plain Bitmap, Coil only reaches widgets through Glance, and Glance would replace the AppWidgetProvider widgets the app already ships. Every failure returns null so a widget update can never take the process down from its own thread.
nodes.languageNotes: Own OkHttp client without the AniList auth interceptor (public CDN art must not carry the bearer token), a single MIN_PRIORITY thread, and two LruCaches bounded by decoded byte count.

nodes.name: WidgetCover
nodes.summary: The loader object: cached-first async cover fetch, a never-null rounded placeholder, and a two-pass sampled decode that keeps a poster inside the RemoteViews Binder budget and guarantees a software bitmap.

nodes.name: TierBoardSheets.kt
nodes.summary: The board's display, colour and rating-band dialogs. Filters, zoom and export live in their own files because they are three different sheets with three different reasons to change, and keeping them here had grown the file past what a reviewer can hold in one pass.
nodes.languageNotes: Takes the board's live zoom rather than the stored one, because the stored value lags a pinch by the write debounce.

nodes.name: TierDisplaySheet
nodes.summary: Titles under the cover, on it, or off, plus a zoom readout and reset. The zoom is repeated here because the board's stepper floats over the posters and can be mistaken for part of a tier, so this is where someone who pinched to 180% goes looking.

nodes.name: TierColorDialog
nodes.summary: The tier colour picker, offering a fixed palette rather than an HSV wheel because the row label is white text on the fill and a colour that looks good in a wheel can still be unreadable at 14sp.

nodes.name: TierScoreFloorDialog
nodes.summary: Edits a tier's rating band as a 0-100 score floor on a 5-point grid, kept beside the row it describes so moving or renaming a tier cannot leave its band behind. Defaults to 75 when switched on so the slider starts somewhere meaningful.

nodes.name: SettingsComponents.kt
nodes.summary: The shared Settings vocabulary: section cards, field labels, whole-row switches, info rows and the centred scrolling column. Extracted so the tabs agree on one card shape and one heading level instead of each re-deriving its own bold 16sp header.
nodes.languageNotes: Section titles carry the semantics heading role and nothing else does, so a screen-reader user has one stable landmark per card.

nodes.name: SectionCard
nodes.summary: One titled block of Settings: an icon tile plus a title and optional subtitle. The tile uses secondaryContainer by default because under Material You the primary role follows the wallpaper and a saturated tile reads as a sticker.

nodes.name: SwitchRow
nodes.summary: A switch whose whole row is the touch target, because a settings row whose label does nothing when tapped is the most common way a screen like this feels broken.

nodes.name: InfoRow
nodes.summary: A label/value pair with the value right-aligned and allowed to wrap, used by the Info tab's version and build rows.

nodes.name: SettingsScrollColumn
nodes.summary: The scrolling column every Settings tab sits in, capped at MaxSettingsContentWidth so the cards do not stretch to a tablet's full width and become unreadable lines.

nodes.name: TierBoardSheetHost.kt
nodes.summary: The single switch that decides which board sheet or dialog is open, plus the saved state, the data every sheet reads and the callbacks they can invoke. Extracted because seven rememberSaveable flags and eight dismiss lambdas had turned the screen's composition root into a branch ladder.
nodes.languageNotes: The whole sheet state is saved as one mapSaver so a rotation keeps an open sheet open.

nodes.name: TierBoardSheetState
nodes.summary: The set of nullable/boolean fields describing which modal is open, in one object so the board can open a sheet from the app bar, the header or a poster tap by setting a single field.

nodes.name: rememberTierBoardSheetState
nodes.summary: Remembers the sheet state through the mapSaver so an open sheet survives rotation, with missing keys restored to their closed defaults.

nodes.name: TierBoardSheetData
nodes.summary: Everything the sheets read, bundled so the host takes three arguments instead of a dozen. Carries both the full and the filtered assignment, and the live zoom beside the stored display value.

nodes.name: TierBoardSheetActions
nodes.summary: The callback set a sheet can invoke on the board, travelling with the host because the open sheet changes on every tap and the set would otherwise be twenty parameters.

nodes.name: TierBoardSheetsHost
nodes.summary: Renders at most one board sheet or dialog from the state, and hands the display sheet the live zoom rather than the debounced stored one so toggling a title cannot write a stale zoom back over a fresh pinch.

nodes.name: ListFreshnessWatch.kt
nodes.summary: Decides when the list already on screen is due another trip to AniList: re-check on every return to the foreground and sleep the chosen interval while the app stays open. Nothing observed the app resuming before, so reopening AniSequel served the same collection for a flat hour.
nodes.languageNotes: The clock is injectable so the interval boundary is testable; the loop re-checks lastLoadedAtMillis rather than the wall clock, because the sleep is what carries the schedule.

nodes.name: ListFreshnessWatch
nodes.summary: The watch itself: a restartable foreground check, a timer loop with a five-minute retry floor so one failed fetch cannot become a tight retry loop against a rate-limited API, and two separate cooldowns for gestures and automatic triggers.

nodes.name: ApiStatusProbe.kt
nodes.summary: The status strip's state and the reachability probe behind it. A classified failure seeds the verdict immediately so only genuinely ambiguous errors cost a test request, and a probe of an old failure is cancelled when a newer one arrives so the strip cannot announce a stale verdict.
nodes.languageNotes: Exposed as a StateFlow of an immutable UI value; the pending-tap flag turns a manual Check during an in-flight probe into one queued request instead of a dropped one.

nodes.name: ApiStatusUi
nodes.summary: What the strip draws: reachability, latency, whether a check is running, why the last check produced no verdict, and a monotonic failure count. The count exists because two failures in a row usually carry the same message, so an effect keyed on the string would skip the retry.

nodes.name: ApiStatusProbeState
nodes.summary: Owns one screen's probe: seeds from the error kind, runs at most one request at a time, and turns an exception that escaped the repository into UNKNOWN plus a message rather than leaving isChecking true forever.

nodes.name: rememberApiStatusProbe
nodes.summary: Creates one probe per screen scope, reading the request lambda through rememberUpdatedState so a method reference that is reallocated each recomposition cannot rebuild the state and cancel the check the reader is watching.

nodes.name: TierBoardZoomSheet.kt
nodes.summary: The discoverable version of board zoom: one slider across the full range, five presets, and the drag lock beside the pinch that needs it. The stepper is precise but slow to cross 35-200% and a pinch needs two fingers on a poster the drag gesture used to win.
nodes.languageNotes: Height-bounded and scrollable because a landscape phone is shorter than the sheet, and writes the board's local zoom so the slider moves the board live.

nodes.name: TierZoomSheet
nodes.summary: The zoom sheet composable: percentage readout, slider bound to the shared TIER_MIN_ZOOM..TIER_MAX_ZOOM range, presets selected by a small epsilon, the drag lock switch and a reset to 100%.

nodes.name: libs.versions.toml
nodes.summary: The version catalog, and the project's only record of why each pin exists. material3 is held above the Compose BOM at 1.5.0-alpha14 because the Expressive component set is alpha-only and alpha15+ pulls a Compose line that requires compileSdk 37, while AGP stays on 9.4.1 because 9.5.0 has no stable release and a wrong pin stops every task at configuration time.
nodes.languageNotes: Also documents that coil-gif is load-bearing (ImageDecoderDecoder lives there) and that graphics-shapes is a direct dependency so MaterialShapes types in our own signatures resolve.

nodes.name: WidgetUpdater.kt
nodes.summary: The update path all four widget providers share: paint the placeholder synchronously, fetch the cover off the main thread, repaint, and always finish the pending result. An object rather than a base class because WidgetDeclarationTest reads each provider's source and requires the literal `: AppWidgetProvider()`.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps both the render and the callback in catch(Throwable) because an exception escaping the cover thread would take the whole process down.

nodes.name: WidgetUpdater
nodes.summary: The shared widget update helper: updateWidgets paints with no cover, refreshCover keeps a goAsync() result alive across the fetch, and updateAll does both for an app-triggered refresh.

nodes.name: ProfileStatsSections.kt
nodes.summary: The Stats tab's three-way split (Overview, Genres, Tags) and its section selector. The tab used to stack ten cards, so the genre chart - the most interesting thing on it - sat three phone screens below the fold with nothing saying it was there.
nodes.languageNotes: The selected section is held by the screen, not by the tab, because the profile disposes the tab it switches away from.

nodes.name: StatsSection
nodes.summary: The three groups the Stats tab is read in, each carrying its label; the long-tail genre and tag charts get a screen each where their length is the point rather than something to scroll past.

nodes.name: StatsSectionRow
nodes.summary: The section selector as a scrolling chip row, because the three labels plus their counts need about 330dp of a 360dp phone once the font size is turned up and an overflowing chip would be unreachable. The counts let a reader see whether a section is worth opening.

nodes.name: WidgetImageBudget.kt
nodes.summary: Derives the per-image decode ceiling from the display and divides it by the number of covers an update will decode, so several stacked widget instances cannot each decode a full poster on a low-memory device. Pure Kotlin so the degenerate cases (zero images, zero-sized display) are testable on the JVM.
nodes.languageNotes: Returns a pixel count, never zero and never more than MAX_EDGE_PX squared, because a zero handed to a sample-size calculation would ask for an infinitely down-sampled bitmap.

nodes.name: WidgetImageBudget
nodes.summary: The budget object: maxPixels turns a display size and an image count into a bounded pixel allowance, and targetSize turns that allowance back into a width/height pair at the AniList cover aspect without asking the network for dimensions.

nodes.name: ProfileFormatters.kt
nodes.summary: Shared date, relative-time, watch-time and score formatters for the Profile screens. Every format is pinned to Locale.ROOT so a device that writes decimals with a comma does not render "8,2/10", which is not a score.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses java.time on minSdk 31 (no desugaring needed) with an injectable `now` so the relative-time boundaries are testable.

nodes.name: formatJoinYear
nodes.summary: The four-digit year an account was created, for the join chip. Accounts AniList does not backfill have no field at all, so the caller hides the chip rather than printing "Joined unknown".

nodes.name: formatRelativeSeconds
nodes.summary: A Unix timestamp as "5h ago", collapsing to minutes, hours, days or years, and treating a future timestamp as "just now" so clock skew cannot produce a negative age.

nodes.name: formatWatchTime
nodes.summary: Minutes watched as the largest two units that still say something: minutes under an hour, hours under a day, then days plus remaining hours.

nodes.name: formatMeanScore
nodes.summary: AniList's mean score out of 100 as the out-of-ten number people quote, one decimal only when the mean is not whole, because 82.3 and 82 describe different lists.

nodes.name: Color.kt
nodes.summary: The raw colour tokens: the AniList brand blue seed, hand-picked semantic status colours for light and dark (the old hardcoded 0xFF10B981 did not clear 4.5:1 on a light surface), the navy surface ladder and the light neutrals.
nodes.languageNotes: DarkSurfaceDim and DarkSurfaceBright are pinned because Material's defaults are derived from a purple-grey seed and read as a different palette wherever an Expressive component used them.

nodes.name: Type.kt
nodes.summary: The app's only type scale: all fifteen Material 3 styles set explicitly, so screens that reach for titleMedium or labelSmall get this app's sizes instead of the platform's. The previous file overrode only bodyLarge, which produced a dozen call-site font sizes nothing could change in one place.
nodes.languageNotes: One private style() helper copies weight, size, line height and tracking onto each base style, with a shared LineHeightStyle.

nodes.name: ExpressiveTheme.kt
nodes.summary: The app's single Shapes scale (10 / 14 / 20 / 28 / 36dp), built from the ExpressiveShapes corner tokens. A second Shapes used to live in Type.kt with different values, so "the app's roundness" depended on which file a surface happened to import.
nodes.languageNotes: The token object is aliased as Corner because this file's own ExpressiveShapes shadows the identically named token object.

nodes.name: RepositoryResults.kt
nodes.summary: Turns an exception thrown on the way to a repository Result back into that Result. A store that only handled the Result half let the thrown half escape into a viewModelScope launch, where a supervisor job hands it to the thread handler and Android closes the app - the reported force-stop when a comment thread or title page opened.
nodes.languageNotes: CancellationException is rethrown because it is the scope being torn down, not a failure.

nodes.name: repositoryResult
nodes.summary: Runs a repository call and converts any non-cancellation exception into Result.failure, so the screen's existing "couldn't load" state is reachable instead of the process dying.

nodes.name: ic_launcher.xml
nodes.summary: The adaptive launcher icon: background, foreground and a separate monochrome layer. The monochrome layer is its own silhouette rather than the foreground because the system tints that layer with one wallpaper colour, and reusing the three-colour foreground flattened the icon into a solid blob.

nodes.name: build.gradle.kts
nodes.summary: The root Gradle build: declares the Android application, Compose compiler and KSP plugins from the version catalog with `apply false`, so each module opts in and the root build resolves nothing on its own.
nodes.languageNotes: Every plugin is referenced through the libs catalog aliases rather than pinned inline, which is what keeps gradle/libs.versions.toml the single source of versions.

nodes.name: ic_launcher_round.xml
nodes.summary: The round-variant adaptive icon, declaring the same background, foreground and monochrome layers as ic_launcher.xml; on API 26+ the system masks a single adaptive icon, so this file exists for launchers that still request the legacy round resource.

nodes.name: gradlew
nodes.summary: Gradle's generated POSIX shell launcher: resolves its own location through daisy-chained symlinks, picks a JVM from JAVA_HOME or PATH, raises the file-descriptor limit, and execs java -jar gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar with the caller's arguments. It is the entry point CI and the documented `./gradlew test` gate use, so it is left byte-identical to the upstream template rather than hand-edited.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately avoids bash arrays and other extensions because it targets any POSIX shell; argument handling packs DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS through xargs plus sed backslash-escaping so quoted options survive the eval. Cygwin/MSYS paths are rewritten with cygpath.

nodes.name: gradle-wrapper.jar
nodes.summary: The committed Gradle wrapper bootstrap JAR (46 KB binary, not source). gradlew runs it, and it reads gradle-wrapper.properties to download and cache the pinned Gradle 9.6.1 distribution, then starts the build with it. Committed on purpose so a clean checkout needs no pre-installed Gradle.
nodes.languageNotes: Binary class archive; not read. Its behaviour is fixed by the sibling gradle-wrapper.properties and by the wrapper version that generated it.

nodes.name: settings.gradle.kts
nodes.summary: Declares the AniSequel build: the single `:app` module, the repositories used for plugins and dependencies, and the foojay toolchain resolver that lets Gradle provision the JDK the Kotlin/AGP toolchain asks for. `RepositoriesMode.FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS` keeps every repository declaration in this one file, so a module cannot silently add a repository that would break reproducible builds.
nodes.languageNotes: Kotlin DSL settings script. pluginManagement narrows the google() repository by group regex so only Android, Google and AndroidX artifacts are fetched from it; dependencyResolutionManagement pins repository mode for all projects.

nodes.name: gradle-wrapper.properties
nodes.summary: Pins the Gradle distribution the wrapper downloads (gradle-9.6.1-bin.zip) and where it is cached (GRADLE_USER_HOME/wrapper/dists). This is the single place the Gradle version is decided, so a local run and CI resolve the same distribution; `validateDistributionUrl=true` rejects a malformed or non-HTTPS distributionUrl instead of failing later in the download.
nodes.languageNotes: Java properties file; the `https\://` colon is escaped because ':' is a properties key/value separator. networkTimeout is 10 s.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what AniSequel does - walking the AniList relation graph backwards from your completed list - then read the architecture specification for the layer model, the data flow and the non-negotiable invariants (no backend, freshness over offline caching, spring-only motion).

tour.title: Application Entry Point & App Shell
tour.description: AniSequelApplication owns process-wide singletons; MainActivity sets up edge-to-edge Compose and hosts AppNavigation, which defines every route and the spring transition between them. This is where the three-page capsule bar and the profile tabs are wired.

tour.title: The Domain Heart: Relation-Graph Traversal
tour.description: FindMissedSequelsUseCase is the reason the app exists. discover() walks every completed entry's relation edges in O(V+E) and applyFilters() re-filters only the resulting candidates in O(N), so a keystroke never re-walks an account. It has no Android imports.

tour.title: Network Layer & GraphQL
tour.description: AniList is spoken to exclusively through GraphQL. AniListApiService declares the Retrofit calls, GraphQLQueries holds the document constants, AuthInterceptor attaches the bearer token, RateLimitInterceptor honours 429 Retry-After, and RequestCoalescer collapses identical concurrent reads into one request (mutations are never coalesced).

tour.title: Repository, Caching & Disk Snapshots
tour.description: AniListRepositoryImpl is the single implementation behind every read and write: it chunk-merges paginated lists, keeps bounded TTL caches for lists/details/covers/profile, and classifies failures. SnapshotStore persists what a process death would otherwise throw away, always returning the timestamp a value was written with so reading never renews it.

tour.title: Authentication: OAuth2 PKCE or Public Scan
tour.description: Sign-in never touches an AniSequel server. AniListOAuth builds the PKCE challenge and parses the anisequel://oauth/callback redirect, AuthRepositoryImpl stores the tokens in DataStore, and LoginScreen offers the same screen for OAuth, scanning a public username, and demo mode.

tour.title: Dashboard: State Pipeline & Screen
tour.description: DashboardViewModel loads the viewer and list, memoises the relation walk behind a filter key and debounces recomputes; DashboardScreen renders the arriving and missed-sequel sections and hosts the filter sheet. The title sheet SequelDetailSheet answers everything about a media in one place.

tour.title: Profile, Library & Studio Pages
tour.description: UserOverviewViewModel publishes the profile overview first and merges the media list when it arrives, which is what isLibraryLoading exists for. UserProfileScreen hosts the Home, Activity, Stats and Social tabs built from the same destination list.

tour.title: Tier List: Documents, Geometry & Board
tour.description: Tier lists are a library of documents, not one blob: TierListViewModel edits through a single mutate path with a bounded undo stack, TierListLayout computes the arrangement, and TierBoard draws exactly those boxes so the screen and the exported PNG cannot disagree.

tour.title: Material 3 Expressive Design System
tour.description: ExpressiveMotion.kt names every spring in the app and switches its physics on the user's MotionStyle; AppVectorIcons.kt is the vectors-only icon registry that makes the no-emoji rule enforceable. Animate through these tokens, in the draw phase.

tour.title: The Self-Updater
tour.description: No Play Store, so the app updates itself. UpdateManager fetches update.json, ApkDownloader resumes a .part transfer, and the file is only renamed to .apk after zip-magic, package-name and pinned-certificate checks pass; UpdateController drives the UI and the onResume install handoff. update_file_paths.xml is the other half of the FileProvider contract.

tour.title: Build, Versioning & Signed Release
tour.description: Version lives in three files that must agree (gradle.properties, app/build.gradle.kts, update.json) and VersionBaselineTest enforces it. The version catalog records why pins exist - material3 alpha14, compileSdk 36.1, minSdk 31. The single workflow runs the JVM tests as the gate, signs with repository secrets and only publishes on non-PR runs.

tour.title: Contributor Rules & Decision Log
tour.description: AGENTS.md is the constraint list - no pushes to main, spring-only motion, vectors-only icons, keystore rules, changelog-and-version coupling. NOTES.md records why the code is shaped this way, and BUILDING.md is the release runbook.
